rationale.rationale: Management's stated reason is that UPL is a conglomerate whose crop protection business is trapped inside a diversified holding structure and is therefore mis-valued: Bikash Prasad said on the May 2026 Capital Markets Day that "even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple" and that UPL carries "a huge conglomerate discount," so separation would make "the sum of the parts... much, much clearer." The Scheme (board-approved 20 Feb 2026) is a three-step composite arrangement: amalgamate UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL SAS, India crop protection, 90.91% owned, FY25 turnover INR 24,120 Mn or 31.15% of UPL's turnover) into UPL Limited; demerge that India crop protection undertaking into UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions (UPL 2) on a 1:1 share entitlement; then amalgamate UPL Crop Protection Holdings Ltd., Cayman (UPL Cayman, the 77.78%-held international crop protection vehicle, FY25 turnover USD 4,187 Mn, net worth USD 1,599 Mn) into UPL 2 at 1,000 UPL 2 shares for every 213 UPL Cayman shares, with UPL SAS holders getting 1,000 UPL shares per 48 UPL SAS shares. The problems it is said to solve: a split holding structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out that left India and international crop protection in separate vehicles; a single conglomerate multiple and no value visibility per platform; crop protection's cash-flow and capital-allocation needs being, as COO Toshan Tamhane put it in Feb 2026, "very different from that of the seeds business" (he cited Corteva's own crop protection/seeds split); and inability to raise capital or set governance per platform — the filing says the Scheme lets UPL 1 and UPL 2 "raise capital independently" and "optimize its capital structure," and Prasad said platforms with "independent capital structure, independent governance structure... will grow much faster." The demand came from several directions: analysts and investors gave five pieces of feedback that Prasad catalogued (reporting consistency, the four below-EBITDA items worth ~INR 5,000 crore or 60% of FY25 EBITDA, and debt/liquidity), rating agencies and lenders drove the deleveraging that Jai Shroff said had removed the leverage drag on the multiple, and private investors needed exits — KKR (which wrote a "$300-plus million check" into Advanta) and Alpha Wave (USD 350 Mn for ~12.44%, of which USD 250 Mn secondary from UPL Limited), plus The Upswing Trust, the UPL SAS investor that swapped into UPL Cayman and ends with 16.78% of UPL 2 as a public shareholder with one board nomination right. The result is two listed entities: UPL Limited as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform keeping SUPERFORM as its manufacturing arm and incubating new verticals, and UPL Global as what Mike Frank (its CEO-designate) called "the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform" in 140+ countries with 9 R&D centres, 25 formulation facilities and a 14% innovation rate. Shroff framed it as each business needing "a kind of independent life" and said the plan went through advisors and "at least 10 different structures," expected to complete in 12-15 months.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced as an unspecified value-unlock exercise on the 1 Aug 2025 Q1FY26 call, where Prasad said advisors had just been engaged to "explore unlocking value across all platforms" with "no firm decision on any structure," after Jai Shroff's press-release comment on restructuring; before that, on 31 Jan 2025, the only visible step was private monetization of Advanta (Alpha Wave's USD 350 Mn) and a net-debt/EBITDA target of ~2x. On 6 Nov 2025 it broadened to "restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO," explicitly linked to deleveraging, alongside the DECCO-into-Advanta integration. By 2 Feb 2026 it had a timetable and a first concrete step — Advanta's DRHP filed 19 Jan 2026, described as "the first such step in this direction," with corporate actions for all platforms "within a period of 1 to 3 years" — and management argued seeds and crop protection are fundamentally different businesses. The crop protection scheme itself was announced 20 Feb 2026 (CCI clearance 2-3 Jun 2026, exchange observation letters and the Upswing swap completed 29-31 Jul 2026), and by the 11 May 2026 Capital Markets Day the debate had shifted to the structure's fairness, with Old Bridge calling it "fairly detrimental to the current shareholders," Shroff defending it and Prasad promising to take investor feedback "unfiltered to the board" within a month or two.

points.point: Pre-history: value was being unlocked privately, not structurally — Alpha Wave bought ~12.44% of Advanta for USD 350 Mn, USD 250 Mn of it secondary from UPL Limited, the second global investor into Advanta in two years, with proceeds earmarked for debt repayment.
points.quote: We have signed a definitive agreement with Alpha Wave Global under which they will invest US$350 million, US$100 million as primary investment in the company, and US$250 million as secondary through purchase of shares from UPL Limited for an approximate 12.44% stake in the company.

points.point: First mention of structural work: advisors newly engaged to explore unlocking value across all platforms, with no decided structure and no timeline; Prasad tied it to a focus on significantly deleveraging the balance sheet over the next year or two.
points.quote: The idea behind engaging advisors is to explore unlocking value across all platforms.

points.point: The option set was named for the first time — restructuring, strategic fundraising or an IPO — after the DECCO post-harvest business was folded into Advanta in September 2025.
points.quote: I think we had indicated in our Q1 press release and subsequently also during the earnings call that UPL continues to evaluate various strategic opportunities to unlock shareholders' value across platforms, including restructuring or strategic fundraising, potential liquidity events like IPO.

points.point: Prasad linked the value-unlock options directly to the debt problem, in the context of USD 500 Mn due March 2026 and ~USD 900 Mn of Q3/Q4 FY27 maturities.
points.quote: We had indicated during Q1 earnings call and press release that we are looking at various options to unlock shareholders' value. And if some of those we decide to take, that would also help in terms of deleveraging the balance sheet.

points.point: Advanta's DRHP (filed 19 January 2026) was presented as the first concrete step, within a stated 1-to-3-year window of corporate actions covering every platform.
points.quote: As we have communicated earlier, we remain focused in evaluating various corporate actions for all our platforms, including IPO and restructuring within a period of 1 to 3 years.

points.point: The Advanta IPO was an offer for sale, not a primary raise — KKR selling 2.2% and UPL Limited 7.8% — with proceeds going to the group, principally to cut debt rather than to fund Advanta.
points.quote: This transaction is offer for sale. It's not a primary transaction. So the cash is not going to Advanta. It is coming to the selling shareholders, which are KKR and UPL Limited in this case.

points.point: The clearest business logic given for separating platforms: crop protection and seeds have fundamentally different cash-flow and capital-allocation profiles, with Corteva's own split cited as precedent and Advanta called the eighth-largest global seeds player.
points.quote: As you would have seen globally, Corteva has also announced a split between crop protection and seeds because just those two businesses are fundamentally different, and we believe Advanta as the eighth largest seeds player globally has a journey and destiny of its own.

points.point: Tamhane conceded the trigger was partly that private-round valuations (KKR, then Alpha Wave) were not being reflected in UPL Limited's own price, so public-market separation was needed to capture it.
points.quote: Because, if you look at the valuation that KKR and subsequently Alpha Wave came in at, at least we feel that the full value of that is not flowing through to UPL Limited.

points.point: The 20 Feb 2026 board-approved Composite Scheme consolidates UPL SAS (India crop protection) and UPL Cayman (global crop protection) into UPL Global, to be listed; UPL Limited stays listed as a diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform.
points.quote: The Scheme proposes to consolidate the India Crop Protection Business held in UPL SAS and Global Crop Protection Business held in UPL Cayman, under a single entity, creating a focused, pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: Independent capital raising and capital-structure optimisation for each entity is given as a core benefit, alongside simplification of the group structure created by the 2022 platform carve-out and enhanced managerial and board focus.
points.quote: The Scheme will allow UPL 1 and UPL 2 to raise capital independently, allowing each entity to optimize its capital structure and pursue business opportunities more efficiently and effectively.

points.point: Scale claim for the new entity, with Mike Frank named CEO of UPL Global; promoters hold 71.56% of UPL 2 post-Scheme versus 28.44% public (The Upswing Trust alone 16.78%), and UPL promoters agreed to an 18-month voluntary lock-in from listing.
points.quote: Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.

points.point: The valuation argument stated most bluntly: a single conglomerate multiple is being applied to UPL, and separation is meant to make the sum of the parts visible once each platform has its own capital and governance structure.
points.quote: You know that even today market is valuing us using a single conglomerate multiple, they are applying on us.

points.point: Shroff's framing: brand- and IP-led businesses growing 3x-4x peers need autonomy, and the structure was chosen after extensive tax and structuring advice ahead of the announcement; SUPERFORM stays inside UPL Limited as the manufacturing platform.
points.quote: All these businesses need long-term need a kind of independent life, right?

points.point: Shroff said the historic leverage overhang that had suppressed UPL's multiple is gone — gross debt down 40% from USD 3.8 bn (FY24) to USD 2.3 bn and net debt down 48% to USD 1.6 bn, gearing from 4.6x to below 1.6x — clearing the way for the separation to be read as value unlock.
points.quote: We've also made sure that the as in the past leverage was an issue for which kept the multiple of the company.

points.point: An existing shareholder (Old Bridge Asset Management) objected that the announced structure would trigger a HoldCo discount and dilute existing holders, and pressed management on alternate structures; Shroff offered a meeting.
points.quote: But the challenge is that the manner in which that the current structure has been announced, it's likely to trigger a significant HoldCo discount.

points.point: Management said it had run a two-month investor consultation with a tracker of feedback that would go unfiltered to the board within a month or two, and that at least ten structures had been reviewed with advisors before this one was chosen.
points.quote: And very shortly, we will be presenting that unfiltered to the board.

rationale.what_management_expects: UPL Global: pure-play crop protection across 140+ countries, independent capital structure and governance, faster growth, wider investor and lender base. UPL Limited: diversified agri and specialty-chemicals platform retaining SUPERFORM, incubating new ventures, deleveraged with net debt/EBITDA below 1.6x. Both: independent fundraising, clearer sum-of-parts valuation removing the conglomerate discount, sharper board and managerial focus.
rationale.gaps: No debt split between UPL 1 and UPL 2, no UPL 2 standalone financials or guidance, no answer to the HoldCo-discount objection, no word on Advanta's IPO post-Scheme.

rationale.rationale: Astra Microwave is splitting itself into two sector-focused listed companies: the parent (AMPL) keeps Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry, while the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business is demerged on a going-concern basis into its wholly-owned subsidiary Astra Space Technologies Pvt Ltd (ASTPL), which will itself be listed on BSE and NSE. On the May 27, 2026 call MD S.G. Reddy said the board had given in-principle approval and framed the objective as creating 'sharper strategic and operational focus,' enabling dedicated management teams to chase sector-specific opportunities, enhancing governance and accountability, simplifying the corporate structure and creating 'clearer investment propositions to shareholders,' with focused growth, better capital allocation and improved operational efficiency over the medium to long term. The sizing numbers management gave: FY26 standalone turnover INR1,157 crore of which radar was ~60% and space plus meteorology ~16%; the scheme puts the demerged undertaking's FY26 turnover at ~INR157 crore, i.e. 13.58% of standalone turnover; the Dec-2025 order book of INR2,226 crore contained INR249 crore of space and INR369 crore of meteorology/hydrology orders. The scheme's stated reasoning is that space/met/hydro has 'distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile' needing a differentiated strategy, and that a standalone entity would be 'better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests,' thereby unlocking the value of that undertaking for shareholders. Mechanically there is no cash consideration: shareholders get 1 ASTPL share of Rs 2 for every 1 AMPL share of Rs 2, ASTPL's existing promoter-held capital is cancelled, and post-scheme ASTPL mirrors AMPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55%). No investor, lender or partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as management/board-initiated strategic re-alignment, though Atim Kabra had repeatedly argued on earlier calls that the embedded space business was worth far more than the market credited (Aug 2025: 'very, very valuable'; Nov 2025: peers raising at $750-800m valuations with almost no revenue, close to Astra's whole market cap). The move is also backed with people: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy took on oversight of the demerger, stepped down as AMPL MD and director from close of September 30, 2026 to join ASTPL as a director, and Joint MD Dr M.V. Reddy became AMPL's MD from October 1, 2026. As of the last filings, BSE gave 'no adverse observations' and NSE 'no objection' on October 29, 2026, SEBI/NCLT approvals are still pending, and no effect of the scheme has been taken into the Q2 FY27 accounts.
rationale.evolution: Through the Aug 14, 2025 and Nov 13, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk at all, but the groundwork was visible: Astra Space Technologies had been incorporated as a wholly-owned subsidiary with Bangalore clean rooms and a ~INR230-239 crore space order book, and Atim Kabra argued the space business was being carried inside Astra at far less than standalone peers' valuations. On the Feb 13, 2026 call there was still no mention of a demerger, only Kabra's hint about needing to 'be creative' on financing and 'watch the space.' The board granted in-principle approval on Feb 27, 2026, which surfaced publicly in the April 3, 2026 press release (tied to the MD succession) and was first spoken to investors on the May 27, 2026 (Jun 2026) call, where the detailed scheme was promised 'over the next few weeks.' The board approved the full Scheme of Arrangement on June 10, 2026, and the stock exchanges issued their observation/no-objection letters on October 29, 2026; notably, not a single analyst asked a question about the demerger on the May 27, 2026 call.

points.point: First disclosure on a call: the board has in-principle approved demerging the space, meteorology and hydrology business, with the formal scheme to follow within weeks.
points.quote: On a strategic front, the Board of Directors have in-principle approved demerger of our space, meteorology, and hydrology business.

points.point: The stated objective is focus, not cash or deleveraging.
points.quote: The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments.

points.point: The specific problems named: management bandwidth, governance/accountability, a complicated corporate structure and an unclear investment case for shareholders.
points.quote: The proposed structure will enable dedicated management teams to pursue sector-specific growth opportunities, enhance governance and accountability, simplify the corporate structure, and create clearer investment propositions to shareholders.

points.point: Expected outcome framed over the medium to long term, including capital allocation.
points.quote: Over the medium to long term, we believe this initiative will support focused growth, better capital allocation, and improved operational efficiency.

points.point: Scale of the business being separated, as management described FY26 revenue mix: space and meteorology ~16% versus radar ~60%.
points.quote: Our radar business continued to be a primary growth driver, contributing nearly 60% of our revenue, while space and meteorology segment contributed around 16%, demonstrating our expanding footprint in strategic and high-technology domains.

points.point: The June 10, 2026 scheme disclosure states the purpose as creating two separately listed sector-focused companies — radar/EW/telemetry on one side, space/met/hydro on the other.
points.quote: The proposed demerger is intended to create two sector-focused listed entities, namely: (a) Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry business focused entity; and (b) Space, Meteorology and Hydrology focused entity;

points.point: Core argument: the two businesses face different industry, competitive, regulatory and risk conditions and therefore need different strategies.
points.quote: The Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy aligned with its specific market opportunities.

points.point: Capital-access rationale — the only place any outside constituency (investors, partners, lenders) is invoked, and as a prospective benefit rather than as a party that asked for the split.
points.quote: A standalone Space, Meteorology and Hydrology entity would be better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests.

points.point: Explicit value-unlock objective for AMPL shareholders.
points.quote: unlocking the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company.

points.point: Size of the carve-out quantified in the filing: ~INR157 crore of FY26 turnover, 13.58% of the parent's total.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking of the Company for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 was approximately INR. 157 Crores , representing 13.58% of the total turnover of the Demerged Company for the said year.

points.point: No cash changes hands; a 1:1 share entitlement mirrors AMPL's register into ASTPL (promoters 6.45%, public 93.55% post-scheme), and ASTPL shares will be listed on BSE and NSE.
points.quote: For the purpose of the demerger of Demerged Undertaking ( as defined in the Scheme ) of Demerged Company into Resulting Company, the Resulting Company shall issue 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each for every 1 fully paid-up equity share of INR 2 (Indian Rupees 2/- only) each held in the Demerged Company ("Share Entitlement Ratio").

points.point: Leadership is being split alongside the businesses: MD S. Gurunatha Reddy was given the demerger and will move to ASTPL, with Dr M.V. Reddy taking over as AMPL MD from October 1, 2026 (April 3, 2026 press release; confirmed in the August 10, 2026 board outcome).
points.quote: In this role, he will lead the adoption of tailored growth strategies and capital allocation frameworks suited to the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology sector, thereby enabling focused management attention, enhanced operational efficiency and the unlocking of value for the shareholders of the Company.

points.point: Status as of the latest filings: exchange clearances in hand on October 29, 2026; SEBI/NCLT and other approvals still pending, with no accounting effect taken in Q2 FY27.
points.quote: AMPL has received observation letter with "no adverse observations" from BSE Limited on 29th October 2026 and observation letter with "no objection" from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited on 29th October 2026 in relation to the Scheme of Arrangement.

points.point: Pre-announcement value framing: Kabra argued the embedded space business alone could justify something close to Astra's entire market capitalisation, versus peers raising at high valuations with little revenue.
points.quote: Companies are raising money at like $750 million, $800 million valuation with hardly any revenue numbers to their credit. If I extrapolate these numbers, actually, I got close to my current market capitalization.

points.point: Earliest hint of the value-unlock logic, alongside disclosure that Astra Space Technologies had been set up as a wholly-owned subsidiary with a ~INR230 crore space order book.
points.quote: So our order book, as SG mentioned, is in excess of INR230 crores over there. And given where companies with very limited indigenous capabilities are valued, you might find that our space business is actually very, very valuable.

points.point: Two weeks before the in-principle board approval, Kabra flagged a need for creative financing for development projects and told investors to watch for options crystallising — the closest the calls come to foreshadowing the restructuring.
points.quote: But as you know, balance sheet for efficiently -- for them to efficiently function, especially when our sales volumes are projected to go significantly higher, we need to be creative as well as ensure that there is enough financing is there so that our NCNC projects, the products being developed and the large blue sky thinking driven projects do not suffer due to inadequate financing.

rationale.what_management_expects: AMPL becomes a radar/EW/telemetry-focused listed company; space/met/hydro becomes a separately listed entity with its own management team, tailored growth strategy and capital allocation, sharper focus, better governance and accountability, a simpler structure, improved operational efficiency, easier access to sector-specific investors, partners and lenders, a clearer investment proposition and unlocked shareholder value. No margin, EBITDA or valuation targets were quantified.
rationale.gaps: No segment margins/EBITDA, asset-debt-employee split, ASTPL standalone financials, listing timeline, transaction costs, or where ARC/MMIC sit; no analyst questioned it; no requesting party named.

judge.what_is_spun: Asset-heavy hotel ownership and development undertaking: 12 hotels (11 operating, 1 under construction) plus development capabilities, demerged into Fleur Hotels
demerged_business_names: Red Fox by Lemon Tree Hotels
judge.reason: Segregate asset-heavy hotel ownership/development from the asset-light hotel management and brand platform, to achieve operational focus, greater flexibility for capital deployment, clearer alignment of business objectives and unlock long-term shareholder value
judge.insiders: Promoters Patanjali Govind Keswani and Spank Management hold 22.28% of LTH, 7.34% directly in Fleur post-scheme; Keswani non-retiring Executive Chairman of Fleur, turns non-executive at Lemon Tree March 2027
judge.hidden_value: Fleur becomes India's largest hotel owner by rooms (5,556 rooms, 39 hotels; FY25 revenue Rs 1,189 cr, net EBITDA Rs 509 cr), carries all group debt, and gets Warburg's Rs 960 crore; Lemon Tree is left debt-free, 80% EBITDA-margin fee business
judge.selling_pressure_why: Odd-lot entitlement (20 Fleur shares per 311 LTH shares) in a newly listed asset-heavy company whose investor base differs from asset-light Lemon Tree
judge.listing_timeline: Press release of 9 January 2026: "The entire process to listing of Fleur is expected to be completed within 12 to 15 months"; on the 29 May 2026 call Keswani said 12 months from then if NCLT is quick, otherwise 18 months; NSE observation letter of 22 September 2026 requires trading to commence within sixty days of the NCLT order
judge.read_next: Fleur's pro-forma financials in the Q4 FY26 presentation (FY27 net EBITDA ~Rs 850 crore) and Fleur's Information Memorandum

rationale.rationale: Management framed the demerger as splitting one company that had been doing two businesses with two different investor bases: an asset-heavy business that designs, develops, finances and owns hotels (pension funds, insurance companies betting on inflation, repricing and annuity yield) and an asset-light business that monetises brand, management, loyalty, distribution and technology with almost no capital intensity. Keswani said Lemon Tree had only built hotels in 2004-2007 because owners would not hand their hotels to an unknown brand, and that with the brand now widely recognised (MakeMyTrip's CEO told him 20-25% of occupancy comes from them the moment a Lemon Tree opens) there was no reason to keep owning assets rather than monetise the brand — explicitly the Marriott/Host Hotels and Hilton/Park Hotels playbook. Mechanically (Composite Scheme approved 9 Jan 2026, appointed date 1 April 2026): Carnation Hotels and Hamstede Living merge into LTH; Oriole Dr. Fresh, Canary, Sukhsagar and Manakin merge into Fleur against shares to LTH; and the Demerged Undertaking — 11 operating hotels plus Aurika Shimla under construction, the investment in Arum (Aurika Shillong, 165 rooms) and the entire development capability/team with exclusivity on all future ownership, leasing and development — demerges into Fleur, with 20 Fleur shares for every 311 LTH shares (demerged division turnover Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover; 1,563 operating rooms across 15 hotels per the presentation, 1,820 keys/17 hotels per the press release). A second stated problem was conflict of interest: development capability was moved to Fleur with 'Chinese firewalls' so Fleur shareholders could never feel Lemon Tree was cherry-picking the best assets for itself, and Lemon Tree must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur. All group debt (about Rs 1,300 crore at demerger, Rs 1,500 crore total borrowings at FY26-end, cost of debt 7.42%) goes to Fleur, leaving Lemon Tree debt-free with only technology and marketing spend, forcing the Board to frame a dividend/shareholder-reward policy. Warburg Pincus (Coastal Cedar Investments B.V.) bought APG's entire 41.09% of Fleur and committed up to Rs 960 crore of primary equity, giving Fleur roughly Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital at 1:1 debt-equity against 2,500+ rooms under active discussion and Aurika Nehru Place (572 rooms, ~Rs 700 crore); post-scheme LTH shareholders own ~74% of Fleur (32.96% direct plus ~41% through LTH) versus the 59% LTH owns today, and Fleur lists separately for 'transparent price discovery and market-driven valuation of the asset-heavy business'.
rationale.evolution: The idea was first visible as a Fleur listing aspiration in the Nov 2024 call, where Keswani said debt-freedom would come sooner 'if we list Fleur before that' and put an IPO 'within the next 2-3 years at most'; in the Aug 2025 call he disclosed that committees of directors had been set up in both Lemon Tree and Fleur to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via a demerger and listing it, alongside splitting the management teams (Neelendra Singh for LTH from 1 October, Saurabh Shatdal for Fleur), with listing hoped for end-CY2026. In the Nov 2025 call it was 'in process' with a Board subcommittee and a promise of 'some other even more exciting stuff' within three months; the scheme, the Warburg/APG transactions and the 74%/26% shareholding math were announced in the Jan 2026 (15 January) dedicated call with a 12-15 month path to listing. By the Feb 2026 call Keswani confirmed the scheme was effective from 1 April and, responding to Ashish Kumar's request, promised pro forma financials for both entities; those pro formas appeared with the Jun 2026 (29 May) results, where CCI approval (April 2026), Warburg's completed purchase of APG's stake and a longer 12-18 month NCLT-dependent timeline were given, followed by NSE/BSE observation letters on 22 September 2026.

points.point: Asked directly by Kunal Lakhan (CLSA) what was wrong with the old structure, Keswani said the hotel business has two subsets with two different investor types — developers/owners wanting chunky yield and inflation-linked annuity returns versus asset-light investors betting on brand and management — and Lemon Tree was a combination of both.
points.quote: We have actually separated 2 types of businesses. One is asset heavy, long -term appreciating asset, capital intensive. It has a different kind of investor, and this business has a very different kind of investor, and we wanted to actually attract both types of investors.

points.point: He explained the historical accident being corrected: hotels were built only to establish the brand, and with the brand now established the company should monetise it instead of owning assets.
points.quote: We were forced to build hotels to build our brand. But once we build our brand, technically, we do not need hotels because now it is time for Lemon Tree to monetize its brand, which is enormous recall.

points.point: The transfer of the development capability and exclusive development mandate to Fleur was driven by a conflict-of-interest problem — Fleur minorities fearing Lemon Tree would keep the best projects for itself — and was solved with firewalls.
points.quote: Development capability was an issue which was raised in order to maximize Fleur's growth, we did not want shareholders of Fleur to ever feel that Lemon Tree when it recommends any assets was cherry -picking, which means Lemon Tree would say, I have got this very nice asset in Delhi, why should I offer it to Fleur.

points.point: All of Lemon Tree's debt moves to Fleur: Fleur carries roughly Rs 1,300 crore of debt against a ~Rs 900 crore net EBITDA and can borrow another ~Rs 1,300 crore, while Lemon Tree goes to zero debt.
points.quote: Firstly, when this demerger happens, all the debt, including the Lemon Tree's debt, after adjustment is being transferred to Fleur. Fleur will have 100% of our debt and Lemon Tree will have zero debt.

points.point: Keswani justified keeping a ~41% indirect stake in Fleur (challenged by Jinesh Joshi on hold-co discount) as Lemon Tree retaining 'skin in the game' as Fleur's manager, with natural dilution as Fleur raises capital; he quantified that Rs 1,000 crore deployed by Fleur generates ~Rs 350 crore of turnover, Rs 170-180 crore EBITDA and ~Rs 30 crore of fees for Lemon Tree.
points.quote: We felt it was prudent to have significant skin in the game at this stage, which means that going forward, it is very possible that Lemon Tree may dilute or even increase its stake over time; this will obviously be a Board decision .

points.point: Warburg's Rs 960 crore primary commitment plus Fleur's own cash and 1:1 debt gives roughly Rs 3,000 crore to deploy pre-listing against 2,500 rooms in active discussion; Keswani guided Fleur to over Rs 1,000 crore net EBITDA by FY28 and Lemon Tree to 80% EBITDA margin / 60% PAT margin.
points.quote: We have potentially about Rs 3,000 crores available to deploy in this growth before we list.

points.point: Opening the call with pro forma financials for both entities, Keswani described the transaction as simple — Warburg has bought APG's Fleur stake, Lemon Tree transfers 17 hotels and development capabilities in exchange for Fleur shares to LTH shareholders, and Fleur lists.
points.quote: This scheme will result in 2 distinct financially sound businesses.

points.point: He restated the economic outcome for each entity: Lemon Tree debt-free, high-margin, high-ROCE and fee/brand-driven; Fleur the consolidated owner of a fully renovated portfolio, post-scheme India's largest hotel platform by inventory at 5,600 rooms and 39 operational hotels.
points.quote: Post the reorganization , Lemon Tree will emerge as a debt -free, high-margin, high ROCE company generating strong free cash flows from fees and brand -related income.

points.point: Shareholder arithmetic: LTH shareholders end up with close to 74% of Fleur (33% direct, ~41% through Lemon Tree) versus the 59% Lemon Tree directly owns in Fleur today, before Warburg's primary infusion; Keswani also said he will cease to be executive at Lemon Tree from March 2027 and focus on Fleur as Executive Chair.
points.quote: Post reorganization , Lemon Tree shareholders will effectively own close to 74% of Fleur Hotels, 33% directly and about 41% indirectly through Lemon Tree.

points.point: Answering Achal Kumar, Keswani confirmed Fleur will be brand-agnostic post-demerger and may hand assets to other operators — Lemon Tree has no automatic right to Fleur's hotels and must earn them on results.
points.quote: Yes. But Lemon Tree must be able to deliver best results to get it . Just because Lemon Tree has skin in the game with Fleur does not mean that it has an automatic right to any asset that Fleur develops.

points.point: On capital allocation after the split, Lemon Tree is expected to need almost no capital and move to distributing profits, while Fleur will retain capital for growth rather than pay dividends.
points.quote: Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on. It will be essentially a zero -debt cash accretive company.

points.point: Keswani confirmed the scheme is effective from 1 April and that Lemon Tree becomes debt-free from next year, with all assets and debt going to Fleur and fee income becoming free cash; the Board must decide a dividend policy within six months.
points.quote: What will happen is in the scheme of demerger, all the assets of Lemon Tree, including its debt will be transferred to Fleur. Lemon Tree will immediately effectively be a debt -free company from next year.

points.point: Investors pushed for separate reporting: Ashish Kumar of Infinity Alternatives asked for pro forma financials of both businesses while awaiting the listing, and management agreed to publish them from the next quarter.
points.quote: Now that we have decided on the split of the 2 businesses, what might be helpful is if we can add pro forma financials for both of the assets as they look like so that while we are waiting for the l isting, we do get a good sense of what the numbers are looking like.

points.point: Keswani positioned the asset-light entity as a first in India, with fee income from hotels signed three years earlier only now flowing, and Fleur guided to ~Rs 1,000 crore EBITDA by FY28, its first year as a listed company.
points.quote: And keep in mind that Lemon Tree will be the first fully asset -light brand owning tech and distribution and management company in India, the first.

points.point: The demerger was still with Board subcommittees of both Lemon Tree and Fleur, with management hinting that more than the demerger was being negotiated (the Warburg/APG transactions announced two months later).
points.quote: It is not only the demerger of Fleur, but some other even more exciting stuff, but we will talk about it when the time is right.

points.point: First formal disclosure of the structure: committees of directors in both companies to evaluate transferring LTH's assets into Fleur via demerger and then list Fleur, with Lemon Tree becoming asset-light and focused on management, brand and technology — described as the global trend in the space.
points.quote: You may have also seen that we have said that a committee of directors has been set up in Lemon Tree and in Fleur to evaluate how we can possibly look at a transfer of assets from Lemon Tree into Fleur through a demerger scheme and then automatically look at how we can list Fleur.

points.point: The separation of management was done first and explicitly for this purpose — Neelendra Singh to run asset-light Lemon Tree from 1 October and Saurabh Shatdal to drive Fleur's asset-heavy growth, with Keswani handholding and moving to strategic oversight.
points.quote: The intent of the leadership change was to get 2 very good people who would then run these two companies independently on a day -to-day basis.

points.point: Keswani drew a hard line on mandates — Fleur builds, buys and leases, Lemon Tree only manages or franchises — and noted that the more Fleur dilutes and raises capital, the more Lemon Tree's economic interest rises via fees (Rs 100+ crore this year, potentially Rs 300-400 crore from Fleur in three years).
points.quote: Fleur's mandate will be to focus on, at the right value, building, buying, or leasing hotels. Lemon Tree's will only be to manage or franchise. Lemon Tree will not lease hotels once the Fleur demerger happens.

points.point: The earliest trace in these calls: a Fleur listing was already seen as the accelerator of deleveraging, with Keswani putting an IPO within 2-3 years at most when asked by Prashant Biyani.
points.quote: I think we are sticking to our guidance that in the next 3 - 3.5 years, we should be debt free , but if we list Fleur before that then we will be debt free that much earlier.

points.point: The 9 Jan 2026 filing states the Board reviewed the business with a view to segregating the asset-heavy ownership/development undertaking from the asset-light management/brand platform, and that the demerged business is self-sustaining and better housed in Fleur; the demerged division's turnover was Rs 23,037.34 lakh, 59.90% of LTH standalone turnover.
points.quote: Therefore, to achieve operational focus, greater flexibility for capital deployment, and clearer alignment of business objectives, it is proposed under this Scheme to (i) amalgamate Transferor Company 3, Transferor Company 4, Transferor Company 5 and Transferor Company 6 with the Transferee Company; and (ii) demerge and vest the Demerged Undertaking (comprising the Demerged Hotel Properties and the Development Capabilities together with the related undertakings, as defined hereinafter) into the Transferee C ompany, while the Company will continue to focus on the asset -light hotel management support, brand and operations including management support of the hotels transferred to the Transferee Company and other properties.

points.point: A stated purpose is market-driven valuation: Fleur ceases to be LTH's subsidiary and lists, so LTH shareholders participate directly in the asset-heavy business through listed shares rather than through a subsidiary.
points.quote: Following the implementation of the Scheme, the Transferee Company will cease to be a subsidiary of the Company , and its shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges, enabling transparent price discovery and market -driven valuation of the asset -heavy business.

points.point: The filing also sets out structural clean-up and partner-flexibility objectives: merging two wholly owned subsidiaries into LTH to remove layering and cost, and creating a structure that lets Fleur bring in investors or co-development partners per project without touching LTH's brand operations.
points.quote: To create a flexible structure enabling the Transferee Company to attract investors or co -development partners for specific hotel projects, without affecting Company's brand operations or control over strategic decisions.

points.point: Continuity is contractually locked: every hotel amalgamated into or demerged to Fleur stays under Lemon Tree Hotel Operating Agreements (existing ones amended/restated and extended from the Appointed Date), and LTH must refer new acquisition/development opportunities to Fleur and drop them if Fleur declines.
points.quote: Further, all the hotels amalgamated with or demerged into the Transferee Company will continue to be managed and operated by the Company under Hotel Operating Agreements and, the existing Hotel Operating Agreements with the Transferee Company and its subsidiaries shall be amended and/or restated, inter alia, to reflect the revised terms as detailed in the Scheme, and the Company shall refer new hotel acquisition or development opportunities to the Transferee Company and shall not pursue them if declined, except for hotel operations/franchise arran gements through third parties.

points.point: The Shareholders' Agreement with Warburg gives Fleur the exclusive global right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets, Investor/LTH affirmative consent on reserved matters, up to 3 Investor and 3 LTH directors with Keswani as non-retiring executive chairman, and the right to inject up to Rs 960 crore of primary capital.
points.quote: The Agreement provides Fleur t he exclusive right to own, lease and develop hospitality assets globally, with LTHL being entitled to undertake key money arrangements, in the manner as mutually agreed.

points.point: The 22 Sept 2026 filing records receipt of NSE 'no objection' and BSE 'no adverse observation' letters under Regulation 37, valid six months, with NCLT, shareholder and creditor approvals still pending — the gating item management had flagged as the timing risk.
points.quote: In this regard, we wish to inform you that the Company has received the Observation Letter s with 'no objection ' from the NSE and 'no adverse observations' from the BSE on September 22, 2026 vide their respective letters , pursuant to Regulation 37 of the Listing Regulations , in relation to the Scheme .

rationale.what_management_expects: Lemon Tree: debt-free, fee/brand/tech-only, EBITDA margin from ~60% pro forma to 70-80% steady state, ~60% PAT margin, high ROCE, free cash funding dividends. Fleur: India's largest owner (5,600 rooms, 39 hotels), net EBITDA Rs 850 crore FY27 and Rs 1,000+ crore FY28, ~48%+ post-fee margins, Warburg-backed capital for 2,500+ rooms, capital growth not dividends, and separately listed for market valuation.
rationale.gaps: Absolute valuation of the demerged undertaking and Warburg's price for APG's stake, Fleur's issue price, hold-co discount size, post-demerger ROE, and fate of the two retained leases.

judge.what_is_spun: Agrochemicals (Crop Health Sciences) division — pesticides, insecticides, herbicides, biostimulants — demerged into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited
judge.reason: Risk and reward of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals differ; segregation enables focused growth, operational efficiency, independent capital allocation, different investor sets, and is expected to unlock the value of the business verticals.
judge.insiders: Promoter and Promoter Group hold 8,84,65,126 of 17,91,09,870 shares (~49%); 1:1 entitlement carries that stake into the Resulting Company. Demerged Company retains 20% post-listing; director P.S.R.K. Prasad sits on Natco Crop Health Sciences' board.
judge.hidden_value: Demerged turnover was only ₹60.62 crore, 1.48% of total; FY25 agro segment result was a ₹1,458 million loss. Management says it reached ~₹140 crore sales and roughly EBITDA breakeven. Separation removes a loss-maker from pharma and exposes an early-growth agro business.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Tiny (1.48% of turnover), loss-making, different industry; 4,22,879 pharma shareholders receive 1:1 agrochemical shares, with parent holding 20%.
judge.listing_timeline: Not stated as a listing date. Board (March 24, 2026): Appointed Date 1st October 2026 and "Subsequent to the Scheme coming into effect, the Resulting Company /Transferee Company shall apply for the listing of its equity shares over Stock Exchanges in accordance with the Scheme." On the Feb 12, 2026 call management said "roughly, we're thinking by October, November" and "we should be able to do it in the next 8, 9 months"; on Nov 14, 2025 "we are targeting that for the year 2026." On September 9, 2026 the Company said it "has not filed the Scheme and related applications with the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal" and will file a revised Scheme after the Rights Issue.
judge.read_next: The revised Scheme to be filed with Stock Exchanges post Rights Issue — check the share swap ratio and agro segment numbers.
judge.quote: The segregation is also expected to unlock the value of the business verticals of the Demerged Company.

rationale.rationale: NATCO is demerging its Crop Health Sciences (Agrochemicals) division into Natco Crop Health Sciences Limited, leaving the listed parent as a pure pharmaceutical company (FDFs, APIs, oncology-led branded/complex generics). Management's stated reason is that the two verticals carry different risk-reward profiles and serve entirely different customers — Rajesh Chebiyam said the demerger "gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different" — so a dedicated management, channel and product strategy (differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition molecules like the fungicide GLANZ and CTPR combinations) can be run without competing for attention inside a much larger pharma P&L. The second reason is valuation and capital: agro turnover was only INR 60.62 crore in FY25, i.e. 1.48% of total turnover, against FY25 group revenue of INR 4,784 crore and PAT of INR 1,883.4 crore, and Rajeev Nannapaneni said shareholders "will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma"; separately listed, "it can raise its own capital and grow by itself." The timing was deliberately set after the division approached breakeven — segment loss of about INR 150 crore in FY25 (including a INR 50 crore non-cash PP&E impairment taken in Q4 FY25), narrowing to a INR 3.2 crore loss in Q1 FY26 on INR 34.7 crore of sales, EBITDA-positive at INR 52.4 crore of sales in Q2 FY26, and roughly INR 140 crore of FY26 sales versus INR 60 crore the prior year, against the INR 150–170 crore management had said was needed for EBITDA breakeven. The Scheme adds the corporate-finance logic: focused growth, operational rationalisation, optimum use of resources, and the ability for each business to "address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders," plus unlocking the value of the verticals. Shareholders get 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 NATCO share, with NATCO retaining 20% of the post-listing equity to keep supporting a business "still at its early growth stages" — so holders retain 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct, 20% through NATCO). The push came from public-market shareholders, not lenders or partners: an investor on the Nov 14, 2025 call asked directly about "value unlocking for the shareholders," and management separately cited shareholder feedback that NATCO's profit base was too concentrated. Agro is almost entirely domestic ("predominantly domestic" sales, with 25–30% input cost inflation flagged in 2026), which management contrasts with the export-weighted pharma business.
rationale.evolution: On the Feb 13, 2025 and May 29, 2025 calls there was no demerger talk — only agro losses, the INR 50 crore impairment and a INR 120–170 crore breakeven target; the Aug 13, 2025 call reported the loss down to INR 3.2 crore with still no mention. The board gave in-principle approval to evaluate the demerger on Sep 25, 2025, and Rajeev first discussed it publicly on the Nov 14, 2025 call ("demerge this business from the main company and list it separately... targeting that for the year 2026"), framing it as value unlocking plus the ability to raise its own capital; the board approved incorporating the wholly-owned resulting company on Nov 14, 2025. On Feb 12, 2026 the timeline was guided to "October, November" 2026 (8–9 months), and the Scheme itself was approved on Mar 24, 2026 with a 1:1 share entitlement, appointed date Oct 1, 2026 and 20% retained by NATCO; the May 29, 2026 call reiterated focus and different customers as the primary reason. By Sep 9, 2026 the Scheme had stock-exchange observation letters but had not been filed with the NCLT, because the INR 1,279.36 crore rights issue at INR 750/share (allotted Oct 23, 2026) changes the capital structure — the board decided to re-cut and re-file the Scheme after the rights issue while keeping the same swap ratio.

points.point: First public confirmation of the plan: demerge Crop Health Sciences out of the parent and list it separately, targeted for 2026, disclosed alongside the division reaching roughly EBITDA breakeven at INR 52.4 crore of quarterly sales.
points.quote: I think we have announced earlier that we will demerge this business from the main company and list it separately and we are targeting that for the year 2026.

points.point: Rajeev defines the value-unlock logic in response to an investor question: separate listing gives the business special focus and the ability to raise its own capital and grow independently, now that it is breaking even.
points.quote: Value unlocking means I think what we see is this business now is about breaking even now. So, we will list it separately and then we will have special focus on this and it can raise its own capital and grow by itself.

points.point: The core valuation argument: the agro business is too small to be valued inside a pharma company of NATCO's size, and shareholders will get a complete see-through into both businesses.
points.quote: I think you will get another business which is not being valued in our system because it is of a very tiny business and a very large business in pharma.

points.point: Timeline guidance: the process has started, with an internal goal of completing in the next 8–9 months (around October–November 2026), but no firm date committed.
points.quote: I think we have started the process. So , I think roughly, we're thinking by October, November, but I don't want to say any definite time lines, but this is our, what should I say, goal to do.

points.point: Management's clearest operating rationale, from the head of Crop Health Sciences: a focused approach is needed because the agro customer base is entirely different from pharma, with FY26 agro sales of about INR 140 crore versus INR 60 crore the year before.
points.quote: So, as you're aware, so we're in the process of demerging the business. And one of the primary reasons we felt also it gives a more focused approach because the business, ultimately, the customers are quite different.

points.point: Growth plans — new differentiated, patent-controlled, limited-competition products, more channel partners and more people — are tied directly back to the demerger as the reason for sharper focus.
points.quote: So I think we're fairly confident going forward. And that's also one of the main reasons for demerging and having more focus on the business.

points.point: The Mar 24, 2026 Scheme of Arrangement grounds the demerger in differing risk-reward profiles of the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals verticals; agro turnover was INR 60.62 crore in FY25, 1.48% of total company turnover.
points.quote: The Board of Directors of the Demerged Company believe that the risk and reward associated with each of the aforesaid business verticals are different.

points.point: The Scheme's capital-markets rationale: each business can chase its own opportunities, allocate capital efficiently and attract its own investor and lender base, alongside focused growth, operational rationalisation and value unlocking.
points.quote: Each business would be able to address independent business opportunities, pursue efficient capital allocation and attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: NATCO keeps 20% of the post-listing equity of the resulting company so it can keep funding and strategically supporting an early-stage business; shareholders get 1 new share for every 1 NATCO share, retaining 100% of the ultimate economic interest (80% direct plus 20% indirect).
points.quote: Further, the Demerged Company intends to retain the current shareholding in the Resulting Company (20% of post listing shareholding) in order to continue to offer support to the Agrochemicals Business which is still at its early growth stages and help in monitoring the progress and providing strategic support.

points.point: The Nov 14, 2025 board filing states the purpose as unlocking value in the core pharmaceutical business while giving each entity operational flexibility, dedicated management and separate brand positioning.
points.quote: To demerge the Agro business of the Company into a separate entity, the move shall enable value unlocking of the core business (pharmaceuticals) and enhance long -term growth.

points.point: Pre-demerger baseline for why the division was a drag: a INR 50 crore non-cash impairment on agro property, plant and machinery in Q4 FY25, FY25 agro revenue of about INR 60 crore, and INR 160–170 crore needed just to be EBITDA positive.
points.quote: So, I think this year, we feel we are going to hit that critical mass where we'll start breaking even. We are doing about INR60 crores net revenue last year. So, I think we need to hit about INR160 crores to INR170 crores at least to have that EBITDA positive.

points.point: The Sep 9, 2026 board update: the Scheme had received observation letters from both exchanges but was not filed with the NCLT because the INR 1,300 crore rights issue changes the capital structure, so the Scheme will be amended and re-filed post-issue with the swap ratio unchanged.
points.quote: The fund raising by way of a Rights Issue proposed at the meeting of the board of directors held on September 09, 2026 is expected to result in change to the Company's capital structure and shareholding pattern and consequently would require necessary changes to the Scheme.

rationale.what_management_expects: Agro: dedicated management focus, its own capital raising, differentiated limited-competition products, growth past breakeven from roughly INR 140 crore sales. Pharma: a cleaner, focused oncology/complex-generics entity. For shareholders: value unlocked in a business "not being valued in our system," a complete see-through into both, operational efficiency, efficient capital allocation, and distinct investor/lender bases.
rationale.gaps: No standalone agro financials, debt/asset split, valuation or swap-ratio basis; no post-demerger profitability, capital needs, board/management, listing date, or revised Scheme terms.

judge.what_is_spun: The Merchant Power Undertaking — merchant thermal power — demerged into Talwandi Sabo Power Limited, renamed Vedanta Power Limited
judge.reason: Demerger "empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value"; "simpler structures, sharper accountability, and focused platforms"
judge.insiders: Promoter Vedanta Resources held 54.72% of VEDL (Twin Star 40.02%, Vedanta Holdings Mauritius II 12.60%, Welter 0.98%); 1 TSPL share per VEDL share, proportionate, so promoter stake carries over unchanged
judge.hidden_value: Power carried the heaviest leverage of the five: pro forma EBITDA $0.14bn, gross debt $0.9bn, net debt $0.8bn, 4.7x vs group 0.95x. Residual Vedanta kept Zinc India (56% margin) at 0.4x; combined market cap of resulting companies rose over ₹71,000 crore in Q1FY27
judge.selling_pressure_why: Every VEDL holder received 1 TSPL share; standalone thermal power is a different industry from metals, smallest EBITDA share, highest leverage 4.7x
judge.listing_timeline: Apr 29, 2026 call: "The effective and record date is set for May 1st... The shares of the resulting companies are expected to list and commence trading by mid-June." Q1FY27 presentation (Jul 30, 2026): "Demerger effective 1st May '26, 4 new entities listed on NSE & BSE on 15th June"
judge.read_next: Vedanta Power's own first standalone results — 4.7x pro forma net debt/EBITDA and Athena Unit 1 restart timeline
judge.quote: Vedanta's demerger is unlocking significant shareholder value, with combined market cap of resulting companies growing by over ₹71,000 crore in the 1st quarter.

rationale.rationale: Management's stated reason is structural: Vedanta Limited is being split into five independent, sector-specific "pure-play" companies — residual Vedanta Limited (Zinc India/HZL, Zinc International, Copper, Ferrochrome/FACOR, Nickel), Vedanta Aluminium Metal, Vedanta Power (Talwandi Sabo Power), Vedanta Oil & Gas (Malco Energy) and Vedanta Iron & Steel — so each can "chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors," with simpler structures and sharper accountability (Apr 2026). The second pillar is capital structure: the demerger was "architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company," carving the $5.5bn net debt (group leverage 0.95x, down from 1.22x) so Oil & Gas is nil-debt, Iron & Steel ≤$0.2bn, Aluminium carries $3.5bn at 1.3x, Power 4.7x on long-dated 7–10 year PFC/REC maturities, and residual Vedanta ~$1bn at 0.4x. Lenders were an explicit gating party — debt allocation was "broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval" (Jan 2026) — while shareholders and creditors voted on 18 Feb 2025 and MoPNG objected in NCLT over oil & gas disputed dues (~$512m), a concern settled by a Vedanta corporate guarantee, alongside a ₹660 crore full-and-final SEPCO settlement that "paved the way" (Nov 2025). Governance flexibility is a named benefit: five independent boards, with dividend policy moving from prescriptive/rule-based (minimum 30% of profit; HZL dividend upstreamed within six months) to descriptive/principle-based, removing the HZL upstreaming mandate (Apr 2026). Differentiated capital structures were also pitched as a financing route — "many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table" as an additional deleveraging avenue, relevant to the $4.7bn still at Vedanta Resources (FY27 need ~$1bn: ~$0.3bn debt plus ICL and ~$0.45bn interest, funded by ~$400m brand fee and a 4–5% dividend). Specific economics were quantified only for copper: post-demerger its brand fee falls from 3% to 0.75% (~$65m on $3.1–3.2bn revenue), lifting EBITDA by 2.25% and taking a "wafer-thin" ~1% margin trading business to at least 5% in FY27. Post-completion filings supply the value-unlock arithmetic — ₹225.50 at the 29 Sep 2023 announcement versus ₹932.05 combined on the 15 June 2026 listing (>300% upside) and combined market cap up over ₹71,000 crore in Q1 FY27 — and the same logic is then reused for a sixth separation: ~2,264 acres and ~53,185 sq ft of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms (1 share for every 20), because that portfolio sat "embedded within the operating business" with sub-optimal visibility and potential value of ₹30,000 crore+.
rationale.evolution: The idea pre-dates this window (announced 29 Sep 2023) and by Feb 2025 was "in the important stage of execution" with the shareholder/creditor meeting on 18 Feb 2025, moving to the NCLT second-motion petition, and Apr 2025 framed it as creating "pure-play entities" targeted for September 2025. It then slipped repeatedly: Aug 2025 reported the 2 July NCLT hearing left incomplete (next 20 August) plus an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power order and MoPNG's objection; Nov 2025 cleared the blockers via a ₹660 crore SEPCO settlement and a Vedanta corporate guarantee for MoPNG's alleged claims, with final hearing set for 12 November and listing guided "by the end of FY26." Jan 2026 reported NCLT approval (16 December for four businesses, 9 January for power), Ind AS 105 discontinued-operations accounting and a 1 April effective date; Apr 2026 pushed effective/record date to 1 May 2026 with listing by mid-June and added the newly disclosed mechanics — five dividend policies, HZL upstreaming mandate dropped, copper brand fee cut to 0.75%, entity-wise debt split. After listing (15 June 2026), the 30 July 2026 filing extended the same rationale to a further demerger of surplus real estate into Vedanta Property Platforms, targeted for FY28.

points.point: Goel defines the deal: five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, each free to pursue its own growth path and court its own investor base, effective 1 May 2026 with listing targeted in Q1 FY27.
points.quote: This will entail creation of five independent sector-specific pure-play companies, allowing each company to chart out their own growth trajectory and attract respective thematic investors.

points.point: The debt split was deliberately engineered pre-demerger to match each entity's cash generation and growth stage; group leverage was 0.95x going in.
points.quote: The de-merger has been architected with precision on capital structure, aligning debt with earning strength and growth stage of each resulting company.

points.point: Goel gives the entity-wise net debt: Oil & Gas debt-free, Iron & Steel ≤$0.2bn, Aluminium $3.5bn at 1.3x, Power mostly long-dated PFC/REC debt at 4.7x, residual Vedanta ~$1bn at 0.4x.
points.quote: So even before de-merger on 1st of May, Vedanta Oil and Gas will have nil debt, so it will be debt-free company.

points.point: Each of the five boards gets its own dividend policy; Vedanta's shifts from rule-based (minimum 30% payout, HZL dividend passed on within six months) to principle-based, and the HZL upstreaming mandate is removed.
points.quote: Currently, Vedanta's policy on dividend is more prescriptive; it will become more descriptive.

points.point: Asked how VRL's remaining $4.7bn debt gets addressed, Goel names the demerger itself as a new funding lever via differentiated capital structures and anchor investors entering individual cap tables.
points.quote: Now as we de-merge all the five companies, additionally we'll have the optionality of a differentiated capital structure and in that case, many anchor investors domestically and globally are very keen to come in the cap table, and that will be additional avenue for de-leveraging.

points.point: Only quantified per-business economic gain: copper's brand fee is re-benchmarked down from 3% to 0.75% (≈$65m on $3.1–3.2bn revenue), taking a ~1%-margin trading business to at least 5% in FY27; the 3% rate holds for the others to FY29.
points.quote: So the brand fee for copper from the current 3% will go down to 0.75% and that alone from India's viewpoint means higher EBITDA by 2.25%.

points.point: Naidoo explains the post-demerger operating model: CEOs mandated to deliver each company's own 2x/3x organic growth, with cross-portfolio M&A sitting above them at a holdco alongside the Chairman.
points.quote: Anything outside of the portfolio would still happen at the holdco level.

points.point: On NCLT approval (16 Dec 2025 order; certified copy 21 Jan 2026), Naidoo frames the purpose as sharper strategy, stronger balance sheets and faster growth per business.
points.quote: This marks a defining moment in our journey, one that empowers our businesses to sharpen the strategies, strengthen the balance sheets and accelerate growth with the aim of unlocking shareholder value.

points.point: Lenders effectively dictated the debt carve-up: bank NOCs for the demerger were conditional on agreeing the allocation of the ~$6.7bn Vedanta India consolidated net debt across entities.
points.quote: When we went to the banker seeking NOC, in that case, debt allocation was broadly aligned with the bankers as a precondition for granting NOC for demerger approval.

points.point: Goel calls the demerger an opportunity on taxation and structuring, and states the intent to hand over a debt-free oil & gas and near-debt-free iron & steel, part-funded by the ₹3,000 crore HZL OFS used for deleveraging.
points.quote: And as I earlier mentioned, our intent is to make oil and gas business debt-free, and also our iron steel business almost debt-free.

points.point: Litigation is ring-fenced by business: the $512m MoPNG arbitration outcome, gain or loss, follows oil & gas post-demerger rather than the group.
points.quote: It is ring fenced to oil and gas, whatever the decision.

points.point: A long-standing creditor dispute was settled in cash specifically to unblock the scheme — ₹660 crore to SEPCO, booked as an exceptional item alongside the ₹1,407 crore TSPL provision.
points.quote: As part of demerger proceedings, a full and final settlement of Rs. 660 Cr has been done with SEPCO, thereby resolving a long-standing dispute, paving the way for a proposed demerger process.

points.point: MoPNG's NCLT objection was that the demerged oil & gas P&L might not sustain alleged claims (~$520m); Naidoo says a parent corporate guarantee covering the full extent was given to clear it.
points.quote: Their concern has been taken care of by us providing a corporate guarantee from Vedanta.

points.point: Goel positions completion as unlocking value across five verticals, with VRL refinanced to ~10% cost and ~$0.5bn/year maturities in parallel.
points.quote: On the demerger, we are at the final stage. We remain confident of completing our demerger by end of this fiscal, unlocking focused value across our five verticals.

points.point: Process risk was live: the NCLT second-motion hearing on 2 July was not completed, NCLAT had stayed the TSPL power demerger order, and a ₹1,248 crore cash-backed bank guarantee was lodged with NCLAT.
points.quote: Separately, the NCLAT has granted an interim stay on TSPL, our power demerger order by NCLT, with the next hearing scheduled on 4th August.

points.point: Earliest framing in this window from new Group CEO Naidoo under the "Vedanta 2.0" banner: pure-play entities for strategic focus and operational flexibility, with completion then expected by September 2025.
points.quote: We are making good progress with our demerger plan, aiming to create pure-play entities that will enhance strategic focus and operational flexibility.

points.point: Goel places the scheme at the shareholder and creditor voting stage (18 Feb 2025) and casts it as value unlock for investors.
points.quote: This transformative step is poised to unlock significant value for our investors.

points.point: Post-listing filing (30 July 2026) quantifies the claimed unlock: ₹225.50 per Vedanta share at the 29 Sep 2023 announcement versus ₹932.05 combined value of the five companies on 15 June 2026 listing, and combined market cap up over ₹71,000 crore in Q1 FY27.
points.quote: Unlocked hidden value by enabling each business to be valued independently.

points.point: The same logic is extended to a sixth separation — surplus real estate (~2,264 acres, ~53,185 sq ft, FY26 turnover ₹1.26 crore, 0.001% of standalone revenue) into Vedanta Property Platforms, 1 share for every 20 Vedanta shares, with potential value of ₹30,000 crore+.
points.quote: The real estate business is currently embedded within the operating business and the real estate portfolio has been historically subject to limited focused utilisation, resulting in sub-optimal visibility of the real estate business segment and value realization.

points.point: Chairman Anil Agarwal explicitly links the real estate carve-out to the five-way demerger's result, and the scheme is structured as a tax-neutral vertical split with no change in economic interest.
points.quote: After the recent success of the five-way demerger creating "pure-play" entities across oil and gas, aluminium, power, and steel, we plan to demerge the surplus real estate assets into an independent "pure-play" company to unlock significant value for the stakeholders.

rationale.what_management_expects: Each entity: sharper strategy, own board, dividend and M&A mandate (holdco keeps cross-portfolio deals), and a balance sheet sized to its own cash flows. Copper margin from ~1% to at least 5% in FY27 on a 0.75% brand fee; Zinc International EBITDA from ~$100m to ~$450m by FY28; Power targeting 10–12 GW more; thematic and anchor investors to lift valuations and fund growth.
rationale.gaps: No per-entity valuation or multiple math, no demerger cost/tax leakage, no reason HZL and semiconductors stay in residual Vedanta, no view on duplicated listed-company overheads.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is SBI Funds Management Limited (SBIFM) — SBI Mutual Fund, the bank's asset-management joint venture with Amundi — which SBI is partially separating by listing it, not by demerging it; management repeatedly framed the purpose as "value unlocking" and, in Chairman C.S. Setty's words, "more importantly, value recognition for the industry" (Nov 2025), with SBI General Insurance named alongside AMC as the other listing candidate. The driver management gave was that SBI's own stock does not reflect the conglomerate's worth: Setty called SBI's valuation "a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics" (Nov 2025, with ROE 19.7%–20.68% and ROA >1% through FY26), and the same theme runs through the hidden-value argument on strategic holdings — of the group's ~7.3% NSE stake he said "the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market" (May 2026). Explicitly NOT a capital-need story at first: in Nov 2025 Setty said "these two companies do not require capital at this juncture. Neither the parent requires because we just raised Rs. 25,000 crores" (the July 2025 QIP, India's largest, 4.5x oversubscribed on a >Rs. 1.1 trillion book, >60% cross-border), which is why timing was left to "respective boards"; by May 2026 the rationale had hardened into a capital one — the listing "will result in capital augmentation, CET-1" on top of CAR already up 115bps to 15.4%. The structure confirms it is monetisation, not a fix for the business: the IPO is a pure offer for sale (no fresh issue), SBI offering 6.3007% and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006%, total up to 10.0013% / 203,709,239 shares at Rs. 1 face value, so no money reaches SBIFM itself. Management stressed that separation does not break the franchise link — SBIFM stays the country's largest AMC inside the "One SBI" cross-sell engine (a special dividend of ~Rs. 2,200 crore came up to the bank in Q3FY26, cross-sell/CVE income targeted at $1 billion, YONO "deep integration with subsidiary production"), and Setty was explicit that "Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves" (Feb 2026). The push came from the sell side and retail investors — Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity), Manoj Alimchandani and Kunal Shah (Citigroup) raised monetisation/value-unlocking on four of the five calls, Alimchandani even arguing in Feb 2026 that delaying the IPO five years could fetch three times the market cap — rather than from lenders or regulators; the only regulator-linked nudge cited was the SEBI chairman on NSE's listing. No problem with SBIFM's performance was ever offered as a reason: it was described only as "the largest AMC in the country," contributing Rs. 4,969.09 crore of FY26 total income, just 0.70% of group income.
rationale.evolution: May 2025 had no separation plan at all — only "we will continue to nurture these subsidiaries," while the bank instead took an enabling resolution for Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity. By Aug 2025 Setty conceded "a couple of candidates for listing, but… there is no sense of urgency," and in Nov 2025 he named them — SBI AMC and SBI General — as the right candidates for "value unlocking" and "value recognition," with boards to set timing; the SBIFM stake-sale approval for 6.3007% followed on 6 Nov 2025 and the DRHP on 19 Mar 2026 (share count restated to 128,334,397 after a bonus issue and ESOP exercises). Feb 2026 added the retained-upside caveat ("we are not fully exiting") and May 2026 re-cast the deal as CET-1 capital augmentation to be completed within FY27. The plan then changed in execution in July 2026: a pre-IPO placement of 28,832,748 shares (1.4156%) to 30 investors at Rs. 574 for Rs. 1,655 crore on 9–10 July cut SBI's offer-for-sale from 6.3007% to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%), priced at Rs. 574 with allotment expected 18 July 2026.

points.point: No separation on the table: subsidiaries framed purely as value creators to be retained, while the bank instead took an enabling resolution to raise Rs. 25,000 crore of its own equity.
points.quote: Our subsidiaries are consistently performing well and continue to create significant value for all the stakeholders. We will continue to nurture these subsidiaries and maintain leadership position in the respective businesses.

points.point: First acknowledgement of listing candidates, asked for by Sushil Choksey (Indus Equity Advisors); Setty explicitly de-prioritised it because the Rs. 25,000 crore QIP had just closed.
points.quote: No, as we mentioned that we definitely have a couple of candidates for listing, but the timing is not very… there is no sense of urgency there, I believe.

points.point: The rationale stated in full for the first time, in answer to Choksey on the group's underperforming consolidated value: SBI AMC and SBI General named, with value unlocking and industry recognition of value as the purpose.
points.quote: But among these four major subsidiaries, we definitely would be looking at, as I mentioned several times, SBI AMC and SBI General are right candidates for listing in our stable. It also provides some value unlocking and, more importantly, value recognition for the industry.

points.point: Answering Kunal Shah (Citigroup) on what would trigger the decision, Setty ruled capital need out as a motive for either the subsidiaries or the parent, leaving timing and quantum to the subsidiary boards.
points.quote: I think we need to just look at, see, one is, as I mentioned earlier also, that these two companies do not require capital at this juncture.

points.point: The underlying grievance the separation is meant to address — SBI's own market valuation not tracking its ROE and growth — stated in the Chairman's opening remarks; Ashok Ajmera had quantified it as a Rs. 8.82 lakh crore market cap on Rs. 100 trillion of business versus Rs. 15.14 lakh crore for a Rs. 57 trillion peer.
points.quote: Although the current valuations of SBI are a conundrum, considering our return on equity and growth metrics, we are confident that they will eventually align with our fundamental and operational metrics, the institutionalized nature of our business and our market leadership in the coming years.

points.point: Retained-stake logic: asked by Manoj Alimchandani whether delaying the IPO five years could treble the market cap, Setty defended a partial sale that keeps future upside with SBI.
points.quote: Mutual fund, we are not fully exiting. So we still have potential to monetize further when market improves.

points.point: Why the AMC is worth separating while staying attached: it is already the country's largest AMC, upstreamed a Rs. 2,200 crore special dividend into SBI's Q3FY26 profit, and feeds a cross-sell income stream management targets at $1 billion.
points.quote: If I have to talk about one-off, I think the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund.

points.point: The rationale shifts to capital: with the AMC listing under way, Setty tied it to CET-1 augmentation supporting credit growth (the bank could already fund ~Rs. 12 trillion of growth, CAR 15.4%, up 115bps YoY).
points.quote: We are also seriously, as you are aware, we have embarked on listing SBI AMC and hopefully in this financial year we will be able to complete, which will result in capital augmentation, CET-1.

points.point: Same hidden-value argument applied to the group's ~7.3% NSE holding, which is not marked to market today — listing is the mechanism that converts unrecognised strategic stakes into reported reserves.
points.quote: But as you mentioned, I think the moment NSE gets listed, the whole shareholding by SBI will be available as reserve to us to mark to market.

points.point: 6 Nov 2025 board approval, restated in the 19 Mar 2026 DRHP filing: a pure offer for sale of up to 10.0013% (203,709,239 shares of Rs. 1 each) — SBI 6.3007% (128,334,397 shares) and JV partner Amundi India Holding 3.7006% (75,374,842 shares). No fresh issue, so no proceeds go to SBIFM.
points.quote: The IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by State Bank of India, and of up to 75,374,842 Equity Shares (amounting to 3.7006% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFML) by Amundi India Holding.

points.point: Plan changed in execution: a pre-IPO secondary placement on 9–10 July 2026 moved 1.4156% of pre-offer capital to 30 investors at the eventual Rs. 574 offer price, raising Rs. 1,655 crore for SBI ahead of the book build.
points.quote: State Bank of India had entered into share purchase agreements each dated July 9, 2026 to sell, in aggregate, 2,88,32,748 equity shares of SBIFM of face value Rs. 1 (one) each ("Equity Shares"), being equivalent to 1.4156% of pre-Offer share capital of SBIFM, to a total of 30 (thirty) investors at Rs. 574.00 per Equity Share, for an aggregate consideration of Rs. 1,655.00 crores.

points.point: The 11 July 2026 addendum cut SBI's offer-for-sale by exactly the pre-IPO quantum, to 4.8851% (total offer 8.3933%); the offer was priced at Rs. 574 on 16 July with a Rs. 54 employee discount and allotment expected on or about 18 July 2026.
points.quote: The size of the offer for sale by the State Bank of India in the IPO has been revised from up to 128,334,397 Equity Shares (amounting to 6.3007% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM) to up to 99,501,649 Equity Shares (amounting to 4.8851% of the paid-up equity share capital of SBIFM).

points.point: Materiality disclosed for the separated business: SBIFM's FY2026 total income of Rs. 4,969.09 crore is 0.70% of group income and its reserves 0.59% of group reserves — the separation is about price discovery, not size.
points.quote: Total income: Rs. 4,969.09 crores (0.70% of Total Income of SBI Group)

rationale.what_management_expects: For SBIFM: a listed market price that recognises India's largest AMC, with SBI retaining control, banca distribution and future monetisation upside. For SBI: value unlocking and "value recognition," CET-1 capital augmentation supporting 13-15% credit growth, hidden reserves surfaced (as with NSE), and valuation converging on >1% ROA and 15%+ through-cycle ROE. No margin or focus benefit was claimed.
rationale.gaps: No valuation target, expected proceeds, CET-1 basis points, or use of funds; no reason the offer was trimmed; Amundi's motive, SBI General's timeline, and post-listing distribution/royalty terms unexplained.
