rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Bhushan Power and Steel Limited's (BPSL) steel undertaking in Odisha — acquired through the IBC in 2021 and expanded from 2.75 MTPA to 4.5 MTPA — which JSW Steel carved out by slump sale on a going-concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited for cash consideration of Rs.24,483 crores, after which JFE Steel of Japan (a strategic partner since 2009, with Mr. Hiroyuki Ogawa already a JFE nominee on JSW's board) took 50% of holding company JSW Kalinga Steel Limited for Rs.15,750 crores in two equal tranches, valuing the BPSL steel business at Rs.31,500 crores equity and Rs.53,000 crores enterprise value. Management's stated purpose was not to exit steel but to fund growth without stretching the balance sheet: the deal brought a cash inflow of ~Rs.32,000 crores and deleveraging of ~Rs.37,000 crores, of which ~Rs.30,000 crores was completed by 31 March 2026, taking net debt to ~Rs.54,000 crores and leverage from 2.91x (Dec-25) to 1.81x, with a credit-rating outlook uplift; the remaining ~Rs.7,900 crores was to follow with JFE's second tranche by end-June 2026. Jayant Acharya framed it as a 'double engine of growth' — the JV lets JSW expand faster in India while deleveraging, so JSW Steel alone targets 62 million tonnes by FY32 (raised from 50 mt by FY31) and the JFE and POSCO JVs add a cumulative 16 mt, ~78 mt in India and ~80 mt including Ohio, against a capex plan of Rs.1,26,000 crores plus up to another Rs.1,00,000 crores to FY33 where the JV spend is only JSW's equity share (~Rs.4,000-5,000 crores per Rs.25,000-30,000 crore project). For BPSL itself, the filings say the business has 'significant growth potential' and the JV will accelerate capacity with 'best-in-class technology' and high-end value-added products, and the Netrabanda 2 mt iron ore mine now sits inside the JV. The accounting consequences were spelled out: a Q4 FY26 exceptional gain of Rs.18,051 crores on the slump sale (within Rs.17,888 crores of net exceptionals), BPSL assets classified held for sale under Ind AS 105 from Dec-2025, a Rs.1,439 crore deferred tax asset recognised because BPSL's carried-forward unabsorbed depreciation would offset the capital gain (so 'the effective tax on this transaction is significantly lower'), deconsolidation at March-end with BPSL now equity-accounted under income from associates and joint ventures, and FY27 guidance of 29.75 mt production / 28.6 mt sales explicitly excluding JFE JV volumes. In parallel, Piombino Steel Limited — BPSL's parent, 82.65% JSW Steel and 17.35% promoter-group JSW Shipping & Logistics — was amalgamated into JSW Steel (10 JSW shares per 156 PSL shares) precisely so JSW could hold BPSL directly and transact on it 'without minority shareholders' involvement', while gaining 'additional cash to pursue its growth aspirations in a financially prudent manner'. No lender or investor demand is cited anywhere; the pressure visible in the texts is analysts probing the logic (Amit Murarka on running three balance sheets, Sumangal Nevatia asking why a second partner at all given the post-JFE balance sheet), while CCI cleared it on 20 January 2026 and shareholders approved the Piombino merger with 94.86% of votes cast (97.20% of public shareholders).
rationale.evolution: The simplification began on 17 October 2025, when the Board approved folding wholly owned subsidiaries Amba River Coke, Monnet Cement and JSW Retail & Distribution into JSW Steel (effective 1 August 2026) purely for group-structure and compliance reasons. The separation proper was announced on 3 December 2025: the Board approved the JFE 50:50 JV, the slump sale of BPSL's steel undertaking to JSW Sambalpur for Rs.24,483 crores, and simultaneously the merger of Piombino Steel into JSW Steel to hold BPSL directly without the 17.35% promoter-group minority; definitive JV, business-transfer and share-subscription agreements were signed the same day. Execution then ran to schedule — CCI approval 20 January 2026; the Q3 FY26 results on 23 January 2026 reclassified BPSL as held for sale, quantified equity value Rs.31,500 crores / EV Rs.53,000 crores, Rs.32,000 crores cash inflow and Rs.37,000 crores deleveraging, and booked a Rs.1,439 crore deferred tax asset; the slump sale completed 27 March 2026; and the 14 May 2026 call reported the JV entity formed by end-March, JFE's first tranche in, BPSL deconsolidated, Rs.18,051 crores of exceptional gain, leverage at 1.81x and tightened leverage caps. The ambition then widened rather than narrowed: a second 50:50 JV with POSCO was signed in April 2026 for a greenfield 6 MTPA plant in Odisha (via Saffron Resources, Rs.508.8 crore subscription), the India target was raised to 62 mt by FY32 plus 16 mt in JVs, and the Piombino merger was sanctioned by NCLT on 16 October 2026 and became effective 31 October 2026 (appointed date 1 January 2026) — alongside a separate partial monetisation, the 17 July 2026 approval to sell up to Rs.811 crores of JSW One Platforms shares in its IPO.

points.point: The 3 December 2025 Board filing set out the structure: BPSL's steel undertaking sold by slump sale to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited for Rs.24,483 crores cash, with JFE then buying 50% of parent JSW Kalinga for Rs.15,750 crores in two equal tranches.
points.quote: Transfer of BPSL Steel business undertaking, by way of slump sale on a going concern basis to JSW Sambalpur Steel Limited ("JSW Sambalpur") for a cash consideration of Rs 24,483 crores, subject to customary closing adjustments as agreed in the transaction documents.

points.point: The stated purpose was to fund JSW's 50 MTPA-by-FY31 ambition without balance-sheet strain, not to exit the asset.
points.quote: The present transaction is aimed at securing the Company's growth in a financially prudent manner to enable it to pursue its aspirations across business cycles.

points.point: For BPSL itself, management said the JV brings JFE's technology to accelerate capacity and move the product mix up-market; JFE has been a partner since 2009.
points.quote: The BPSL Steel business has significant growth potential and this joint venture will enable acceleration of its capacity with best-in-class technology and enable production of high-end value-added steel products

points.point: The Q3 FY26 press release put hard numbers on the valuation and the balance-sheet effect: Rs.31,500 crores equity value, Rs.53,000 crores EV, Rs.32,000 crores cash in and Rs.37,000 crores of deleveraging.
points.quote: With this transaction, JFE will take a 50% stake in the BPSL Steel business at an equity value of ₹31,500 crores and enterprise value of ₹53,000 crores.

points.point: The simultaneous Piombino Steel merger was justified as letting JSW Steel hold BPSL directly and transact on it without the 17.35% promoter-group minority, while releasing cash.
points.quote: The merger ensures better alignment of the Transferee Company's long-term strategic interests by enabling it to directly hold the investment in Bhushan Power and Steel Limited ('BPSL'). This consolidation provides a platform to facilitate any transactions and investments related to BPSL's business, thereby enhancing strategic focus without minority shareholders' involvement;

points.point: The company deliberately did not treat the carve-out as a discontinued operation — BPSL was never framed as a different line of business, only as capital released from the same business.
points.quote: The Group has also assessed and concluded that transfer of BPSL's steel business undertaking does not qualify as "discontinued operation" as it is not a separate major line of business and forms part of overall steel operations of the Group.

points.point: BPSL's accumulated tax losses were monetised against the sale gain: a Rs.1,439 crore deferred tax asset was recognised in Q3 FY26 on the strength of the expected capital gain.
points.quote: Further, based on the reassessment of unrecognised deferred tax assets, the Group has recognised deferred tax assets (net) amounting to Rs. 1,439 crores as it is probable that carried forward unabsorbed depreciation will be recovered against the likely capital gains on the above mentioned transaction.

points.point: Acharya opened with the deleveraging as the headline benefit, ~Rs.37,000 crores in total with ~Rs.30,000 crores already done by March-end.
points.quote: This transaction entails a deleveraging of approximately Rs.37,000 crores for JSW Steel, out of which about Rs.30,000 crores has been completed at March end.

points.point: Post-deal leverage fell to 1.81x with net debt ~Rs.54,000 crores and gearing 0.51x, and the rating outlook improved — versus net debt of Rs.80,347 crores and 2.91x at 31 December 2025.
points.quote: Our credit rating outlook has seen an uplift, and we expect to see continued progress on this front.

points.point: Asked directly by Amit Murarka (Axis Capital) whether multiple simultaneous projects across three balance sheets is the new normal, Acharya confirmed the separation was designed to do two things at once.
points.quote: So, as we had given you an indication earlier that the idea of the JV was to strategically grow faster in the country, while it helped us to deleverage as well.

points.point: He described the resulting architecture as two growth vehicles running in parallel, with JSW Steel tracked to 62 mt by FY32 and the JVs (JFE 10 mt, POSCO 6 mt) tracked separately.
points.quote: So, we'll have a double engine of growth, one which JSW Steel will grow on and the other which the joint venture will grow on.

points.point: The sale produced a Rs.18,051 crore book gain inside Q4 FY26 exceptionals of Rs.17,888 crores, lifting reported PAT to Rs.19,243 crores against normalised PAT of Rs.3,475 crores.
points.quote: This includes a gain of Rs.18,051 crores on slump sale of BPSL steel undertaking and Rs.163 crores exceptional charge on implementation of new labor code.

points.point: Asked by Indrajit Agarwal (CLSA) about tax leakage, CFO Swayam Saurabh said BPSL's losses sheltered the gain, and confirmed the shelter applied on JSW's own books.
points.quote: So BPSL has had carry forward losses, unabsorbed depreciation. So, the effective tax on this transaction is significantly lower.

points.point: Ashwin Bajaj used closing remarks to clarify the P&L mechanics after fielding investor queries: BPSL's earnings now appear only as a one-line equity pick-up, and FY27 guidance of 29.75 mt production / 28.6 mt sales excludes JV volumes.
points.quote: BPSL has been deconsolidated at March-end. And the numbers for BPSL will not be part of financials of EBITDA. It would be equity accounting, and there is a line in the P&L, which says income from associates and joint ventures.

points.point: Confidence from the carve-out let the Board tighten its own leverage ceilings, with Saurabh telling Nomura they would track ratios rather than an absolute debt number.
points.quote: We have also revised our stated maximum cap for gearing from 1.75x to 1.25x and leverage from 3.75x to 3.00x. However, our comfort level will be to keep the leverage below 2.5x.

points.point: The remaining deleveraging was tied to JFE's second equity tranche, due by end-June 2026.
points.quote: The second tranche of equity investment in JFE is expected by end-June, which will drive further deleveraging of Rs.7,900 crores approximately.

points.point: Sumangal Nevatia (Kotak) pushed on why a second partner (POSCO) was needed given the balance sheet was already repaired after JFE; Acharya cited technology access and POSCO's own need to backward-integrate its 2 mt Maharashtra cold-rolling plant.
points.quote: POSCO also has their own areas of technology and especially in the high-strength steels, giga steels, which would go for lightweighting, replacement of aluminum, hydrogen technology to reduce emissions, digitalisation and AI.

points.point: Capital commitment to the JVs is limited to JSW's equity slice, which is how the separation makes the enlarged capex plan affordable.
points.quote: The JV investment will only be in form of equity.

points.point: Shareholders ratified the Piombino leg overwhelmingly at the NCLT-convened meeting of 21 August 2026, and NCLT found no objector; the scheme took effect 31 October 2026.
points.quote: The Scheme was approved by 2,032 equity shareholders holding 2,14,82,88,337 equity shares, representing 94.86% of the valid votes cast by the Company's equity shareholders.

rationale.what_management_expects: For JSW Steel: Rs.37,000 crore deleveraging, leverage 1.81x, net debt Rs.54,000 crores, rating-outlook uplift, tighter caps (gearing 1.25x, leverage 3.00x), and cash to fund 62 mt by FY32 plus JV equity. For the BPSL JV: accelerated expansion toward ~10 mt using JFE technology and high-end value-added grades; now equity-accounted, so its EBITDA leaves JSW's P&L.
rationale.gaps: Nine of ten call transcripts are unreadable. Nothing explains why 50% rather than less, JV exit/control terms, BPSL's standalone margins or returns post-deal, or who initiated.

segments.segment_name: BPSL (Bhushan Power & Steel Limited) — reported as a separate entity line in "Financials – BPSL and JVML-Vijayanagar"
segments.measure_notes: Operating profit line is 'Adjusted EBITDA', which the presentations define as EBITDA excluding unrealised FX gains/losses on long-term borrowings net of unrealised FX gains/losses on intercompany receivables (not EBIT/PBT). PAT is 'Profit/(Loss) after Tax' and for FY26 is dominated by a large exceptional gain (consolidated FY26 exceptional items +₹17,359 crore; BPSL Q4 FY26 PAT ₹12,244 crore). Revenue is 'Revenue from Operations' of the BPSL entity as presented by JSW Steel, i.e. entity-level revenue before elimination of intra-group transactions — not an external-only segment revenue. JSW Steel's annual report segment notes (AR2024 p.297, AR2025 p.317, AR2026 p.326) disclose a single reportable steel segment with only geographic splits, so they carry no BPSL-specific figures. BPSL steel business was de-consolidated with effect from 27 March 2026, so no BPSL line appears in the Q1/Q2 FY27 presentations.

judge.what_is_spun: The Data Centre and Cloud Services business of ARL and ARCPL, vested in Ashok Cloud Private Limited
judge.reason: Consolidate the entire Data Centre Business in one entity and create two dedicated listed companies, enabling independent market recognition and valuation, dedicated management focus and sector-specific funding.
judge.insiders: ARL promoters hold 57.42% of ARL; post-scheme ACPL is 28.14% promoters directly plus 51% held by ARL (79.14% total), public 20.86%. Promoter-group Anish Sarin oversees data-centre rollout.
judge.hidden_value: Demerged Undertaking turnover Rs 145.90 cr is only 8.96% of Rs 1,627.72 cr; management cites ~75% data-centre EBITDA margin, 357 MW planned capacity, Rs 20,000 cr capex, net-cash parent with Rs 4,471.64 cr net worth.
judge.selling_pressure_why: Small (8.96% of turnover), only 20.86% public float in ACPL, and a digital-infrastructure business alien to real-estate holders.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — the July 21, 2026 filings say only that ACPL's demerger shares and ARL's existing ACPL shares "shall be listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited by seeking exemption under Rule 19(7)", subject to NCLT, SEBI, exchange, shareholder and creditor approvals; no date given
judge.read_next: The full Composite Scheme: asset/liability split and valuation of the Demerged Undertaking versus ACPL's Rs 74.86 cr rights issue.
judge.quote: The Data Centre Business has evolved significantly over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity focused on the rapidly growing Data Centre Business whilst continuing to leverage ARL's institutional strengths, strong brand equity and goodwill.

listing.text: NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; no listing timeline stated

rationale.rationale: Management says Anant Raj Ltd today runs two unlike businesses under one roof — the legacy real estate/infrastructure business (residential townships, luxury housing, commercial leasing, hospitality) and a data centre & cloud services business — and that the Data Centre Business is itself split across two entities, Anant Raj Limited and its wholly owned Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed in both. The Composite Scheme therefore first amalgamates ARCPL into ARL and then demerges the whole Data Centre Business out of ARL into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so all of it sits in one dedicated, separately listed company. The stated problems it solves: the two verticals differ 'significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements', and the Board recorded on May 11, 2026 that keeping both in one company 'does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns'; the split is meant to give independent market-driven valuation of a pure-play digital infrastructure asset, dedicated management focus, a simpler ownership structure with intra-group arrangements cancelled/rationalised, and the ability to attract sector-specific capital, strategic investors and partnerships. The numbers cited: the Demerged Undertaking did ₹145.90 cr turnover in FY26 versus ₹1,627.72 cr aggregated (8.96%); ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 cr and net worth ₹49.45 cr versus ARL's ₹1,491.52 cr turnover and ₹4,471.64 cr net worth; ACPL had nil turnover and ₹0.04 cr net worth and was capitalised days earlier via a ₹74.86 cr rights issue (37,43,22,553 shares at ₹2). Scale is the driver: the Board noted an MOU with the Govt. of Andhra Pradesh for 50 MW IT load taking total planned capacity to 357 MW IT load, requiring about ₹20,000 cr of investment — against a real estate business management repeatedly said should carry as little debt as possible. Mechanically, ARL shareholders get 1 ACPL share of ₹2 for every 1 ARL share of ₹2, giving them 49% of ACPL directly (promoters 28.14%, public 20.86%) while ARL retains 51%, so ACPL stays a subsidiary and ARL holders keep 100% of the ultimate economic interest; ACPL will be listed on BSE and NSE under the Rule 19(7) exemption. The ask came from the equity market side — an investor asked about a demerger as early as the Apr 2024 call, and analysts kept pressing for separate real estate vs data centre reporting — not from lenders or partners, who are never cited as requesting it.
rationale.evolution: On the Apr 25, 2024 call Arpit Shah of Stallion Asset asked outright whether there were plans to demerge the business and Amit Sarin refused — 'too soon', focus on execution — while describing the cloud venture as a half-megawatt pilot with TCIL. By the Oct 30, 2024 call (Q2 FY25) management was framing the group as 'two full-fledged divisions' (real estate plus a technology division) with a ₹2,100 cr fundraise earmarked purely for data centre/cloud, and Raj Sarraf pushed for separate data centre revenue disclosure; on the Nov 12, 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26) the CFO called the company 'at an important inflection point' with a 'legacy real estate business' alongside the data centre/cloud 'future ready platform', the ₹1,100 cr QIP was done, and analysts again asked for a separate segment/EBITDA breakup, which management declined on the 10%-of-revenue threshold. The demerger itself was never discussed on any of the three calls: it surfaced in the May 11, 2026 board note (which recorded the need for merger/demerger and set up a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta to frame a scheme), then was executed as the ACPL rights-issue funding on July 20, 2026 and the Composite Scheme approved on July 21, 2026.

points.point: An investor (Arpit Shah, Stallion Asset) directly asked about demerging the data centre business; management declined to engage, calling the business too young and prioritising execution toward the 300 MW mark in four years.
points.quote: We are too soon to say anything on that. Let's focus on execution, Arpit.

points.point: Management set out the different capital philosophies that later justify separation: real estate was to be net debt-free by December 2024 and the only debt acceptable would be lease rental discounting, including against long 10-15 year data centre leases.
points.quote: And the only debt which Anant Raj is open to taking is LRD and this is one of the best items for LRD because you have long-term leases and good clients.

points.point: Management began describing the group as two separate divisions — the historic real estate 'bread and butter' and a new technology division of colocation and cloud — the same two-vertical framing the Scheme later uses.
points.quote: So Anant Raj Limited will now have two full-fledged divisions. Real estate division which is the historical, the division of the company, the bread and butter of the company as of now and plus the technology division, in which we will be data center, co-location infrastructure and cloud.

points.point: The ₹2,100 cr fundraise (₹100 cr promoters, ₹2,000 cr market) was ring-fenced entirely for the data centre/cloud build-out, with real estate funded from internal accruals — distinct funding requirements per vertical, with cloud capex cited at ~₹100 cr per MW on top of ₹26 cr colocation capex.
points.quote: This is purely data center, sir. This fund is going to be purely for data centers. For our real estate, we are completely funded with our internal sources.

points.point: An analyst (Raj Sarraf of Finvestors) asked for data centre revenue to be reported separately from real estate because it would become the major contributor; management conceded the point.
points.quote: Sir, both the revenues are going to be substantial and we will be breaking them up, sir . We will do that definitely.

points.point: The CFO positioned the company at an 'inflection point' with a legacy real estate business and a separate future-ready data centre/cloud platform — H1 FY26 revenue ₹1,223.2 cr of which data centre only ₹58.42 cr, ₹1,100 cr QIP completed, net cash positive, ~₹700 cr capital employed in data centres at 75% EBITDA margin.
points.quote: Our legacy real estate business continues to deliver a consistent growth and strengthen our leadership in high demanding markets. At the same time, our Data Center and Cloud initiatives are shaping up the future ready platform that positions us as a diversified resilient enterprise s.

points.point: Investors (Sri Gopal of StockHifi, Ashwani Sharma of Emkay) again pressed for separate real estate vs data centre revenue and EBITDA reporting; management said formal segment disclosure was not yet triggered because data centre revenue was under 10% of the total.
points.quote: In this, you have to give segmental breakup once you do 10%.

points.point: Asked whether the company should lever up to scale data centres faster, management refused on the grounds that real estate is the backbone and must stay low-debt — a tension a separately funded data centre entity resolves. Capacity plans were 63 MW by Dec 2026, 117 MW by FY28 and 307 MW by FY31-32.
points.quote: And as it is, we feel that our backbone is still real estate, which will always be. And we feel that real estate should be as low on debt as possible.

points.point: The May 11, 2026 board note first records the need for a merger/demerger, citing differing nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics and capital requirements, plus the 357 MW IT load plan (after the 50 MW Andhra Pradesh MOU) needing about ₹20,000 cr; a committee of Amit Sarin, Ashim Sarin, Manoj Goyal and Pankaj Gupta was formed to design it.
points.quote: The Board of Directors have considered that the Company is presently engaged in two distinct business undertakings, namely Real Estate Development and Data Center Services, which differ significantly in their nature, risk profile, competitive dynamics, and capital requirements and continuing both businesses under a single corporate does not adequately reflect the true potential and intrinsic value of each business segment, thereby impacting stakeholder returns.

points.point: The July 21, 2026 Scheme explains the data centre business is split across ARL and ARCPL, so ARCPL is first merged into ARL and the combined Data Centre Business then demerged into Ashok Cloud — consolidating it in one entity and creating two focused listed companies.
points.quote: The Data Centre Business is presently conducted through ARL and ARCPL, with various assets, employees, investments and business operations pertaining to the Data Centre Business being housed across both entities.

points.point: Stated benefit one: independent market recognition and valuation of the data centre business given its distinct operating profile, growth trajectory, risk-return characteristics and funding needs; demerged undertaking turnover was ₹145.90 cr, 8.96% of ₹1,627.72 cr for FY26.

rationale.rationale: No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the reasoning below is reconstructed only from the filings. The separation is the demerger of Valor Estate Ltd's (formerly D B Realty Ltd) hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited (formerly Shiva Realtors Suburban Private Limited) under a Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement that also amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor; the Explanatory Statement to the 12th December 2025 EGM says the Scheme was entered into 'mainly with aim to demerge hospitality business of the Company into Resulting Company and thus unlock overall value for the shareholders.' NCLT Mumbai sanctioned it on 12 June 2025, it became effective 1 July 2025 (demerger appointed date 1 April 2025; Esteem amalgamation appointed date 1 April 2024), and shareholders on the 18 July 2025 record date received 1 AHIL share of Rs. 10 for every 10 Valor shares. The carve-out moved consolidated net assets of Rs. 1,02,194.65 lakhs (standalone Rs. 1,01,512.91 lakhs) out of Valor — Rs. 1,49,386.00 lakhs of property, plant and equipment, Rs. 54,858.00 lakhs of goodwill, Rs. 29,117.12 lakhs of intangibles, against Rs. 46,196.17 lakhs non-current and Rs. 16,028.03 lakhs current borrowings, Rs. 2,01,956.25 lakhs of other non-current financial liabilities and Rs. 28,951.71 lakhs of deferred tax liability — and took out a business that had FY25 revenue of Rs. 36,650.21 lakhs and PAT of Rs. 4,468.06 lakhs, now shown as discontinued operations. Management's stated problems solved are focus and structure: Valor 'is now engaged solely in the real estate business, which constitutes its only reportable segment,' so segment reporting ceased, while Advent gets 'its own Board and Management team,' NSE/BSE listing on 13 November 2025 for 'enhanced market visibility, liquidity for existing shareholders, and a strengthened capital structure,' and an asset-heavy growth path (five projects, 3,100 keys, EBITDA from under Rs. 200 crore to over Rs. 1,200 crore by FY32, targeted mid-teens compounded ROE) that a combined entity would have had to fund alongside real estate. The second, smaller separation/consolidation strand is non-core cleanup: Sahyadri Agro and Dairy Private Limited (dairy farming, milk procurement and trading), taken to 76.63% via enforcement of security and then to 100% 'as the transaction relates to the liquidation of non-core assets,' sold its entire dairy business under a Business Transfer Agreement at a gain of Rs. 6,901.20 lakhs with Rs. 1,697.63 lakhs of non-compete fees booked as an exceptional item, is now 'evaluating opportunities to engage in the business of real estate development,' and was amalgamated into Horizontal Ventures Private Limited for structural simplification, synergies, avoidance of duplication and lower compliance and overhead costs. Running alongside is balance-sheet repair the filings tie to the same strategy: consolidated secured debt down to Rs. 730 crore, full redemption of Rs. 235 crore of NCDs out of the Rs. 262 crore Dahisar/Aradhya Park development-rights conveyance, and the Scheme-driven reduction and consolidation of the 8% RPS (Clause 32: Rs. 10 face value cut to Rs. 9, then 10 consolidated into 9) plus Clause 20's 1:10 allotment of AHIL preference shares, followed by the November 2025 proposal to convert KRPL's 6,45,75,000 RPS into 0.0001% CCPS converting into 32,02,330 equity shares at Rs. 201.65 'with a view to conserve the financial resources of the Company.' No filing names any investor, lender or partner as having demanded the separation; the only named partner is Prestige Group, which sits on Advent's side as a 50:50 JV partner in the Sahar project and co-developer at Aerocity.
rationale.evolution: There are no transcripts on file, so the idea cannot be traced call by call; the paper trail runs through filings and the Scheme itself. The Composite Scheme was sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 12 June 2025, became effective 1 July 2025 with demerger appointed date 1 April 2025, and the 1:10 entitlement was fixed on the 18 July 2025 record date; the SADPL-into-HVPL amalgamation was approved by both boards on 18 August 2025 with appointed date 1 April 2025. The plan then became visible in public filings in quick succession: Advent's listing press release (12 November 2025), Valor's Q2FY26 results and press release (14-15 November 2025) which first framed the demerger as completed and as the basis for debt reduction, the EGM notice and corrigendum (20 November and 8 December 2025) which disclosed the Scheme's preference-share reduction, consolidation and 1:10 AHIL allotment and layered the RPS-to-CCPS conversion on top, and finally the NCLT order of 29 January 2026 and effective date of 12 March 2026 completing the SADPL consolidation. The shape of the plan therefore widened over time from a single hospitality demerger into a package: demerger plus listing, plus non-core dairy liquidation and merger, plus capital-structure conversion.

points.point: The Composite Scheme's stated purpose, as put to shareholders in the EGM explanatory statement, was to demerge the hospitality business into Advent Hotels International Limited and unlock shareholder value; it simultaneously amalgamated Esteem Properties Private Limited into Valor.

rationale.rationale: These texts contain no separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme of arrangement for HDFC Bank, and management never explains one; the question's premise is not supported by the documents supplied. The only business that was partly separated from the Bank is HDB Financial Services Limited (HDBFS), the group's non-deposit-taking NBFC, and that was done by listing it rather than by demerging it: a June 25, 2025 IPO comprising a fresh issue of Rs 2,500.00 crore plus an offer for sale of Rs 10,000.00 crore of the Bank's shares (13,51,35,135 shares of Rs 10 each at Rs 740 per share), after which the Bank still held 74.1%. Management gave no reason for the listing at all — no regulatory mandate, no capital need, no valuation argument, no investor or lender demand was cited; Sashidhar Jagdishan only reported that 'we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake' and thanked IPO investors. The only strategic point made about HDBFS was in answer to Pranav Gundlapalle (Jul 2025), who asked about customer conflict between the two entities: management said HDBFS serves a segment 'a notch or two below' the Bank, with 'zero or very minimal overlap' expected to persist, i.e. the two are kept distinct by customer segment and pricing, not separated to fix a problem. Financially the event was treated as a one-off gain — Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone and Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated (before tax, net of IPO expenses) — which Srinivasan Vaidyanathan later flagged (Jul 2026) as a base-effect distortion making reported PAT growth 5% versus 9.8% adjusted. Every other corporate action in these texts runs the other way: deepening the 2023 HDFC Limited merger (Apr 2026: e-HDFC home-loan customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA balances up from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 98% of new home loans opening a liability account, 23% carrying active Bank credit cards) and the Apr 16, 2026 board approval to invest up to Rs 1,000 crore in HDFC Life's preferential issue. The closest thing to a forward-looking separation hint is Jagdishan's unprompted remark on surplus capital (Oct 2025): if options arise 'to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so' — unspecified, with no business named.
rationale.evolution: Jul 19, 2025: the HDB Financial Services IPO and the Bank's stake dilution are reported as completed (listed Jul 2, 2025), with no rationale, and management answers only the question of bank-versus-HDBFS customer overlap. Oct 18, 2025: asked by Chintan (Autonomous) what the Bank will do with excess CET1, Jagdishan leaves the door open to unnamed 'other options... to delight shareholders' while stressing capital will be consumed once growth accelerates from FY27. Jan 17, 2026 filings quantify the transaction (Rs 10,000 crore OFS, Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain, 74.1% residual stake); Apr 16, 2026 the Board instead commits up to Rs 1,000 crore of fresh capital to subsidiary HDFC Life. Jul 18, 2026: the HDB gain is referred to only retrospectively, as a prior-year one-timer depressing headline PAT growth to 5% versus 9.8% adjusted — the idea never develops into any separation plan.

points.point: The only partial separation disclosed in any call: HDBFS was listed and the Bank sold down part of its holding, reported as a completed process with no stated rationale.
points.quote: During the quarter, we carried out the HDB Financial Services listing process, wherein the bank also diluted some stake, and which eventually culminated in the stocks being listed on 2nd of July.

points.point: Asked by Pranav Gundlapalle (Bernstein) whether the Bank and HDBFS would end up chasing the same customers, Jagdishan said HDBFS sits a notch or two below the Bank's segment on customer profile and pricing.
points.quote: HDB, we have maintained this. I think the segment that they cater to is about a notch or two below that of HDFC Bank.

points.point: Management framed the two entities as permanently distinct by segmentation rather than as a business being carved out to solve a conflict.
points.quote: There is zero or very minimal overlap at this juncture that will continue to stay for a long period of time.

points.point: On the capital question (CET1 near 20%, draft RWA relief, ECL), Jagdishan said capital will be consumed once FY27 growth exceeds system growth, but left unnamed shareholder-friendly options open — the only forward-looking hint of any corporate action.
points.quote: Having said that, if there are any opportunities that may arise in terms of other options that are available to sort of delight shareholders, we would be more than happy to do so.

points.point: The Jan 17, 2026 filing quantifies the HDBFS sell-down: fresh issue of Rs 2,500 crore plus Rs 10,000 crore offer for sale by the Bank, 13,51,35,135 shares at Rs 740, producing a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone gain (Rs 7,000.27 crore consolidated) with the Bank retaining 74.1%.
points.quote: On June 25, 2025, the Bank's subsidiary company, HDB Financial Services Limited ("HDBFS") launched its initial public offering ("IPO"), comprised of a fresh issuance of equity shares aggregating to 2,500.00 crore and an offer for sale ("OFS") of equity shares by the Bank, aggregating to 10,000.00 crore.

points.point: Six weeks before the Apr 2026 call the Board moved in the opposite direction, approving fresh capital into a subsidiary rather than any separation, subject to RBI approval.
points.quote: the Board of Directors of the Bank, at its meeting held today i.e. on April 16, 2026, approved investment of an amount not exceeding Rs. 1,000 crore (Rupees One thousand crore only) in the preferential issue of equity shares to be made by HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited, a subsidiary of the Bank

points.point: Kaizad Bharucha's merger-synergy update shows integration, not separation: e-HDFC mortgage customers' liability penetration up from 36% to ~50%, their CASA from about Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 86,000 crore, 60-65% paying EMIs from in-house accounts, 23% holding active Bank credit cards.
points.quote: Net of attritions, net of acquisitions over this journey, this 36% has come as high as 50% within the last 2.5 years.

points.point: The HDBFS transaction appears only as a prior-year one-timer distorting the growth base, with adjusted PAT growth of 9.8% versus 5% reported — the last mention of it in any call.
points.quote: But last year included certain one-timers like HDB gains and then we had a floating provision counter-cyclical buffer that we added and some contingent provision and so on.

points.point: At the special call on Atanu Chakraborty's resignation, the only structural change hinted at was an internal reorganisation of responsibilities, explicitly not a business separation and with nothing decided.
points.quote: Yes, as I said, as we move forward, we will sort of re-examine our organization structure and with the consent and the advice of the board, we will announce it at the appropriate time.

rationale.what_management_expects: Nothing was said about a separation, because none was announced. For the one partial carve-out, the HDBFS listing, management claimed no margin, capital, valuation or focus benefit; it cited only a Rs 9,179.40 crore standalone one-time gain (later called a base-effect distortion) and segment distinctness — HDBFS one to two notches below the Bank, with minimal customer overlap.
rationale.gaps: Everything: no separation, demerger or scheme exists here. No reason, regulator, lender or investor demand, valuation case, timeline or margin/capital effect for the HDBFS listing is given.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Linjemontage i Grästorp AB (LMG), KPIL's Swedish power-grid EPC subsidiary held through Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB (KPTS) — separated not by demerger but by an offer-for-sale IPO on Nasdaq Stockholm (listed 25 September 2026), in which KPTS sold down from 96.12% to 66.45% rather than giving LMG new capital. The trigger management cited on the calls was value crystallisation and cash: LMG had compounded from ~INR1,000 crores revenue in FY24 to INR1,800+ crores in FY25 (PBT INR21 crores to INR70+ crores) to ~INR3,000 crores in FY26 with EBITDA ~INR200 crores and PBT ~INR170 crores (both up over 100%), i.e. SEK1.3bn to SEK3.2bn net sales at a 56.6% CAGR with adjusted EBITA margin rising from 4.4% to 7.6%, net cash of SEK172.1m, ROCE of 48.1% and an order book of SEK4,349m — yet it was only ~11.14% of KPIL's consolidated revenue and ~4.5% of consolidated net worth. Mohnot repeatedly placed the Sweden 'fundraise' inside the same bucket as the noncore exits (Vindhyachal road asset sold January 2026 for ~INR799 crores EV / INR600+ crores net, Indore real estate, Shree Shubham Logistics), i.e. as a source of 'further cash flows' to cut leverage and fund the INR800-900 crores/year capex programme and lift ROCE; the IPO delivered KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at SEK46/share, valuing LMG at SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores). The second problem it solves is that LMG's economics are structurally different from KPIL's: management argued a 6%-7% PBT in a 'mature market' is fine there because 'the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always' — a profile the consolidated KPIL multiple was not reflecting. LMG's own filings justify the separation on strategic grounds: visibility, credibility and brand recognition with customers, partners and employees, transparency, a platform for long-term value creation, a broadened shareholder base, and support for its ambition to lead Nordic power-infrastructure EPC in a Swedish serviceable market growing from ~SEK19bn (2025) to ~SEK31bn (2030) at 11% CAGR (transmission 17%), with ~80% of Sweden's transmission grid over 40 years old and Statnett planning NOK150-200bn of 2025-2034 investment. Pressure came from investors and analysts, not lenders: Carnelian and DAM Capital pushed management on why a T&D business sitting inside a T&D company needed its own listing, while cornerstone demand from Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen (SEK290m) anchored the book; LMG's management/employee shareholders (991,950 shares) sold mainly to repay the financing they had used to buy their shares. KPIL stressed continuity, not exit: KPTS 'indicated an intention to remain a long-term major shareholder', is locked up for 360 days, and LMG remains a step-down subsidiary.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced on the 19 May 2025 Q4 FY25 call, where Mohnot disclosed that the Board had approved appointing bankers and intermediaries to examine 'fundraising options' at Linjemontage — framed alongside the noncore clean-up (VEPL, Indore, Shubham); the 14 Feb 2025 call had contained no such plan, only LMG's record order book of INR3,143 crores. By 8 August 2025 (Q1 FY26) it had hardened into a disclosed 'strategic overview… including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions', and management refused to explain the logic when Carnelian asked why a T&D business inside a T&D company needed a separate listing, even withdrawing LMG margin guidance because the process had started. On 31 October 2025 Mohnot said the path was still undecided but expected 'some light' on valuation in FY26-27, and on 5 February 2026 he said the Sweden mandate was 'progressing well' and should throw off cash in FY26-27; by 15 May 2026 he described it only as 'some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes'. The form was fixed in the filings: KPTS board approval on 9 September 2026, prospectus and SEK46 price on 16 September, listing and ~32.1% offer on 25 September, and partial greenshoe exercise on 23-24 October 2026 leaving KPIL at 66.45%.

points.point: Baseline: no separation plan existed; LMG was simply presented as a record performer, with revenue doubling and an all-time-high order book of INR3,143 crores.
points.quote: LMG's order book is at a all time high of INR3,143 crores.

points.point: First disclosure of the separation idea — the Board approved bankers and intermediaries to study fundraising options at Linjemontage, mentioned in the same breath as LMG's PBT rising from ~INR21 crores to ~INR70+ crores.
points.quote: the Board has also approved appointment of bankers as well as intermediaries to look at fund options, fundraising options in Sweden Linjemontage in the last Board meeting, which we have declared to everyone.

points.point: Formalised as a disclosed 'strategic overview' with an IPO explicitly named as one of the options, and merchant bankers and advisers appointed; LMG had already begun preparatory steps.
points.quote: We have initiated a strategic overview on LMG where various options are being evaluated, including options related to IPO, subject to market conditions.

points.point: An investor (Mihir Manohar, Carnelian Capital) pressed on exactly the question management never answered — why carve out a T&D business that already sits inside a T&D company; Mohnot declined to comment.
points.quote: I just wanted to understand the thought process because I mean, it is also T&D business similarly sitting in KPIL.

points.point: Management explained LMG's different economic profile — lower PBT than KPIL's core but very high ROCE and permanently cash positive — the implicit valuation argument for separating it, with bankers still mandated and the path undecided.
points.quote: As far as margins are concerned, I think that those are mature markets where a PBT of 6% to 7% is very reasonably good because the ROCE numbers are very, very high and they are cash positive always.

points.point: The Sweden transaction was placed squarely in the monetisation/debt-reduction bucket alongside transmission assets, the last road asset and Shree Shubham Logistics, with cash expected in FY26-27.
points.quote: We do not know which options and what timing it exactly is, but we have appointed bankers to look at exploring fund option raising at Sweden also, which I'm expecting in FY26-27 should give us further cash flows.

points.point: Final pre-IPO framing: a 'strategic investment' into the Swedish subsidiary grouped with remaining divestments as free-cash-flow events to strengthen the balance sheet, set against INR800+ crores of annual capex and net debt already down 50% to INR915 crores.
points.quote: We also have some events of free cash flows coming in next year, whether it is through a few more divestments which are left, which might happen either next year or a year after that or whether it is through some strategic investment coming into our Swedish subsidiary in whatever form it comes.

points.point: The 9 September 2026 filing/press release gives the official rationale — standalone visibility, credibility, brand and Nordic leadership ambition — and discloses LMG's scale: SEK3,225m FY26 revenue (~11.14% of KPIL consolidated revenue) but only SEK334m net worth (~4.5% of KPIL's).
points.quote: The Listing is expected to enhance the Company's visibility, credibility and brand recognition among customers, partners and employees, and to support Linjemontage's long-term ambition to strengthen its position in the Nordics as one of the leading EPC providers within power infrastructure.

points.point: Transparency, long-term value creation and a diversified shareholder base are the stated second leg, with KPTS committing to stay a long-term major shareholder (360-day lock-up) and LMG remaining a step-down subsidiary.
points.quote: Becoming a publicly listed company will also provide greater transparency and a platform for long-term value creation, while diversifying the shareholder base.

points.point: Structurally this is a pure sell-down, not a capital raise for LMG: 14,311,620 base shares plus a 2,146,743-share greenshoe at SEK46, ~32.1% of LMG, giving KPTS gross proceeds of ~SEK711.45m at a SEK2,356.6m (~INR2,324 crores) valuation and taking KPTS from 96.12% to 66.45% after the partial greenshoe exercise of 1,877,911 shares.
points.quote: The Offering consists only of existing shares and the Company will therefore not receive any proceeds from the Offering.

points.point: Demand was investor-led: Tredje AP-fonden and Unionen cornerstoned SEK290m, while LMG's own management/director/employee holders sold 991,950 shares chiefly to repay the borrowings used to buy them.
points.quote: All individual Selling Shareholders other than Kalpataru Sweden are selling shares in the Offering primarily to repay financing arrangements relating to their respective acquisitions of shares in the Company.

points.point: LMG's standalone financial targets quantify what separation is meant to unlock — revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8% (from 7.6%), net debt/adj EBITDA below 1.0x and a 25% dividend payout — in a market growing 11% CAGR to SEK31bn by 2030.
points.quote: Profitability : Linjemontage aims to reach an adjusted EBITA margin exceeding 8 per cent in the medium term.

rationale.what_management_expects: For LMG: standalone visibility, credibility and brand with customers and employees; transparency; a growth platform and broadened shareholder base; revenue above SEK5bn, adjusted EBITA margin above 8%, net debt/EBITDA under 1.0x, 25% payout. For KPIL: ~SEK711m cash to cut debt and fund capex, value crystallised at SEK2.36bn, retained 66.45% control, higher ROCE and a cleaner noncore-free core EPC portfolio.
rationale.gaps: Calls never explained why a listing over a trade sale, the valuation sought, use of proceeds, dilution to consolidated EPS, or minority/governance terms; management explicitly refused to give the rationale.

rationale.rationale: Management's case, as set out in the 27 June 2026 board filing, press note and demerger presentation, is that Pricol had become two structurally different companies inside one shell: the Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business — instrument clusters (mechanical, electro-mechanical, LCD/TFT), integrated infotainment, e-cockpit, telematics, battery management systems and some sensors — versus the Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems (ACFMS) business and the polymer/precision business held in wholly owned Pricol Precision Products (P3L). DICVS was the bigger half, at INR 2,424.63 crore of FY26 revenue, or 61.17% of consolidated turnover (the press release rounds it to ~INR 2,400 crore and ~60%), against FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 3,963.85 crore and total income of INR 40,523.70 million. The problem they said this solves is divergence: the two now operate with "differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles" — DICVS innovation-led (display, electrification, connectivity, e-cockpit, ADAS, software-defined vehicles; risk = technology disruption and the semiconductor ecosystem; partners = display, chip-design and semiconductor firms; talent = embedded software, system architects, cyber-security and functional-safety experts) while ACFMS/P3L is scale-led (manufacturing excellence, cost competitiveness, lightweighting, exports; risk = automotive cyclicality and commodity costs; partners = Tier-2/3 suppliers). Capital deployment priorities were said to be incompatible in one entity: DICVS money goes to talent, software, global R&D centres, technology investments and overseas acquisitions, Pricol Limited's to manufacturing capacity, automation, productivity and domestic acquisitions. Other stated benefits: financial flexibility for each entity, reduced operational complexity and faster decision-making, independent and dedicated management teams, the ability to tailor processes, policies, systems and governance, improved visibility of each business's value and growth prospects, better ability to attract strategic and financial investors, and "appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount." Consideration is non-cash: 1 Pricol Autotech share of INR 1 for every 1 Pricol Limited share, so Autotech's register mirrors Pricol's (promoters 38.51%, public 61.49%), with listing sought on NSE and BSE; SSPA & Co. gave the share-entitlement report and Saffron Capital the fairness opinion. The 13 November 2026 filing revealed the commercial endpoint the June rationale did not mention: the promoters (Vijay, Vikram and Vanitha Mohan plus family and Pricol Holdings, Pricol Engineering Industries, Shrimay Enterprises and Pricol Logistics) will sell their entire 38.51% — 4,69,34,833 shares — of Pricol Autotech to Topaz Terrace Investments B.V., a Warburg Pincus affiliate, for up to INR 1,663.07 crore, followed by a mandatory open offer for up to a further 26%, after which Warburg controls Autotech and the family keeps ACFMS and polymer with no change in shareholding; no investor, lender or customer is named as having asked for any of this, and the only disclosed initiators are the board and the promoters, who used Veda Corporate Advisors as exclusive financial advisor.
rationale.evolution: The idea is entirely absent from the eleven earnings calls (Nov 2023 through the 15 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call), where management instead talked up a single integrated group — a FY31 INR 8,000 crore target, INR 680–700 crore of FY27 group capex across DICVS, ACFMS and polymer, and converting polymer "from a component maker to a value-added polymer player." The nearest hint is the 30 January 2026 (Feb 2026) call, where Siddharth Manoharan confirmed a newly incorporated subsidiary but attributed it to technology-partnership flexibility and the BOE MOU, saying the plan would be discussed "later"; Pricol Autotech Limited was in fact incorporated on 21 February 2026. The board then approved the scheme on 27 June 2026 — six weeks after a call that never raised it — and the purpose sharpened on 13 November 2026, when the promoters' entire 38.51% of the demerged entity was agreed for sale to Warburg Pincus for up to INR 1,663.07 crore plus a 26% open offer, converting a stated "focus and agility" restructuring into a control exit from the group's largest business.

points.point: The 27 June 2026 board filing frames the DICVS demerger as creating a simpler, faster entity matched to fast-changing technology, because the two halves already ran on different customer, competitive, capital and risk logic.
points.quote: The demerger of the DICVS Business is a strategic decision to create a simpler, sharper and more agile corporate entity, to meet the fast changing needs and technologies related to this business and its dynamic market realities.

points.point: The demerged undertaking is the majority of the company: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crore in FY26, 61.17% of consolidated turnover (press note: ~INR 2,400 crore, ~60%), against consolidated FY26 revenue from operations of INR 3,963.85 crore.
points.quote: The turnover of the DICVS Business for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, stood at INR 2,424.63 crores. This represents 61.17% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026.

points.point: Consideration is a mirror 1:1 share entitlement with no cash, so Pricol Autotech starts with promoters at 38.51% and public at 61.49%, and is to be listed on NSE and BSE; Pricol Limited receives nothing and retains no shares.
points.quote: 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of the Resulting Company having face value of INR 1 (Rupee One only) each for every 1 (One) fully paid-up equity share of INR 1 (Rupee One only) each of the Company.

points.point: The presentation makes valuation an explicit objective — separate frameworks for two structurally different businesses, removing the holding-company drag of one blended multiple.
points.quote: Clear market recognition and appropriate valuation benchmarks for each business, free from conglomerate discount

points.point: The side-by-side table splits the two on capital deployment (software, global R&D centres and overseas acquisitions for Autotech versus capacity, automation and domestic acquisitions for Pricol), talent, partners and risk (technology disruption versus automotive cyclicality and commodity costs).
points.quote: Talent, product development, software, global R&D centres, tech investments & overseas acquisitions

points.point: The 13 November 2026 share purchase agreement discloses the endpoint: Warburg Pincus affiliate Topaz Terrace Investments B.V. buys the promoters' entire 4,69,34,833 shares (38.51%) of Pricol Autotech for up to INR 1,663.07 crore, plus a mandatory open offer for up to 26% more.
points.quote: For completeness, the aggregate consideration payable for the sale by the Sellers of their entire stake of Pricol Autotech of 38.51% (to be issued to the Sellers pursuant to the Scheme) is up to INR 1,663.07 Crores (Indian Rupees One Thousand Six Hundred and Sixty Three Crores and Seven Lakhs) subject to the terms of the Share Purchase Agreement.

points.point: Control of the demerged business passes to Warburg and the Mohan family seeks reclassification out of Autotech's promoter group, while the agreement imposes non-compete obligations on the sellers and on Pricol Limited itself; ACFMS and polymer stay with the family with no shareholding change.
points.quote: Amongst other things, the Share Purchase Agreement contains customary stand still provisions, warranties and indemnities being provided by the Sellers, subject to customary limitations and caps, and certain non-compete obligations on the Sellers and the Company for a specified period.

points.point: Vikram Mohan ties the separation rationale directly to handing the business to Warburg, describing DICVS as having been "at the heart" of Pricol's five-decade journey and Warburg as its next owner-custodian.
points.quote: The proposed demerger will give Pricol Autotech the focus and independence to realise its full potential.

points.point: Asked on the 30 January 2026 call why a new subsidiary had been incorporated, Siddharth Manoharan attributed it to technology-partnership flexibility and the BOE MOU, not to any restructuring; Pricol Autotech Limited was incorporated on 21 February 2026.
points.quote: But whenever the plan materializes, we will talk about that in detail later.

points.point: Management's own segment guidance showed the margin and growth divergence later used as rationale — DICVS at INR 2,100–2,200 crore and 12.5–13% EBITDA, ACFMS at INR 600 crore growing 30–35%, polymer at INR 850–900 crore on 9.5% — though no separation was suggested.
points.quote: This year, the plastics, the Polymer business will be about INR 850 crores to INR 900 crores with a steady-state margin of 9.5%.

points.point: A year earlier Vikram Mohan had conceded that consolidating the lower-margin plastics business pulled the group's blended EBITDA down even as rupee profit rose — the conglomerate-mix problem the 2026 presentation addresses via separate valuation frameworks.
points.quote: Overall margin of Pricol will be maintained, but when Sundaram consolidates, it is going to come down lower because plastics is a single digit margin and not a double digit EBITDA product.

points.point: Six weeks before the board approved the scheme, the Q4 FY26 call described a unified group starting a fresh INR 680–700 crore capex cycle across all three divisions, with no hint of a demerger; Ganesh put DICVS at ~60%, ACFMS ~20% and P3L ~20% of revenue.
points.quote: In fact, this year, in itself, we have planned for about between INR 680 crore to INR 700 crores of CAPEX to cater to all of our new businesses that we have won, new plants, new machines, so on and so forth, which will keep propelling us forward and to maintain this growth momentum.

points.point: The same call disclosed the governance handover that preceded the restructuring: Vanitha Mohan stepped back from Pricol to chair Pricol Holdings and Vikram Mohan became Chairman and Managing Director — the signatory of both the June scheme and the November stake sale.
points.quote: Mrs. Vanita Mohan has stepped down as an active role from PRICOL, and I have taken over as the Chairman of the company.

rationale.what_management_expects: Pricol Autotech: a focused automotive-electronics platform — innovation-led growth, higher content per vehicle, global R&D, IP-led acquisitions, Warburg's capital and sector network. Pricol Limited: scale-led precision engineering — ACFMS exports, disc brakes, a polymer centre of excellence, domestic acquisitions. Both: dedicated management, tailored capital allocation, faster decisions, separate valuation benchmarks free of conglomerate discount, easier access to strategic and financial investors.
rationale.gaps: No call ever mentioned it. Filings omit stranded corporate costs, debt/asset and employee/IP allocation, tax, the INR 1,663.07 crore valuation basis, and why promoters exited DICVS.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG/consumer-brands arm, Reliance Consumer Products Ltd (RCPL) — Campa, Independence, Good Life, Ravalgaon/Toffeeman/Lotus, Velvette, Glimmer, Enzo, SIL, Maliban, Alan's, plus acquisitions Udhaiyam, Manna, Sosyo, Goodness Group and the Toni & Guy/Brylcreem/Badedas/Matey brands — which was carved out of Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL) under a composite scheme effective 1 December 2025: the 'Consumer Brands Business Undertaking' was demerged from RRVL into Tira Beauty Ltd (renamed RCPL), the old RCPL was dissolved, RRVL shareholders received 1 new RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares, and the new entity became an 83.56% direct subsidiary of RIL rather than a retail subsidiary. The only rationale management actually articulates is in the Chairman's 16 January 2026 statement: the consumer products vertical is 'progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure' — i.e. a dedicated, directly-held vehicle for a business scaling far faster than retail (Q3 FY26 Rs 5,000 crore, +60% Y-o-Y; 9M FY26 Rs 15,000 crore; FY26 Rs 22,000 crore, 2x Y-o-Y; Q4 FY26 Rs 7,350 crore; Q1 FY27 Rs 8,600 crore, 2x; Campa Rs 4,700 crore and India's 4th largest CSD brand; Independence Rs 2,600 crore; beverages over Rs 6,000 crore; 3rd largest packaged water player; 5,000+ distributors, 3 million outlets, 40 export markets; target Rs 1 lakh crore by FY2030). The problem it visibly solves, though never stated as the reason, is mixing an only-breakeven, capex-hungry FMCG build-out (12 plants, integrated food parks, Kurnool and 'one of the largest beverage plants in Asia', edible-oil facility in West Bengal) into Reliance Retail's P&L: on every call since, management has had to strip RCPL out to show the underlying retail trend — Q3 FY26 8.1% reported, Q4 FY26 11% reported vs ~14% adjusted, Q1 FY27 7.4% reported vs 11.6% adjusted — while Ketan Mody confirms RCPL itself is only 'breakeven on EBITDA terms'. Two parallel separations run alongside it: the Jio Platforms IPO (DRHP 19 June 2026 for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares of Rs 10, SEBI observation 28 August 2026, RHP 14 October 2026, priced at Rs 1,119 on 24 October 2026, with Rs 500 crore reserved for employees and Rs 2,500 crore for individual/HUF RIL shareholders), and the carve-out of AI/data-centre activity into 'Reliance Intelligence'/RIL so that JPL stays asset-light — capex at RIL or Reliance Intelligence, service provision and products accessed by Jio under long-term leases. No investor, lender or partner is recorded as having asked for any of this; analysts' only questions on the demerger were for like-for-like revenue and EBITDA adjustments, and management expressly deferred the EBITDA impact to the next quarter.
rationale.evolution: On the Oct 2024 call the consumer-brands business was still just a bullet inside Dinesh Taluja's retail section (general-trade revenue '250% plus' Y-o-Y) with no hint of separation. The 1 Dec 2025 scheme filings made it real — RCPL demerged out of RRVL into a directly held 83.56% RIL subsidiary — and on the 16 Jan 2026 call (Q3 FY26) RCPL got its own speaker (Ketan Mody), its own Rs 5,000 crore quarter, and the Chairman's 'focused organizational structure' line, while analysts (Investec's Harit Kapoor, CLSA's Vikash Jain) could only extract 'we will have to wait for the next quarter' on the margin impact. By 24 Apr 2026 RCPL presented through its own CFO (Ashutosh Goyal, FY26 Rs 22,000 crore) and retail growth was being quoted both reported and ex-demerger; by 17 Jul 2026 an RCPL Executive Director gave a Rs 1 lakh crore FY2030 ambition and admitted EBITDA breakeven. Over the same window the separation theme widened: AI data centres were explicitly moved out of JPL into Reliance Intelligence (Jan/Apr 2026 calls) and the JPL IPO moved from 'imminent' (Apr 2026) to DRHP (19 Jun 2026) to pricing at Rs 1,119 (24 Oct 2026).

points.point: The 1 Dec 2025 composite scheme demerged the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL into Tira Beauty Ltd (renamed RCPL), dissolved the old RCPL, and paid RRVL shareholders 1 new RCPL share for every 2 RRVL shares.
points.quote: in terms of the Scheme, as consideration for the demerger of the Consumer Brands Business Undertaking from RRVL to New RCPL, New RCPL will allot 1 (one) fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each for every 2 (two) fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10 (Rupees ten only) each of RRVL, to the shareholders of RRVL.

points.point: The structural outcome: FMCG stops being a retail subsidiary and becomes a business RIL owns directly at 83.56%, with the pre-scheme RRVL-held capital of the new entity cancelled.
points.quote: Accordingly, New RCPL will become 83.56% direct subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The only stated rationale anywhere in these documents: the Chairman frames the demerger as giving the consumer products vertical a focused organisational structure to support accelerated growth.
points.quote: The demerger of consumer products business came into effect this quarter. With a broad and diverse product basket ranging from classic Indian brands to new age labels, the consumer products vertical is progressing on its accelerated growth trajectory with a focused organizational structure.

points.point: CFO V Srikanth confirmed the 1 December effective date and sized the separated business at over Rs 5,000 crore of quarterly turnover, growing 60% Y-o-Y — the growth differential versus retail's 8%.
points.quote: On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December. And we are at more than 5,000 Crores of turnover, and this is 60% up on a year-on-year basis.

points.point: Ketan Mody opened RCPL's first post-demerger section by stating the new ownership line (direct subsidiary of RIL, not of Reliance Retail), with 9M revenue of Rs 15,000 crore and four brands above Rs 1,000 crore.
points.quote: So RCPL became the direct subsidiary of RIL from 1st December 2025.

points.point: Asked by CLSA and Investec to quantify the EBITDA that left Reliance Retail with the demerger, Dinesh Taluja declined to give the number — the separation's margin arithmetic was never explained on the call.
points.quote: We will have to wait for the next quarter.

points.point: From Q4 FY26 the demerger became a permanent adjustment in retail's reported growth: 11% reported, ~14% ex-RCPL for the quarter and 12% for the year.
points.quote: Now, if you recollect, RCPL business was demerged out in the last quarter adjusted for that, the growth is almost 14%, for the full year the growth is 12% and if you exclude RCPL demerger the growth would be even higher.

points.point: RCPL began reporting through its own CFO with full-year scale figures — Rs 22,000 crore FY26 revenue (2x), Campa Rs 4,700 crore as India's 4th largest CSD brand, Independence Rs 2,600 crore, 12 plants, 5,000 distributors, 3 million outlets, 40 countries.
points.quote: From an FMCG business perspective, we closed our revenue of Rs.22,000 Crores in 2026 and for the Q4 alone, we delivered a revenue of Rs.7350 Crores, both these are two times growth on the similar period for the last year.

points.point: A full year of the demerger now creates a ~4 percentage point gap between retail's reported and underlying growth, the clearest evidence of the optics the separation changes.
points.quote: In terms of topline growth, as you would recollect, RCPL business was demerged out on 1st of December. So Q1 had the full revenue. Adjusted for that, the underlying revenue growth is 11.6%. On a reported basis, the growth is 7.4%.

points.point: The separated entity's own target is Rs 1 lakh crore of revenue by FY2030, with Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 8,600 crore (2x) — but it is still only at EBITDA breakeven, with margins to come from scale and supply chain.
points.quote: So, like we have announced, the target continues to kind of grow leadership in all categories and we have anyway announced the target is to kind of take this to Rs.1 lakh Crores on FY2030.

points.point: Ketan Mody conceded RCPL earns essentially nothing today — i.e. a breakeven, market-share-focused business was removed from a retail P&L running at ~8% EBITDA margin.
points.quote: EBITDA, I would put it across since the concentration there, yes, we are breakeven on EBITDA terms, but EBITDA will improve as a scale and all the supply chain is kind of put it across but yes, right now the concentration more on the market share

points.point: Baseline before the separation: the same brands (Campa, Independence, Maliban, Ravalgaon) were reported as one line inside Reliance Retail, with no mention of any demerger or separate entity.
points.quote: Consumer brands business continues to scale up very nicely. We are expanding our distribution network. The general trade revenues are growing at 250% plus on Y-o-Y basis.

points.point: A second, explicitly-reasoned separation: AI/data-centre capex is placed in RIL / Reliance Intelligence while Jio buys capacity under long-term leases, keeping JPL asset-light ahead of its IPO.
points.quote: Capex will be RIL or Reliance Intelligence. Service provision will be done by JPL; it will be asset-light service. Products will be developed by Reliance Intelligence, AI products and capex will be incurred there.

points.point: Management clarified that the gigawatt-scale AI data centres (including the 168 MW Meta project at Jamnagar) sit outside Jio Platforms in the already-created intelligence entity.
points.quote: So firstly, I would like to clarify that the AI data centers are not being done in Jio Platforms Limited. They are going to be part of the intelligence business, so RIL or the intelligence entity that has already been created.

points.point: The Jio Platforms IPO (fresh issue of up to 27 crore Rs 10 shares) carved out reservations specifically for RIL's own individual shareholders and for employees — a partial separation that hands RIL holders direct access to the asset.
points.quote: The IPO includes reservation of equity shares of JPL (i) for a value not exceeding Rs. 500 crore for subscription by the Eligible Employees (as defined in the RHP) ; and (ii) for a value not exceeding Rs.2,500 crore for subscription by the Eligible RIL Shareholders

points.point: The JPL listing was priced on 24 October 2026 after a 21–23 October book-build, putting an external price on the separated digital business.
points.quote: JPL has today finalised the Issue Price (including the anchor investor issue price)  at ₹1,119  per Equity Share of face value of  ₹10 each  and has  also filed the Prospectus dated October 24, 2026  with the Registrar of Companies, Gujarat at Ahmedabad .

points.point: Context for separating consumer assets: S&P's upgrade to A- was credited to the rising share of less-cyclical consumer earnings, and RIL cited access to A-rated capital pools and tighter spreads.
points.quote: They have focused on the fact that higher portion of our earnings are coming from less cyclical businesses, especially the consumer side.

rationale.what_management_expects: RCPL: a focused structure for accelerated growth to Rs 1 lakh crore by FY2030, with EBITDA rising from breakeven as capacity, food parks and supply chain scale. Retail: cleaner double-digit underlying growth plus ~8% margins, free to fund hyperlocal/digital commerce and double EBITDA in three years. RIL shareholders: direct 83.56%-held ownership and 1-for-2 shares; Jio stays asset-light with capex in Reliance Intelligence.
rationale.gaps: No stated reason for separating rather than retaining RCPL, no RCPL margin, capex, funding or listing plan, no EBITDA quantification, no synergy loss, tax or governance discussion.

segments.segment_name: Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL) — consumer brands / FMCG business (reported within the 'Others' segment; demerged from RRVL, a direct RIL subsidiary from Dec 01, 2025)
segments.measure_notes: No profit line is disclosed for this business anywhere in the tagged pages — FMCG sits inside the 'Others' segment of RIL's segment reporting (Others EBITDA/segment result also includes Media, Real Estate, treasury income and unallocable expenses), so no RCPL-only segment result, EBITDA, PBT or PAT exists. Revenue shown is 'Gross Revenue' as labelled in the quarterly presentations (gross, i.e. before netting of GST/discounts, not the segment 'external turnover' line); FY26 gross revenue explicitly includes RCPL sales before the de-merger from RRVL.

rationale.rationale: Religare is demerging its entire financial services business — SME/MSME lending (Religare Finvest), retail broking plus e-governance (Religare Broking and its subsidiary Religare Digital Solutions), affordable housing finance (Religare Housing Development Finance, already an RFL subsidiary), and the related investment and ancillary/support activities — out of the listed holdco REL into RFL, which will itself be listed, leaving REL as a pure-play holder of its 63.2% stake in Care Health Insurance; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every REL share, and RFL's pre-scheme capital held by REL is cancelled so RFL's shareholding mirrors REL's. Management framed it as three converging conditions rather than a reaction to distress: the Burman Group's completed takeover as promoters (open offer concluded Feb 2025, board reconstituted July 2025, promoters at 29.75% fully diluted in Feb 2026 and ~30.3% by May 2026 after ~4% of open-market buying, heading to ~34% on warrant conversion), the INR1,500 crore preferential warrant raise subscribed 50:50 by the Burmans and marquee investors (earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, INR75 crore to repay REL's own debt and INR375 crore general corporate purpose), and the fact that the businesses had reached an inflection point where "each business also operates with different capital requirements, risk frameworks, manpower talent and growth trajectories." The stated problems it solves are a conglomerate structure in which insurance (FY26 GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore on 'n' basis, 19.7% retail SAHI share) drowns out a tiny financial services segment (FY25 demerged-undertaking turnover of only INR457.29 crore, 6.2% of consolidated revenue), investors who cannot value the two halves, and management bandwidth: the scheme's four pillars are streamlined focus/simplified structure, value unlocking plus targeted capital raising through a separate RFL listing, dedicated leadership with sector-specific talent and performance-linked rewards, and risk/compliance frameworks tailored to each segment. The financial services side is being restarted from a cleaned-up base — RFL is debt-free with all legacy promoter-era diversion issues provided or written off (including the full INR750 crore Lakshmi Vilas Bank FD), RBI's Corrective Action Plan lifted in July 2025 and bank fraud tags removed, leaving ~INR591 crore cash, ~INR900 crore net worth, 261% CRAR, NOF of INR821 crore and only a ~INR60 crore core SME book — so Arjun Lamba tied the demerger directly to scaling: "Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this." Who asked for it: shareholders and analysts had been pressing since the first call back in Nov 2025 (Vikas Shrivastav on demerging Care and removing the holdco discount, Dixit Doshi on IPO vs demerger of Care), and after the announcement nearly every questioner — Umang Shah, Adarsh, Hitaindra Pradhan, Ravi Purohit, Niharika Karnani, Sarvesh Gupta — argued the value sits in Care and demanded a reverse merger giving direct Care shares, citing the Max Financial precedent. Management conceded the point but said IRDAI's 25–26% promoter requirement cannot be met while the Burmans' look-through stake in Care is only ~18–19%, so this was "the first step in that direction," done after evaluating structural alternatives with leading advisors; Lamba refused to amend the scheme and would not commit to a timeline for a second one. Execution has since run into the regulator: exchanges gave no-objection/no-adverse-observation letters on 7 July 2026, but on 6–7 August 2026 RBI informed REL and RFL that their application for no-objection/prior approval "has not been acceded to," and the companies said they would engage further with the regulator.
rationale.evolution: On the Nov 2025 call (Q2/H1 FY26, the first investor call after the Burman takeover) there was no plan — Vikas Shrivastav asked directly what the structure would look like in two years and whether Care would be demerged from the holdco, and CFO Pratul Gupta would only say the board was evaluating options and wanted to make the businesses "larger, better, stronger" before any capital-market action, while Dixit Doshi asked whether Care would be IPO'd or demerged. A Moneycontrol report on 3 Feb 2026 that REL would demerge and list Care drew an exchange query, which REL denied as a disclosable event; eleven days later, on 14 Feb 2026, the REL and RFL boards approved the scheme — and the Feb 2026 call (16 Feb) was where Gupta laid out the full rationale, the four pillars, the 1:1 ratio, the 15–18 month timetable and a Q1 FY28 RFL listing, while every analyst pushed back that Care, not financial services, should have been separated. By the May 2026 call (13 May, Q4/FY26) the framing had shifted from Gupta's structural logic to Executive Director Arjun Lamba's: separating FS from insurance was "number one," the promoters had bought ~4% more stock toward the IRDAI threshold, and he declined to amend the scheme while leaving a later reverse merger of Care open "at an appropriate stage." The 7 July 2026 exchange observation letters cleared the way, but the 7 Aug 2026 filings disclosed RBI had refused to accede to the application, leaving the scheme stalled pending further engagement.
