points.point: Management said the structure was chosen after a full review of alternatives with external advisors, and promised no operational, customer or employee disruption during implementation.
points.quote: This has resulted after comprehensive evalu ation of various structural alternatives which were discussed with leading advisors.

points.point: Arjun Lamba restated the core purpose as separating financial services from insurance to give shareholders a clean, understandable structure and management a single focus, while acknowledging the holdco-discount complaint.
points.quote: And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.

points.point: Lamba linked the demerger to the capital allocation plan — INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking, ~INR375 crore general corporate purpose, with RFL needing none given ~INR900–1,000 crore net worth and ~INR600 crore cash.
points.quote: Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.

points.point: Pressed by Vikas Srivastava on whether the scheme could be amended to fold Care in once the promoters reach 26%, Lamba ruled out amending it but left a subsequent scheme open.
points.quote: No, I'll answer your last question first. We don't want to amend the scheme.

points.point: Lamba conceded the value is concentrated in Care and said the separation is intended to create value in the other entity too, as promoters moved from ~26% toward ~34% diluted.
points.quote: Yes, we understand that the value is in Care. We are cognizant of that. That's why we are separating the entities, creating clear paths, and we hope to create value in the other entity as well

points.point: The 14 Feb 2026 filing states the demerged undertaking is all of REL's financial services activity — lending, broking, investment and ancillary/support services — explicitly excluding the retained insurance business, i.e. the Care Health shareholding.
points.quote: Provided that, the Demerged Undertaking shall exclude the Remaining Business ( as defined in the Scheme ) compris ing of all the units, divisions, undertakings, assets and liabilities in relation to the Demerged Company’s insurance business, comprising of its investment and shareholding in Care Health Insurance Limited .

points.point: The scheme quantifies how small the demerged half is: FY25 turnover of INR457.29 crore on a consolidated basis, just 6.2% of REL's consolidated turnover.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31  March , 202 5 was INR 457.29 Crores on a consolidated basis  representing 6.2% of the total consolidated turnover of the Company for the year ended 31 March , 202 5.

points.point: Stated rationale includes that the two businesses face different competition and attract different investors, partners and lenders, and that a separately listed vehicle enables sector-focused talent and growth opportunities.
points.quote: The nature and competition involved in the businesses comprising of the Demerged Undertaking is distinct from the other businesses and it is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: The press release lists four objectives — streamlining businesses, listing financial services, focused management with performance mapped to each business, and segment-tailored risk and compliance frameworks — with 1:1 mirror shareholding in RFL and listing targeted for Q1 FY28.
points.quote: Focused management attention:  Enable mapping of employee p erformance and rewards to respective business outcomes, and facilitate attraction and retention of sector -specific talent and resources.

points.point: SEBI's comments routed through the NSE observation letter of 7 July 2026 require REL to disclose the need for the demerger, cost-benefit analysis, risks and the RBI approval position to shareholders — i.e. the rationale was not yet fully documented for them.
points.quote: Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.

points.point: Execution setback: after exchange no-objections on 7 July 2026, RBI declined the no-objection/prior-approval applications of both REL and RFL in letters dated 6 and 7 August 2026, and the companies said they would go back to the regulator.
points.quote: The Company has received a letter dated August 6, 2026 , from the RBI, conveying that the application has been examined and that the request has not been acceded to .

rationale.what_management_expects: REL becomes a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care (GWP INR11,417 crore, PBT INR539 crore 'n' basis, combined ratio heading from 101.4% to ~100% in two years on operating leverage, 18–24% growth). RFL becomes an integrated, separately listed financial services platform — debt-free, ~INR900 crore net worth, ~INR591 crore cash, 261% CRAR — able to leverage to industry norms, raise targeted capital, hire sector-specific leadership on performance-linked rewards, run tailored risk frameworks, and unlock value via mirror 1:1 listing.
rationale.gaps: No cost-benefit or synergy quantification, no RFL valuation or AUM/ROE targets, no holdco-discount fix or Care reverse-merger timeline, no stated path to IRDAI's 26%, and no RBI-rejection reasoning.

rationale.rationale: The separation is the demerger of the Industrial undertaking of SKF India Limited (automotive remaining with SKF India Ltd.) into SKF India (Industrial) Limited, a company incorporated 17 December 2024 purely to receive it, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on 26 September 2025 with appointed/effective date 1 October 2025, a 1:1 share exchange (49,437,963 shares to SKF India holders on the 15 October 2025 record date) and listing on BSE/NSE from 5 December 2025. Management's stated reason is sector focus: the Q3 FY25-26 release frames it as 'SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders,' a 'pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey,' with the industrial entity 'more agile and focused,' able to 'respond faster to market needs' and 'tailor it's manufacturing capabilities' for manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering. On the 13 May 2026 call the operating logic is spelled out as the ACES strategy to 2028 (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF) plus the point that industrial economics differ structurally from automotive — 'industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels... because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller' — and that localization lets it re-enter segments it had exited (wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors). Dedicated capacity is the second half of the logic: the Board approved a new Pune factory on 3 February 2026, part of INR 800 crore+ capex to FY29-30 (including INR 350-400 crore of DGBB/TRB channel additions), commissioning end-CY2028, because the business is 'running out of capacity' and currently relies on SKF India job work. The cost of separating was explicit: INR 1,800.8 million of exceptional demerger charges in Q3 FY26 (IT, professional fees, large stamp duty/transfer premium on the land transferred from SKF India), INR 1,961 million for nine months, and a further INR 183 million of demerger IT cost in Q4, which turned reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million against INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals. Management's payoff case is margin recovery to ~13% once demerger costs lapse by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 and an aspiration of 16-18%, on 8%+ growth; interim performance cited was Q4 FY26 sales INR 9,457.2 million (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY), PBT 9.5% reported and 11.5% ex-one-offs, net working capital down 2.8% to 18.7% of sales, then Q1 FY27 revenue INR 9,707.7 million (+18.3% YoY) at 9.0% PBT.
rationale.evolution: These texts contain no pre-demerger call, so the origin of the idea is not on record here; the earliest document is the Scheme itself (NCLT order 26 September 2025, effective 1 October 2025, listing 5 December 2025). The 4 February 2026 press release, reporting the first post-demerger quarter, carries the only explicit rationale statement (two sector-focused independent organizations, sharper orientation, faster decisions, shareholder value) alongside INR 1,800.8 million of separation costs, and the same Board meeting on 3 February 2026 approved the new Pune factory — converting the rationale into standalone capacity. By the 13 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call the framing had shifted from justification to execution: the ACES strategy 'as we are now a separate listed entity,' INR 800 crore+ capex, re-entry into previously exited wind/railway/tractor business, and a margin path of 13% near term to 15% by FY29-30. The 12 August 2026 Q1 FY27 release continues the 'focused, independent business' framing with 18.3% YoY growth at 9% PBT.

points.point: The Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) transferred the Industrial Undertaking on a going-concern basis at carrying values, with the difference credited to Capital Reserve; NCLT order dated 26 September 2025, appointed and effective date 1 October 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme, among other provisions, entails the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking from the Demerged Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis.

points.point: The only explicit statement of purpose in the filings: two sector-focused, independent organizations for sharper market orientation, faster decision-making and shareholder value, after 102 years of SKF in India.
points.quote: The results come against the backdrop of SKF's demerger into two sector-focused, strategically independent organizations, enabling sharper market orientation, faster decision-making, and enhanced long-term value creation for shareholders, marking a pivotal step in SKF's 102-year India journey.

points.point: MD Mukund Vasudevan's rationale in the 4 February 2026 Q3 FY25-26 release: agility, speed of response and manufacturing tailored to industrial customers, serving manufacturing, railways, renewables, cement and heavy engineering.
points.quote: As a more agile and focused industrial entity, SKF India (Industrial) is well-positioned to respond faster to market needs, tailor it's manufacturing capabilities, and support India's accelerating infrastructure and manufacturing build-out.

points.point: Separation cost quantified as exceptional items: INR 1,800.8 million in Q3 FY26 and INR 1,961 million for nine months for IT cost, professional services and stamp duty including transfer premium on land acquired under the Scheme — which pushed reported Q3 PBT to negative INR 671.4 million versus INR 1,129.4 million before exceptionals.
points.quote: During the quarter and nine months ended 31 December 2025, the Company accounted certain demerger expenses for IT Cost, professional services and stamp duty, including estimated transfer premium payable to statutory authorities to effect transfer of registration of land acquired under the Scheme, aggregating to Rs. 1,800.8 million and Rs. 1,961 million, respectively, which have been included under "Exceptional items".

points.point: The Board meeting of 3 February 2026 — the same meeting that approved the first post-demerger results — approved a new standalone factory at Pune, the capacity leg of the separation.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. on February 03, 2026, has approved the setting up of a new factory /plant at Pune, Maharashtra.

points.point: Management re-stated the ACES strategy (accelerate localization, commercial excellence, disciplined execution, one SKF, defined through 2028) explicitly because the company is now separately listed and needs its own growth and profitability narrative.
points.quote: I thought it's important to reiterate our strategy as we are now a separate listed entity as SKF India (Industrial) and I think it helps to kind of say what are we trying to do and how are we trying to grow and make our business more profitable.

points.point: The structural case for separate industrial management: industrial runs on small lot sizes and channel flexibility unlike automotive — the Pune TRB example raised capacity from 600,000 to 886,000 pieces, cut cost ~18% and improved changeover/flexibility 20% and new-product lead time 35%.
points.quote: Flexibility, which is key, which is industrial business is all about flexibility in the channels, which means we can switch between one product and another because the lot size, unlike automotive, is smaller.

points.point: A concrete problem the focused, localized entity solves: segments previously abandoned on cost/margin grounds — wind, freight railways, agricultural tractors — are being re-entered via localization, including a 32.5 crore tractor OEM win and ZF/Suzlon wind orders that drove 91% QoQ wind growth.
points.quote: The reason you are right, we did exit wind business . Because of localization we are now getting back into it.

points.point: Residual entanglement with the automotive entity persists: SKF India (Industrial) manufactures for SKF India Automotive (~4% of FY26 sales), pays royalty/trademark (up ~INR 60 million QoQ) and a transfer-pricing margin on services, and SKF India job-works for it until the new plant starts.
points.quote: We are , till that new plant comes up , comes about, we are continuing to do some our SKF India entity is continuing to manufacture some for us on a job work basis.

points.point: The one-off separation charges continued into Q4 FY26 at INR 183 million, so reported PBT of 9.5% was 11.5% adjusted (versus 13.1% adjusted in Q3), with the remaining gap blamed on OEM mix (OEM up from 46% to 50%) and full bonus accrual.
points.quote: In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.

points.point: Margin roadmap post-separation: back to ~13% once demerger costs end around end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 through localization, operational efficiency and S&A leverage, with 16-18% only an aspiration held back by OEM mix, competition and depreciation from the new plant.
points.quote: So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.

points.point: Standalone capital plan: INR 800 crore+ capex FY26-27 to FY29-30, a large part for the new Pune plant plus DGBB and TRB channel additions (the INR 350-400 crore earlier flagged), operational mid-2028 and fully ramped by end-CY2028, with growth of ~8% in the interim.
points.quote: So, on capex, the overall plan for the between FY 26, FY27 to FY 29, FY30, we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant which we are in the process of setting up.

points.point: Q1 FY27 (12 August 2026) validates the focused-entity framing: revenue INR 9,707.7 million, up 18.3% YoY, PBT INR 869.2 million at 9.0%, with growth in Wind, General Machinery and Agriculture (Tractors) despite currency and residual demerger costs.
points.quote: In our 3rd quarter as a focused, independent business, SKF India (Industrial) delivered 18.3% year-on-year Sales growth, while maintaining a healthy 9% PBT (in spite of headwinds from currency and demerger-related expenses).

rationale.what_management_expects: For SKF India (Industrial): sharper market orientation, faster decisions, agility and manufacturing tailored to industrial lot sizes; ~8% growth with PBT recovering to ~13% by end-CY2026, ~15% by FY29-30 (16-18% aspiration); net working capital 19-20% of sales; INR 800 crore+ own capex and a new Pune plant replacing SKF India job work; shareholder value via two independent listed entities.
rationale.gaps: No pre-demerger call rationale; no named requester (investors, lenders, partners); no synergy loss, standalone-cost, tax or valuation quantification; nothing on the automotive entity's economics or arm's-length agreement terms.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is not a pharma business at all: it is the Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business that grew up inside Arco Lab Private Limited, Strides' wholly-owned Global Capability Centre, covering life-sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, drug safety and technology-enabled operational services delivered by 400+ subject-matter experts. Management's account is that this began as a captive serving Strides — its FY26 revenue of ₹1,447 million explicitly 'including revenues for services rendered to Strides', with EBITDA of ₹169 million, 3% of Strides' turnover and ~1% of consolidated net worth — but that 'as demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers', which it could not remain inside a generics manufacturer's subsidiary. The filings name four specific problems the carve-out solves: supporting the next phase of growth, serving global customers effectively, building agentic-AI platforms, and enabling access to external capital — so the vehicle was created first (Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, appointed date April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approval May 18, 2026, effective June 1, 2026, making Pivot Path a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides) and only then sold down. The sale values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m post-money: Strides divests a majority for ~₹1,000m (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), Ascent Growth Trust and co-investor Vintage Classic Limited take 65.05%, a 15% ESOP pool is carved for the team, Ascent infuses ₹500m of primary capital, Strides keeps 19.95% and reclassifies Pivot Path as an Associate. Strides frames this as a repeatable playbook rather than a distress exit — 'creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth' — and says it 'strengthens the Company's balance sheet and provides growth capital for Pivot Path', consistent with the three FY26 priorities Badree repeated on the calls (geographic diversification, profitability, balance sheet strength, with net debt at ₹1,437 crores and net debt/EBITDA 1.55x). The stated precedent is the Softgel/OneSource demerger, which Arun Kumar justified in exactly valuation terms — the softgel business was 'adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation' until its 'true value' was discovered through OneSource, with ₹78.8 billion distributed to shareholders. No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the Pivot Path separation; pricing rests on an independent valuation by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, and the deal is stated not to be a related-party transaction.
rationale.evolution: On none of the eight calls (Oct 2024 through May 2026) did management ever mention Pivot Path, Arco Lab's Life Sciences/Digital Innovation business or this Scheme; the only separation discussed was the Softgel-to-OneSource demerger (Oct 2024, Feb 2025, Aug 2025 calls), which established the 'unlock true value outside the generic space' template, and Arco Lab appeared only once, in May 2025, as the wholly-owned subsidiary parked with the retained 1.6% OneSource stake 'for a rainy day'. The Pivot Path track runs entirely through filings: the Scheme was intimated on May 15, 2025 with an appointed date of April 10, 2025, NCLT Bengaluru approved it on May 18, 2026 (the very day of the Q4 FY26 earnings call, which made no reference to it), the order reached the portal May 20 and the certified copy May 25, and the Scheme became effective June 1, 2026. Twenty-six days later, on June 27, 2026, the Board approved the majority-stake sale to the Ascent Capital consortium plus ₹500m primary infusion, with definitive agreements to be executed before June 30 and the share sale to complete by June 30, 2026 and the infusion by July 31, 2026. So the plan visibly changed shape only once: from an internal reorganisation creating a wholly-owned subsidiary into a control sale leaving Strides a 19.95% associate holder.

points.point: The separated unit is Arco Lab's Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business, demerged into Pivot Path Private Limited under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013; on effectiveness Pivot Path became a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of Strides, with the undertaking vesting from the appointed date of April 10, 2025.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the demerger of Arco Lab’s Life Sciences business and Digital Innovation business (the “Demerged Undertaking”) into Pivot Path, pursuant to Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder (“Scheme”).

points.point: The stated reason for the carve-out is four-fold and explicit: next-phase growth, serving global customers, building agentic-AI platforms, and access to external capital — i.e. things the business could not do while embedded in Strides' Global Capability Centre.
points.quote: To support its next phase of growth, serve global customers effectively, build agentic-AI platforms, and enable access to external capital, the business was carved out into Pivot Path pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in May 2026.

points.point: The origin story management gives: a captive capability centre function (life sciences consulting, digital transformation, quality and compliance, technology-enabled operational services) that outgrew its captive role as third-party pharma demand arrived.
points.quote: As demand from external pharmaceutical and life sciences companies grew, the business evolved into an independent platform serving industry-leading customers.

points.point: Size and profitability disclosed for the carved-out business for FY26 — and the admission that its revenue still includes intra-group work for Strides, which is why standalone turnover contribution is shown as Nil and consolidated contribution as only 3% of Strides' turnover and 1% of net worth.
points.quote: For FY26, the carved-out business reported revenue of ₹1,447 million (including revenues for services rendered to Strides) and EBITDA of ₹169 million, demonstrating its operating scale and growth trajectory.

points.point: The deal terms: ~₹2,300m post-money valuation, ~₹1,000m to Strides (₹750m at initial closing, ₹250m on the first anniversary), ₹500m primary into the company, and a resultant cap table of Strides 19.95% / investors 65.05% / ESOP pool 15%, with Pivot Path becoming an Associate.
points.quote: The transaction values Pivot Path at ~₹2,300m on a post-money basis, enables Strides to realise ~₹1,000m while retaining a ~20% stake, and includes a primary capital infusion of ₹500 million to accelerate Pivot Path's next phase of growth.

points.point: The corporate-strategy framing: a repeatable incubate-scale-monetise model in which Strides keeps a minority economic interest, with balance-sheet strengthening named as a direct benefit to the parent.
points.quote: The transaction reflects Strides' strategy of creating, scaling and unlocking value from high-potential businesses while retaining participation in their future growth.

points.point: Badree's stated timing logic: the business needs a partner with capital and expertise that Strides itself does not bring, and the separation is what lets Pivot Path scale independently while Strides still participates.
points.quote: As the business enters its next phase, we believe this is the right time to bring in a strategic investment partner with the expertise and capital to accelerate its growth.

points.point: The buyer's rationale is that independence itself is the enabler — combining technology and agentic AI with 400+ subject-matter experts for compliance, digital transformation and drug safety work for global customers.
points.quote: As an Independent entity, Pivot Path is exceptionally well positioned to combine the power of technology and Agentic-AI with its 400+ subject matter experts in building purpose-built solutions that enable global customers to manage their compliance, digital transformation, and drug safety requirements with greater speed, precision, cost effectiveness and confidence.

points.point: Governance framing: pricing rests on an independent SEBI-registered merchant banker valuation, the buyers (Ascent Growth Trust and BVI-incorporated Vintage Classic Limited) are not promoter/promoter-group/group companies, and the transaction is declared not a related-party transaction and outside Regulation 37A.
points.quote: The transaction has been undertaken based on an independent valuation conducted by a SEBI-registered merchant banker, reflecting the strength of Pivot Path's differentiated capabilities, established customer relationships and long-term growth potential.

points.point: The template for this separation — never applied to Pivot Path on any call, but stated for the Softgel/OneSource demerger: a niche business trapped inside the generics platform was being valued suboptimally, so carving it out revealed its true value.
points.quote: And discussing its true value, while it was adjusting within the generic space at a suboptimal valuation, we discovered its true value of a niche business through OneSource.

points.point: Management quantifies the prior unlock as the proof of its shareholder-value method — ₹78.8 billion distributed via demerger and listing — framing further separations as shareholder-value actions rather than disposals.
points.quote: And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.

points.point: The only call reference to Arco Lab, the entity Pivot Path was carved out of: it is described merely as the wholly-owned subsidiary holding the retained OneSource stake, with no hint that a services business inside it was being prepared for separation.
points.quote: So we retained this in Arco Lab, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Strides.

points.point: On the Q4 FY26 call held the same day NCLT approved the Scheme, management restated the three priorities the Pivot Path monetisation serves (diversification, profitability, balance sheet strength — net debt ₹1,437 crores, 1.55x) but said nothing about the demerger or any intent to sell the business.
points.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have been very clear on our priorities, geographical diversification, profitability and balance sheet strength.

points.point: Sequencing confirms a two-step design: the Scheme was made effective on June 1, 2026 after the certified NCLT order was filed with the RoC, and the stake sale was approved just 26 days later on June 27, 2026.
points.quote: Further, pursuant to filing of the certified true copy of the Order with the Registrar of Companies by the participating entities, namely Arco Lab and Pivot Path, the Scheme of Demerger has become effective from June 1, 2026.

rationale.what_management_expects: Pivot Path: ₹500m primary capital, independence to serve global customers, build agentic-AI platforms, scale with a 15% ESOP pool for 400+ experts, and access external capital. Strides: ~₹1,000m cash (₹750m now, ₹250m deferred), a strengthened balance sheet, Associate accounting, continued ~19.95% participation in the upside, and sharper focus on its pharma core.
rationale.gaps: Calls never mentioned Pivot Path, Arco Lab's carve-out or the Scheme; no stated investor, lender or partner request; no margin, valuation-gap or post-deal related-party pricing explanation.

segments.measure_notes: No profit or revenue line of any kind is disclosed for this business on the supplied pages. Segment reporting in all three annual reports covers only 'Pharmaceutical' and 'Bio-pharmaceutical' (FY2025/FY2026 report a single 'Pharmaceutical' segment post the CDMO/Softgel demerger), so the segment result / PBT figures shown there belong to the Pharmaceutical segment, not to Arcolab/Pivot Path. None of these are revenue, operating profit or PAT of the business.

rationale.rationale: Management presents the separation as a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232, sanctioned by the NCLT Mumbai Bench amongst Tata Motors Limited (the demerged company, now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited), TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the resulting company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (amalgamated into the demerged entity), effective 1 October 2025; the resulting company was renamed Tata Motors Limited on 29 October 2025 and its shares listed on BSE/NSE (ticker TMCV) on 12 November 2025, with outstanding PSUs replaced one-for-one under a new scheme covering up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution). The stated problem the split solves is a reporting and identity one: 'Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then' — from Q4 FY26 the company reports standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as its primary lens, giving 'a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture'. The separation cost ₹960 crore of one-time demerger expense booked in Q3 FY26 (part of ₹1,500 crore standalone / ₹1,600 crore consolidated exceptionals, alongside ₹603 crore of new labour code and ₹82 crore of Iveco acquisition cost). The pure-play case is argued with numbers: FY26 revenue ₹77,000 crore (vs ₹66,000 crore FY23), EBITDA margin up from 7.8% (FY23) to 13.2% (FY26) — ~550bps of 'structural improvement' — EBITDA doubled from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore, PBT before exceptionals ₹8,700 crore, first-ever double-digit EBIT at 11% (the CV segment first crossed it at 10.6% in Q3 FY26), FCF ₹9,200 crore or 12% of revenue, Auto ROCE 72%, cash conversion cycle of negative 31 days, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated, and a maiden final dividend of ₹4/share (~₹1,500 crore outflow). Cyclicality is the second problem: non-cyclical revenue (parts & service, Fleet Edge digital subscriptions, Smart City e-bus operations) is compounding at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR, 'deliberately building this mix', and Q4 working-capital sinks historically concentrated in Q4 have been spread through the year. Third, the standalone CV entity became the acquisition vehicle: its own balance sheet and a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG funded an all-cash voluntary totalitarian tender offer for Iveco Group N.V. at EUR 14.10 (raised to EUR 14.40), valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, creating ~EUR 21 billion (INR 2,28,000 crore+) of combined revenue and ~590k units with Europe ~46%/India ~32%/South America ~8%/RoW ~14% and 'substantially no overlap' — expected to 'drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector', plus enhancing Iveco's FPT powertrain business. Structural simplification continues inside the CV entity: TMF Holdings Limited and TMF Business Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiaries) are being amalgamated into it, and Tata Motor Finance had already been folded into Tata Capital (whose October 2025 IPO priced 20–25% below the merger valuation, forcing a ₹2,000 crore mark-to-market loss in Q2 FY26 and a ₹295 crore write-back in Q3).
rationale.evolution: In the Nov 2025 call (Q2 FY26, 13 November 2025) management reported the split as done rather than argued for it — demerger effective 1 October, CV listing completed as TMCV 'as committed previously', Iveco approvals underway and the bridge loan secured. In the Feb 2026 call (Q3 FY26, 29 January 2026) the cost showed up as a ₹960 crore one-time demerger exceptional while the CV segment hit a double-digit EBIT margin (10.6%) for the first time and Iveco approvals were guided to end-March. In the May 2026 call (Q4 FY26, 13 May 2026) the framing shifted decisively: 'Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company... a defining shift', the old carved-out CV segment was retired in favour of standalone reporting, three-year pure-play metrics were laid out, and Iveco closure slipped to Q2 FY27 pending French and Spanish financial-regulator approvals. Filings then show execution: offer launched 4 September 2026, 89.42% tendered by 27 October 2026, 96.29% after the reopening on 6 November 2026, triggering the Dutch legal squeeze-out, alongside the TMF Holdings/TMF Business Services amalgamation notices.

points.point: The CV business crossed a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time as a standalone reporting unit — the profitability milestone used to validate the standalone case.
points.quote: The CV segment also achieved the milestone of a double-digit EBIT margin for the first time, which now stands at 10.6%.

points.point: The clearest statement of what the separation achieved: a pure-play commercial vehicle company, which management calls a defining shift that changes how the business should be presented.
points.quote: Demerger being effective from 1st of October 2025, Tata Motors is now a pure play commercial vehicle company, and this is a defining shift that changes how we think is most appropriate to present our financials.

points.point: The problem the split solves, as stated: the CV business was previously visible only as an internal carve-out construct inside the combined entity.
points.quote: Historically, we reported a CV segment. It was an internal construct that carved out CV operations from within the erstwhile combined entity. That was a practical necessity then.

points.point: Post-demerger reporting switched to standalone financials including the Tata Cummins joint operation as the primary lens, for transparency and comparability.
points.quote: This gives you a cleaner, more complete, and more directly comparable picture of the business going forward.

points.point: The margin record cited as structural rather than cyclical: 7.8% to 13.2% EBITDA over three years, with EBITDA doubling from ₹5,100 crore to ₹10,200 crore and FY26 EBIT at 11%.
points.quote: EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26. That's nearly 550 bps of structural improvement over three years.

points.point: Capital-efficiency case for the standalone entity: ₹9,200 crore FCF (12% of revenue), ₹2,800 crore reinvested, Auto ROCE of 72%, negative 31-day cash conversion cycle, net cash ₹7,500 crore standalone and ₹13,700 crore consolidated.
points.quote: Finally, the Auto ROCE stands at 72% is an industry-leading number, when EBIT doubles, capital discipline holds, returns follow.

points.point: Deliberate de-cyclicalisation of the standalone business via parts & service, Fleet Edge digital and Smart City e-buses, growing far faster than the cyclical truck business.
points.quote: Over the period, non-cyclical CAGR is running at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.

points.point: Mechanics of the separation as disclosed in every filing: NCLT Mumbai-sanctioned Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited, with the resulting company renamed and listed.
points.quote: As per the Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench—amongst Tata Motors Limited, TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (the Company) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited—the Company’s name was changed to Tata Motors Limited from TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (effective 29 October 2025), and its equity shares are listed on the BSE Ltd and the NSE Ltd.

points.point: Employee incentives were carried across the split one-for-one: outstanding PSUs of the demerged company entitle holders to a matching PSU from the CV entity, implemented via a new scheme for up to 23,07,647 shares (0.062% dilution).
points.quote: the unexercised performance share units (“PSUs”) (whether vested or unvested) granted to participants under the Demerged Company’s Incentive Scheme(s) and remaining outstanding as on the record date shall entitle such participants to receive one (1) corresponding PSU to be granted by the Resulting Company under a new incentive scheme.

points.point: The separated CV entity's strategic use of its independence — the Iveco combination is justified on scale, no overlap, operating leverage and dampening CV cash-flow volatility; ~EUR 21 billion combined revenue, ~590k units, Europe 46%/India 32%.
points.quote: The new company will be able to drive better operating leverage by spreading its capital investments over larger volumes, generating operating efficiencies and reducing the cash flow volatility inherent in the commercial vehicles sector.

points.point: Iveco was pursued as an all-cash EUR 14.10 (later EUR 14.40) offer valuing Iveco at ~EUR 3.82 billion, funded by a committed EUR 3.825 billion bridge from Morgan Stanley and MUFG, with Exor (27.06% of shares, 43.19% of votes) irrevocably committed.
points.quote: TML CV HS signed a debt commitment letter with Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. and MUFG Bank, Ltd. for fully committed bridge financing to be used in connection with the Transaction, which was subsequently implemented through a facility agreement entered into by the Offeror for an aggregate amount of up to EUR 3,825,000,000.00.

points.point: Structural simplification continued after the demerger: the CV entity is absorbing its own wholly owned financing subsidiaries TMF Holdings and TMF Business Services under a further NCLT scheme.
points.quote: The Scheme provides for the merger of Amalgamating Company 1 and Amalgamating Company 2 (being direct and indirect wholly owned subsidiaries of the Company respectively) with the Company.

rationale.what_management_expects: Pure-play CV: cleaner, comparable standalone reporting including Tata Cummins joint operations; teens (not mid-teens) EBITDA guidance, double-digit EBIT, capex 2–4% of revenue, FCF ~12% of revenue, 72% ROCE, net cash ₹7,500cr standalone/₹13,700cr consolidated funding a ₹4 dividend and the Iveco bid; with Iveco, ~EUR21bn revenue, operating leverage over larger volumes, less cash-flow volatility. No PV-entity commentary.
rationale.gaps: Why separate at all — no pre-demerger call is in the record: no stated valuation-unlock, synergy or capital-allocation rationale, no investor, lender or partner named as requesting it, no entitlement ratio.

rationale.rationale: TVS Motor is carving its consumer finance and related business undertaking — the lending, investment, leasing and ancillary/support activities it runs directly and through subsidiaries, principally the NBFC TVS Credit Services — out of the listed automotive company into Harita ARC Limited, a shell wholly-owned subsidiary bought from TVS Credit Services for Rs 25,000 on 28th October 2026, with TVS Motor shareholders getting 1 share of the resulting company for every 1 TVS Motor share (47,50,87,114 shares, valuation by Bansi S. Mehta Valuers LLP, fairness opinion by JM Financial), and the resulting company to be listed; the same Composite Scheme also amalgamates the dormant wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited (total assets Rs 251.44 Cr, net worth Rs 198.93 Cr, nil turnover) into TVS Motor 'to streamline the group corporate structure', after which it is dissolved without winding up. Management's stated problem is that finance has outgrown its host: the demerged undertaking already turned over Rs 3,921 Cr of TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated revenue in H1 FY27, and the Financial segment carries Rs 43,003 Cr of assets and Rs 33,288 Cr of liabilities against Automotive's Rs 23,868 Cr, which is why consolidated net debt/equity sits at 2.90x versus 0.37x standalone. The Scheme says the consumer finance business 'needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path', that 'the nature of, and competition in, the consumer finance and related business differ from those of the other businesses', and — the capital-structure crux — that 'a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth'. The second stated problem is investor mismatch: a standalone entity 'can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business', and the demerger will 'unlock the value of the Demerged Undertaking for the shareholders of the Demerged Company'. Chairman Sudarshan Venu framed it as 15 years of sustained investment reaching scale — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India serving 'more than 45 million customers across 100,000 touchpoints', plus the Varthana education-finance acquisition and the Jana Small Finance Bank stake — so the platform should now allocate capital to its own priorities while TVS Motor 'remain[s] focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally'. It follows the August 2026 step in which the group's NBFCs approved merging STPL Trading and Services into Home Credit India Finance (155.79 shares per 200) and then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance into TVS Credit Services (9.94 per 180), expressly for 'consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions'; alongside the demerger the board also bought STPL outright for Rs 530.08 Cr to pick up ~2.4% more of TVS Credit post-merger. No lender, partner or named investor is cited as having asked for the split.
rationale.evolution: Strikingly, the separation is absent from all seven earnings calls in the window (Jan 2025 through Jul 2026): management discussed TVS Credit only as a performance line — book Rs 26,647 Cr and PBT Rs 1,027 Cr in FY25 (28 Apr 2025 call), Rs 30,631 Cr and Rs 1,248 Cr in FY26 (13 May 2026), Rs 32,053 Cr and 2.6 crore customers in Q1 FY27 (21 Jul 2026) — while repeatedly describing fresh equity infusions into it (Rs 200 Cr in Q3 FY26 per the 28 Jan 2026 call, Rs 200 Cr across FY26, Rs 711 Cr in Q2 FY27 per the filing). The only hint of structural intent came from an analyst on the 31 Jul 2025 call asking about monetising or IPO-ing TVS Credit, which CFO Gopala Desikan shut down as 'not yet even discussed at the Board level'. The plan then surfaces entirely in filings: the 5 Aug 2026 NBFC-consolidation scheme (STPL → Home Credit India Finance → TVS Credit Services, citing RBI directions), then the 28 Oct 2026 board approval of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement that demerges the undertaking into Harita ARC Limited 1:1 and folds TVS Motor Services into TVS Motor, with the press release calling the demerger 'the next step in this strategic process'.

points.point: The 28 Oct 2026 Composite Scheme demerges the consumer finance and related business undertaking from TVS Motor into Harita ARC Limited and simultaneously amalgamates wholly-owned TVS Motor Services Limited into TVS Motor.
points.quote: The Scheme, inter alia, provides for: (i) the amalgamation of the Transferor Company with the Company; and (ii) the demerger of the Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) from the Company into the Resulting Company on a going concern basis, in consideration for which the Resulting Company shall issue its shares to the shareholders of the Company in proportion to their shareholding in the Company.

points.point: Stated rationale #1: structural simplification into two independent standalone platforms, each with its own strategy and capital plan.
points.quote: The demerger will simplify the group structure and create focused businesses, with a clear segregation of the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business.

points.point: Stated rationale #2: the lending business has risk, competitive and growth characteristics unlike the vehicle business, so it needs its own strategy.
points.quote: The consumer finance and related business needs a separate strategy suited to its industry-specific risks, market dynamics and growth path;

points.point: The capital-structure crux — an NBFC can run far more balance-sheet leverage than a manufacturer; consolidated net debt/equity was 2.90x at 30 Sep 2026 against 0.37x standalone.
points.quote: a financial services company can have a higher leverage (as compared to the Demerged Company) for its growth .

points.point: Investor/lender mismatch is named explicitly: a pure-play finance entity can draw capital providers who want finance exposure, and this unlocks value for existing holders.
points.quote: the independent company can attract different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the consumer finance and related business .

points.point: Size of the carve-out: the demerged undertaking produced Rs 3,921 Cr of revenue in the period ended 30 Sep 2026 against TVS Motor's Rs 35,770 Cr consolidated turnover; shareholders get 1:1 shares and the new entity will be listed.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the period ended 30th September 2026 was Rs. 3,921 Crore out of the total turnover of Rs. 35,770 Crore of the Company .

points.point: Press release frames the trigger as scale reached after 15 years of investment — TVS Credit plus Home Credit India at 45 million customers and 100,000 touchpoints, plus Varthana and Jana Small Finance Bank — needing a dedicated structure for capital allocation.
points.quote: The consumer finance and related business have expanded in scale and scope and a dedicated st ructure will provide greater strategic focus, flexibility in capital allocation and the ability to pursue opportunities across the consumer finance and related sector s.

points.point: Chairman Sudarshan Venu's framing: full value realisation for the finance platform while TVS Motor concentrates on global mobility leadership, with shareholders participating in both.
points.quote: It positions them to realise the full potential of their assets and capabilities while enabling TVS Motor Company to remain focused on strengthening its leadership in mobility globally .

points.point: The precursor step (5 Aug 2026): STPL merges into Home Credit India Finance, then Home Credit India Finance and TVS Housing Finance merge into TVS Credit Services — partly driven by regulator-led NBFC consolidation; TVS Motor separately paid Rs 530.08 Cr for STPL to gain ~2.4% more of TVS Credit.
points.quote: consolidating the NBFCs within the group in terms of RBI directions.

points.point: The only investor-side prod in three years of calls: an analyst asked about earlier plans to monetise or IPO TVS Credit Services, and the CFO said the board had not taken it up — no mention of a demerger.
points.quote: And as far as the question is all about IPO, not yet even discussed at the Board level.

points.point: Scale of the business being separated, as management last described it on a call: book up 19% to Rs 32,053 Cr, PBT Rs 283 Cr for the quarter, ~2.6 crore customers, ~62,000 touchpoints.
points.quote: The book size of TVS Credit grew by 19%. Now it is at INR 32,053 crores as against INR 26,898 crores last year.

points.point: FY26 record finance earnings quantified on the call — the profit stream now leaving the listed automotive entity.
points.quote: PBT has grown by 22%, INR 1,248 crores as against INR 1,027 crores during last year.

points.point: TVS Motor was repeatedly injecting equity into the finance arm while it sat inside the parent — Rs 200 Cr in Q3 FY26, and Rs 711 Cr in Q2 FY27 per the quarterly filing — the capital drain the separate structure is meant to re-route.
points.quote: Now coming back to the second question on INR 900 crores, the delta this quarter has been TVS Credit Services, we have invested about INR200 crores.

rationale.what_management_expects: For the finance platform: strategic autonomy, sharper capital allocation, freedom to run higher NBFC-style leverage, a dedicated investor/lender/partner base, and value unlocked via a 1:1 listed entity. For TVS Motor: a simplified group structure, operational synergies from absorbing TVS Motor Services, and undiluted focus on automotive/mobility leadership globally. Shareholders participate in both.
rationale.gaps: No call ever discusses the demerger; no margin, ROE, capital-release, cost, tax, debt-allocation or timeline numbers for either entity; no promoter-control or future-stake-sale intent disclosed.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Amber's Electronics / EMS arm, housed in IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd — PCB assembly (~INR2,281cr of FY26 revenue), bare PCB through Ascent Circuits (98.5% owned), Shogini Technoarts (80%) and the Ascent-K/Korea Circuit HDI JV (~INR600cr), plus Power-One Microsystems (60%, power electronics, ~15% EBITDA) and 50.4% of Israel-listed Unitronics (industrial automation, 24-25% EBITDA) — leaving Amber with the RAC/consumer-durables division (INR8,383cr FY26) and Sidwal railway/defence (INR535cr). The stated driver is funding: essentially all of the group's capex sits in electronics, with more than INR4,500cr of ECMS investment approvals (Ascent multilayer INR991cr, Ascent-K HDI INR3,200cr, Shogini INR500cr), asset turns of only 0.75-1.1x, and the 48% MeitY plus 42% UP incentives arriving 5-6 years after the spend, so FY27 capex of INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash) and ~INR1,400-1,500cr in FY28 must be pre-funded against a board policy never to exceed 2x debt/EBITDA and Jasbir Singh's pledge to be net-debt-free. Management said investors asked for it: private equity funds were 'chasing to invest in the electronic division', and instead of loading Amber's balance sheet they raised INR1,750cr inside ILJIN (mostly CCPS, including ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr) while Amber separately did a INR1,000cr QIP. Separation also gives electronics its own margin and valuation identity — 2.8% EBITDA when ILJIN was bought in 2018 on INR300cr revenue, 6.9% FY25, 8.8% FY26, 10.8% in Q4 FY26, 26% ROCE, guidance of 40% FY27 growth at 9.5-10% and a $1bn revenue target at 11.5-12% EBITDA — against a weather-driven RAC business that saw quarters of -30% to -35% and nine bad seasons in 25 years. The outside CCPS holders also need a price: conversion happens 'based on the future multiple and valuation' (auditors provisioned up to ~30% dilution in NCI), which a listing supplies; and their presence already constrains group structuring, since management could not say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business would sit in ILJIN 'because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table'. It is being done as a listing of the subsidiary, not a demerger: in April 2026 Amber put another INR296.02cr into an INR328.12cr ILJIN rights issue (89.58% to 89.72%); in July 2026 ILJIN split shares from Rs10 to Rs5, raised authorised capital to Rs250cr, issued a 25:1 bonus, converted from private to public limited, shifted its registered office from Pune to Greater Noida and resolved to explore fund-raising 'including... public issue'; the DRHP was filed on 7 November 2026. In parallel Amber is cleaning up the rest of the portfolio — merging wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast into itself for compliance/cost reduction and peer benchmarking, and selling Sidwal's entire 49% Shivaliks (Titagarh Firema) JV for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85 after INR112cr of FY26 impairment/JV losses, 'to curtail future losses'.
rationale.evolution: The capex trigger appears first on the Jan 2025 call (Korea Circuit JV awaiting the ECMS scheme, Rs1,000cr+ threshold) and on 19 May 2025, when the funding answer is still vague — 'in touch with various institutions' — alongside an INR3,000cr application plan. By 30 July 2025 it has split into two named routes, an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and 'private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division', with the $1bn/11.5-12% electronics ambition and a net-debt-free pledge framing why outside money must sit at ILJIN; on 7 Nov 2025 the INR1,750cr ILJIN raise (CCPS, ChrysCapital INR1,100cr pending CCI) and Amber's INR1,000cr QIP are both announced, and 10 Feb 2026 confirms the full INR1,750cr received with Amber still at 90% until CCPS convert. From there it becomes an exit path for those investors: 18 May 2026 ties conversion to 'future multiple and valuation' (~30% assumed dilution), 20 June 2026 shows the ILJIN cap table already constraining where new businesses can be placed, and the filings then execute mechanically — Mar/Apr 2026 rights issue, 11 July 2026 split, 25:1 bonus, public-limited conversion, registered office to Greater Noida and a 'public issue' resolution, and the DRHP on 7 Nov 2026 — none of it ever discussed on an earnings call.

points.point: The capex need that later drives the separation starts here: the Korea Circuit HDI/substrate JV is on hold pending the ECMS scheme, with a likely Rs1,000cr-plus minimum investment and 70-75% of it only reimbursed later by MeitY and the states.
points.quote: So, on Korea Circuit we are waiting for Government to finalize the incentive scheme.

points.point: With an INR3,000cr PCB application planned and subsidies spread over 5-6 years, management says the Electronics division is itself seeking third-party funding — the first hint of capital being raised at the subsidiary rather than at Amber.
points.quote: So we are already in touch with various institutions for that.

points.point: Two funding routes are named — an INR2,500cr QIP enabling resolution at Amber and private equity money targeted specifically at the electronics arm; the same call sets the constraint that drives it, a board cap of 2x debt/EBITDA and a goal to be net-debt-free by FY27.
points.quote: Second direction is a lot of private equity funds who are chasing to invest in the electronic division.

points.point: The separated entity is given its own standalone ambition and margin identity — $1bn revenue in three years at 11.5-12% EBITDA, versus ILJIN's 2.8% EBITDA on INR300cr when acquired in 2018.
points.quote: With all the add -ups, we intend to take Electronics division to $1 billion by next 3 years with target EBITDA of 11.5% to 12% range.

points.point: The raise happens at two levels simultaneously: INR1,750cr into ILJIN (mostly CCPS; INR370cr in September, INR280cr in October, ChrysCapital's INR1,100cr pending CCI) and a separate INR1,000cr QIP at Amber used mainly to cut debt.
points.quote: We secured funding of INR1,750 crores from marquee investors.

points.point: ILJIN's raise closes in full and Amber's stake stays at 90% only because the instrument is CCPS; the same call adds the ECMS approvals (Ascent-K HDI, Shogini) and 116 acres at Jewar that the money has to fund.
points.quote: On the balance sheet front, ILJIN Electronics has successfully concluded fundraise with the entire INR1,750 crores received from marquee investors.

points.point: The outside investors' economics depend on a valuation event: no dilution has occurred yet because CCPS convert off a future multiple, with auditors provisioning roughly 30% maximum dilution in non-controlling interest. FY27 capex is guided at INR1,800-2,000cr (INR1,100-1,200cr cash), net debt INR511cr rising to INR700-800cr.
points.quote: It will happen in future based on the future multiple and valuation.

points.point: The ILJIN cap table already limits group structuring — management cannot say whether the new Oppo mobile-phone business (8m units year one, 13-15m year two, sub-INR50cr capex, 1.5-2% industry EBITDA) will sit inside ILJIN or directly under Amber.
points.quote: But we will not be able to define it right now because we have other shareholders also in the IL JIN cap table .

points.point: April 2026: Amber pre-funds ILJIN again, subscribing INR296.02cr of a INR328.12cr rights issue (12,46,430 shares), taking its holding from 89.58% to 89.72% — capital in before the listing, not a stake sale.
points.quote: Further, pursuant to the allotment of equity shares under the rights issue by IL JIN on 21st April 2026, which has resulted in an investment of Rs. 296.02 Crore, Amber Enterprises India Limited (“Amber” or “the Company”) has subscribed to and been allotted 12,46,430 equity shares.

points.point: July 2026: ILJIN is mechanically prepared for listing — Rs10 to Rs5 share split, authorised capital to Rs250cr, 25:1 bonus, conversion from private to public limited, registered office moved Pune to Greater Noida, and a board resolution to explore fund-raising modes including a public issue.
points.quote: Evaluation and exploration of various fund-raising options to support its future growth initiatives.

points.point: 7 November 2026: the separation becomes a formal partial listing of the electronics arm — a DRHP for ILJIN's IPO filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, Amber retaining ~90% pre-offer.
points.quote: IL JIN Electronics (India) Limited (formerly known as IL JIN Electronics (India) Private Limited), a material subsidiary of the Company, has ﬁled the Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated 6th November 2026 (“DRHP”), on 7th November 2026 with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited in connection with its proposed Initial Public Oﬀer (“IPO”).

points.point: The rest of the group is being simplified in the opposite direction: wholly-owned AmberPR Technoplast (cross-flow fans) is merged into Amber — no shares issued, NCLT dispensed with meetings, appointed date moved to 1 April 2026 — for compliance savings, scale synergies and cleaner peer comparison.
points.quote: more absolute and profound comparison with industry peers ie. benchmarking business performance with industry; and

points.point: Portfolio pruning runs alongside: the 49% Shivaliks/Titagarh Firema stake is impaired (INR94cr in Q3, INR112cr FY26 including JV losses) and then sold in March 2026 to JP Fincap for a nominal Rs1,09,798.85, ending Italy export ambitions while keeping the Titagarh commercial relationship worth ~INR700cr of visibility.
points.quote: And to curtail future losses, on etime exceptional impairment loss has been recognized during this quarter.

rationale.what_management_expects: Electronics: self-funded ECMS PCB capex, $1bn revenue in ~3 years, margins from 2.8% (2018) toward 11.5-12%, double digits from FY27, ~26% ROCE, stickier high-entry-barrier industrial/defence mix. Amber: retains ~89.7%, frees cash for consumer durables and railway (30-35% growth, 16-17% margins), stays under 2x debt/EBITDA near net-debt-free; CCPS dilution finally priced off a market valuation.
rationale.gaps: Calls never discuss the IPO itself: offer size, fresh issue versus OFS, use of proceeds, valuation, Amber's post-listing stake, CCPS conversion terms, or why listing rather than demerger.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is Swara Baby Products Limited, Brainbees' diaper/hygiene manufacturing subsidiary, which filed a DRHP on July 02, 2026 for an IPO of up to Rs 10,000 million (Rs 5,000 million fresh issue plus Rs 5,000 million offer for sale), with Brainbees itself selling up to Rs 3,000 million in the OFS (board approval July 01, 2026). Management's stated reason is drift in purpose: Brainbees invested Rs 906.17 million in 2020 for 53.45% (fully diluted) purely as backward integration — "to scale up our home brands within diaper category" with "more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing" — but Swara then became the largest contract manufacturer by value in Fiscal 2025 in Indian hygiene manufacturing, adding adult diapers and sanitary napkins (similar absorbent raw materials and processes), third-party and multinational customers, and exports via a US subsidiary (Swara Corp, incorporated 08 December 2025). Brainbees' share of Swara's revenue fell from 27.03% in FY24 to 22.64% in FY26, so management says Swara "has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees," with "different capex and working capital needs" it should "bridge their own capital requirement" rather than draw on Brainbees' cash. On selling into the OFS despite holding cash, management argued "holding cash and holding an investment are two different capital allocation decisions" and that partial monetisation lets it "crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities." Control and commercials are explicitly unchanged: Brainbees stays Promoter at 76.59% (raised from 75.92% in a December 2025 swap that moved Solis Hygiene under Swara to put the hygiene vertical "under a single roof"), Swara remains a subsidiary, Brainbees' management has no involvement in running it (Alok Birla and Udit Birla lead; Supam Maheshwari and Gautam Sharma sit as non-executive directors), and "terms of trade" stay at arm's length with "no impact either on supply chain or pricing." Swara contributed Rs 11,639 million revenue in FY26 (Rs 9,004.39 million after eliminating Rs 2,634.61 million of inter-company sales) and Rs 1,445.7 million of adjusted EBITDA into the India multi-channel segment. No lender, partner or investor is named as having demanded it; analysts had only pushed on a separate asset, GlobalBees, where Supam said in August 2025 that "the most probable outcome for Globalbees... will be listing" given its separate board, management and investors (Premji, Lightspeed, Chiratae).
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced as an analyst question about a different unit: on the Aug 2025 call (Aug 13, 2025) Sachin Dixit asked whether FirstCry investors could expect liquidity from GlobalBees "getting demerged, having its own IPO," and Supam said listing was the most probable outcome over a few years; on the Feb 2026 call (Feb 13, 2026) Ajay Agarwal asked for GlobalBees listing timelines and got no answer. Meanwhile the hygiene business was quietly being tidied for separation — a December 26, 2025 intra-group restructuring put Solis Hygiene under Swara Baby to bring the whole hygiene vertical under one roof, lifting Brainbees' Swara stake to 76.59%. Neither the Feb 2026 nor the Jun 2026 call (May 26, 2026) mentioned Swara or any separation at all; on Jun 2026 Supam even said buybacks and similar capital actions had not been discussed internally or at board level. The plan then appeared fully formed in filings only — board approval of OFS participation on July 01, 2026, DRHP plus a management Q&A on July 02, 2026 — followed by a related narrowing at GlobalBees, whose non-core brand rationalisation culminated in the October 07, 2026 sale of its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile.

points.point: Asked by JM Financial's Sachin Dixit whether FirstCry shareholders could get liquidity from GlobalBees being demerged or separately IPO'd, Supam framed listing as the likely eventual route and Brainbees' monetisation path over a few years.
points.quote: Having said this, the most probable outcome for Globalbees as an outcome will be listing, which company and its shareholders will decide over a period of time, is when Brainbees also will find a monetization opportunity over a period of a few years.

points.point: The structural argument for separability given for GlobalBees was that it already runs independently of Brainbees, with its own CEO, board and outside shareholders including Premji, Lightspeed and Chiratae.
points.quote: The company has a separate management team, which is run separately and also it has its separate board, and also it has a separate set of investors as well, apart from Brainbees as well, which includes Premji, Lightspeed, and Chiratae, and so on and so forth.

points.point: Garima Mishra pressed on the CCPS infusion into GlobalBees; Gautam said it funded working capital, and that all three investor-directors who had stepped off the GlobalBees board participated in that round — the capital-need theme that later justifies Swara funding itself.
points.quote: This is largely for taking care of their working capital requirement, Garima

points.point: Ajay Agarwal again asked directly for a GlobalBees listing timeline; the reply covered only Flipkart's revenue-recognition impact and GlobalBees' EBITDA growth (c.150% YoY in Q3, c.50% in 9M), with no timeline given.
points.quote: And again on Globalbees, any plans on listing of Globalbees? Can you share the tentative timelines or any sense on the same?

points.point: Five weeks before the Swara DRHP, asked about the low valuation, takeover risk and buybacks, Supam said no such capital action had been discussed internally or by the board — and said nothing about any separation.
points.quote: Yes, we have sufficient cash on the company, but we haven't discussed any of these buybacks and stuff like that so far, in our internal discussions or even board discussions.

points.point: The July 02, 2026 DRHP filing states the original purpose of the 2020 Rs 906.17 million investment for 53.45%: backward integration to scale FirstCry's own diaper home brands with control over quality, timelines and innovation.
points.quote: We wanted to scale up our home brands within diaper category and wanted to do backward integration to get more control on quality at scale, production timelines and continued innovation in diaper manufacturing.

points.point: Core rationale: Swara outgrew the FirstCry ecosystem — multiple third-party and multinational customers, adult diapers and feminine hygiene, exports and a US subsidiary, with Brainbees' share of its revenue down from 27.03% (FY24) to 22.64% (FY26).
points.quote: With Swara Baby's diversification across product lines, more channels, expansion into International geographies, the business has charted a very different long term vision as compared to the original alignment with Brainbees.

points.point: Why not just fund Swara off Brainbees' balance sheet: its capex and working-capital profile differs, so it should raise its own money while Brainbees keeps supply and arm's-length pricing unchanged.
points.quote: With this expansive and global vision in contract manufacturing of disposable hygiene products with different capex and working capital needs, we decided to initiate the process of separately listing this business so that they can follow their independent journey and bridge their own capital requirement.

points.point: Why Brainbees sells up to Rs 3,000 million into the OFS despite ample cash: capital-allocation discipline and value crystallisation, while Swara stays a 76.59% subsidiary and Brainbees' management stays out of its operations.
points.quote: Partial monetization of a successful investment allows us to crystallize value, improve return on investment and maintain flexibility for future strategic opportunities.

points.point: Preparatory step on December 26, 2025: Swara Baby acquired 100% of Solis Hygiene (FY25 turnover Rs 240.73 crore, 3% of consolidated), with Brainbees swapping its 79.34% Solis stake for 56,26,738 Swara shares, lifting its Swara holding from 75.92% to 76.59%.
points.quote: In order to bring the complete Hygiene vertical under a single roof, the restructuring is being done.

points.point: The parallel pruning at GlobalBees: on October 07, 2026 it signed an MOU to sell its entire 51.54% in Mush Textile (brands Mush and BePlush, Rs 11.34 crore or 0.13% of FY26 turnover) for Rs 5,68,93,940 to Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt.
points.quote: Upon completion of the aforesaid transaction, Mush will cease to be a Subsidiary of GlobalBees and, accordingly, will also cease to be a Step-down Subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The GlobalBees brand-rationalisation logic that frames the Mush exit: loss-making, slow-growing non-core brands were being exited, with core categories at 30% growth and 4.9% adjusted EBITDA versus 2% consolidated.
points.quote: As you're aware, over the last few quarters, we've been speaking about rationalizing certain brands because they were delivering a relatively lower revenue growth as well as incurring losses.

rationale.what_management_expects: Swara funds its own capex/working capital from the Rs 5,000 million fresh issue and pursues an independent global contract-manufacturing path; Brainbees crystallizes value, improves ROI and gains flexibility via up to Rs 3,000 million OFS cash, while keeping 76.59% control, Promoter status, consolidation of Swara's Rs 9,004 million revenue and Rs 1,445.7 million adjusted EBITDA, and unchanged arm's-length supply and pricing.
rationale.gaps: No earnings call ever mentions the Swara IPO, its valuation, or use of OFS proceeds; GlobalBees listing timeline never answered; Mush sale pricing and loss unexplained.

judge.what_is_spun: Bio Pharma undertaking into Ennature Bio Pharma; Spirits and Biofuel undertaking into IGL Spirits Limited
demerged_business_names: Ennature Bio Pharma Private Limited (former name)
spirits business, including IMFL, country liquor and bio-fuel businesses
judge.reason: Creation of three separate companies, each with a clear business focus and dedicated management oversight, enabling more efficient allocation and utilisation of capital, investments and resources towards growth.
judge.insiders: Promoter family leads both spins: U.S. Bhartia Chairman & MD of IGL Spirits, daughter Pragya Bhartia Barwale MD of Ennature; sons-in-law non-executive directors. Promoter group voted 3,99,67,854 shares 100% in favour.
judge.hidden_value: Cost apportionment splits value IGL 31.77%, Ennature 20.61%, IGL Spirits 47.62%. Q1FY27 revenue: IGL Rs 345cr, IGL Spirits Rs 694cr, Ennature Rs 90cr. Spirits earned 21-22% EBIT margins inside a chemicals-labelled parent; Ennature margins depressed (4.1% EBIT 9MFY26).
judge.selling_pressure_why: Ennature small (2,23,42,255 shares, 1-for-3 odd lots, Rs 90cr quarterly revenue) and a different industry from chemicals parent.
judge.listing_timeline: Both resulting companies received listing and trading approvals from BSE and NSE on November 02, 2026, with "Date of Commencement of Trading: November 04, 2026" (stated in filings dated 2nd November, 2026); earlier filings said only that management "will apply to BSE and NSE for listing" (1 September 2026).
judge.read_next: Information Memorandum of Ennature Bio Pharma and IGL Spirits (approved 8 September 2026) — segment debt allocation and standalone margins.
judge.quote: Ennature Bio Pharma Limited will house the bio-pharma and bio-polymers businesses.
