rationale.rationale: Management presented the break-up of India Glycols into three listed companies — India Glycols Ltd (bio-based specialty and performance chemicals, glycols/bio-glycols, new specialties, industrial gases, plus the 49% Clariant IGL JV), IGL Spirits Ltd (IMFL, Indian Made Indian Liquor/country liquor, ENA and the bio-fuel/ethanol business) and Ennature Bio Pharma Ltd (plant APIs and nutraceuticals — thiocolchicoside, nicotine, curcumin brands — plus the small bio-polymers/guar gum business) — as a focus and investor-appetite problem, not distress and not a lender demand. On the 6 Feb 2025 call Rupark Sarswat said the idea was to run the companies differently because they have different focuses, to give them much more focus, and because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments, creating potential to unlock value; CFO Anand Singhal listed four benefits: independent growth for each business, reducing the risk of one business affecting the others, drawing focused investors, and clearer management and resource allocation. They sized the three P&Ls on 9MFY25 — chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Bio Pharma Rs 178 cr at 14.9% — against FY24 reported segments of BSPC Rs 1,626 cr, bio-fuel Rs 512 cr and potable spirits Rs 5,575 cr gross. A named driver was premiumisation of IMFL: Sarswat called focus on the IMFL business one of the significant rationales, in a potable-spirits market management put at about $56bn in 2025 growing 7.2% to roughly $112bn by 2034, with the Amrut royalty/distribution tie-up, CSD and paramilitary registrations, Bacardi contract bottling and Kerala entry as the engines; conversely he argued the chemicals business would show up better once it got more focus. The scheme also split the balance sheet: of about Rs 1,200 cr of long-term debt, roughly Rs 500 cr was earmarked to chemicals and Rs 700 cr to liquor (restated in Nov 2025 as Rs 600 cr India Glycols and Rs 800 cr IGL Spirits), big capex was frozen until after the demerger so the separate companies could decide it, bank limits had to be re-allocated with the SBI-led consortium, and the credit rating stayed on watch list until completion. No outside party was said to have demanded the separation — the board initiated it on 4 Feb 2025; analysts pressed on listing and value unlock (Balasubramanian, Rohit Nagraj) and one investor objected to demerging a margin-squeezed Ennature (Jaswinder Singh, 11 Aug 2025); approvals came from shareholders (4,42,48,625 of 4,42,48,626 votes in favour) and unsecured creditors (36 of 36, 100% by value), with the secured creditors meeting dispensed with on 95.46% consent. To Saket Kapoor's objection that clubbing government-priced grain ethanol with liquor would dilute the liquor valuation, management answered with synergy — captive high-quality ENA, backward integration, scale, piped supply, better resilience and absolute margin — and said this seemed like the most optimal way going forward, not with a valuation argument.
rationale.evolution: First disclosed on the 6 Feb 2025 call as a composite scheme: amalgamation of promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings into IGL (so promoters held IGL directly) plus a three-way demerger, appointed date 1 April 2026, with all three companies to be listed via the NCLT route in 12-15 months. The board dropped the KHL amalgamation leg on 16 May 2025 and pursued the demerger alone; the 11 Aug 2025 call restated the rationale (different investor appetites, enhancing value) and deferred capex to the post-demerger companies, while 18 Nov 2025 added the per-entity debt split (Rs 600 cr / Rs 800 cr) funded partly by a Rs 467 cr promoter-and-friends preferential issue at Rs 915. By 12 Feb 2026 capex and the credit rating were both explicitly waiting on the demerger, and on 18 May 2026 management was awaiting the NCLT order expected 21 May. NCLT Allahabad sanctioned the scheme on 17 July 2026; it became effective 1 Sept 2026 (record date 2 Sept), with 1 IGL Spirits share per IGL share and 1 Ennature share per 3 IGL shares, and the two new companies listed on 2 Nov 2026 and began trading 4 Nov 2026.

points.point: Sarswat's first statement of purpose: three separate companies, run differently, to create focus and let different investors back different businesses, with value unlock as the outcome.
points.quote: And the whole idea behind this is to run these companies differently.

points.point: Sarswat tied the structure to investor appetite and future outside money coming into individual businesses.
points.quote: And also, to allow potential investments in different businesses because different investors tend to have a different focus for investments.

points.point: CFO Anand Singhal's four formal benefits of the scheme — independent growth, risk insulation, focused investors, better management and resource allocation.
points.quote: The main benefits of the proposed scheme will be that the demerger will enable independent growth for each businesses. Separating the business will reduce the risk of one business affecting the others.

points.point: Singhal explicitly framed the shareholder-value objective as attracting a different investor base to each entity.
points.quote: Will create a potential to unlock value for the shareholders by drawing focused investors.

points.point: Singhal sized each proposed entity on 9MFY25: chemicals Rs 1,079 cr at 13.6% EBITDA margin, IGL Spirits Rs 1,628 cr net at 14.4%, Ennature Rs 178 cr at 14.9%.
points.quote: IGL Spirits, which is proposed to be the other Company which will be having the Liquor business and the Bio-Fuel business, is having 9MFY25 turnover of Rs. 1,628, this is on net basis with 14.4% EBITDA margin.

points.point: The original scheme also merged promoter vehicle Kashipur Holdings into IGL so promoters would hold IGL shares directly; this leg was later dropped.
points.quote: The merger of Kashipur Holdings, holding Company with India Glycols, is largely keeping in mind that the promoters will have the direct shareholding of IGL in their names.

points.point: Sarswat named IMFL premiumisation as a principal reason for the separation, citing a potable-spirits market of about $56bn in 2025 growing 7.2% to ~$112bn by 2034.
points.quote: one of the significant rationales for us is to provide the focus on the IMFL business, which you know is a very interesting business going forward.

points.point: Bio-polymers/guar gum was moved out of chemicals into Ennature; the Clariant JV stayed with chemicals because the JV sells chemicals and its profits flow there.
points.quote: And the third one will be Ennature Bio Pharma, which will be Ennature as it is right now, and also taking the Bio Polymers business, which is a small business, from chemicals and putting it into Ennature Bio Pharma.

points.point: Saket Kapoor challenged the valuation logic of putting government-priced ethanol with liquor; Sarswat answered with captive-ENA synergy and resilience, not multiples.
points.quote: So, we are clubbing the government regulated business of grain-based ethanol and the liquor part. So, does that gel better for getting the right valuation going ahead since other liquor companies may or may not be having this under the portfolio.

points.point: Sarswat conceded the choice of perimeter was a judgement call, and said shared corporate resources would continue so standalone costs did not balloon.
points.quote: So far in the wisdom of people who sat together, this seemed like the most optimal way going forward.

points.point: Singhal confirmed all three companies would be separately listed through the NCLT route, with a 12-15 month timeline and appointed date 1 April 2026.
points.quote: So this demerger will be effective from 1st April, 26 and all the three companies will be listed on the stock exchange.

points.point: Debt was pre-allocated by business: of ~Rs 1,200 cr long-term debt, ~Rs 500 cr to chemicals and ~Rs 700 cr to liquor, with annual repayments of Rs 150-160 cr (liquor) and Rs 90 cr (chemicals).
points.quote: Just to brief you as of now position, we are having about INR 1,200 crores long-term debt in the books of the company, out of which about INR 500 crores will go to the Chemical division and INR 700 crores will go to the liquor division.

points.point: Rationale restated after the KHL leg was dropped: value enhancement through separate strategies matched to separate investor appetites, while retaining plant-proximity synergies.
points.quote: The idea is that different investors have different appetites for different kind of businesses.

points.point: Capital allocation was deliberately parked until separation — only rollover/maintenance capex of Rs 40-50 cr in FY26, with real capex decisions left to the new companies.
points.quote: So, we are not targeting any big size CapEx in this year, and we will like to consolidate. And after the demerger, the separate companies will think over the CapEx.

points.point: Investor Jaswinder Singh attacked the premise, noting Ennature's net margin had fallen from ~33% in 2021 to 2.38% while being spun out as a value-unlock story.
points.quote: We are planning to unlock shareholder value by demerging our business units when there is extreme degrowth in that business.

points.point: Debt split restated per entity and part-funded by a Rs 467 cr preferential issue at Rs 915 to promoters, friends and relatives used wholly to prepay debt.
points.quote: So, in these two companies, India Glycols and IGL Spirits, the segregation what we have done as of date is about INR 600 crores and INR 800 crores.

points.point: The pending demerger froze both capex and the credit rating: rating agencies kept IGL on watch list, so no upgrade or full benefit on cost of funds until completion.
points.quote: So, you will not find the rating improvement till our demerger happens.

points.point: Sarswat argued the chemicals business is structurally better than reported numbers show and would look better once separately focused; Rs 804 cr of debt was prepaid in Q4FY26.
points.quote: And for the year at least, we see that we should have improved profitability and also top-line growth.

points.point: Singhal linked post-demerger deleveraging to the Clariant JV: a further 24% equity sale in FY29 per agreement would make the chemical business debt-free.
points.quote: So, in '28-'29, I'm hopeful that the Chemical business will be totally debt-free.

points.point: The 16 May 2025 board meeting removed the Kashipur Holdings amalgamation from the scheme, leaving a pure three-way demerger with appointed date 1 April 2026.
points.quote: The earlier proposal for the amalgamation of KHL into the Company will no longer form part of the Scheme being pursued.

points.point: The 1 Sept 2026 news release gave the official benefit set — dedicated focus, improved oversight, resource allocation and entity-specific capital management — with Q1FY27 net revenues of Rs 345 cr (IGL), Rs 694 cr (IGL Spirits) and Rs 90 cr (Ennature).
points.quote: The demerger will result in the creation of three separate companies, each with a clear business focus.

points.point: Share entitlement: 1 IGL Spirits share per IGL share and 1 Ennature share per 3 IGL shares; 6,70,26,765 and 2,23,42,255 shares listed, trading from 4 Nov 2026.
points.quote: Resulting Company 2 shall issue 1 (One) Equity Share having face value of INR 5 (Indian Rupees Five) each, to the shareholders of Demerged Company holding 1 (One) Equity Share of INR 5 (Indian Rupees Five) each.

points.point: Cost-of-acquisition apportionment implies the relative values management assigned: IGL 31.77%, Ennature 20.61%, IGL Spirits 47.62% — spirits plus biofuel is the largest piece.
points.quote: India Glycols Limited 31.77% ... Ennature Bio Pharma Limited 20.61% ... IGL Spirits Limited 47.62%

points.point: Approval was overwhelming: shareholders voted 4,42,48,625 to 1 in favour and all 36 participating unsecured creditors (100% by value) backed it; the secured creditors meeting was dispensed with on 95.46% consent.
points.quote: the Scheme of Arrangement has been approved by the requisite majority of Equity Shareholders (4,42,48,625 votes in favour out of 4,42,48,626, with 1 vote against)

points.point: Separate boards and leadership were installed on 21 Aug 2026 — U.S. Bhartia as CMD of IGL Spirits, daughter Pragya Bhartia Barwale as MD of Ennature (credited with taking that division past Rs 200 cr revenue), each with four independent directors.
points.quote: Ms. Pragya Bhartia Barwale (DIN: 02109262) has been appointed as Additional Director (Managing Director) & Key Managerial Personnel

rationale.what_management_expects: IGL: chemicals judged on its own — richer performance-chemicals mix, Clariant JV cash, debt-free by FY29. IGL Spirits: IMFL premiumisation plus captive ENA/ethanol synergy, carrying the larger debt. Ennature: branded nutraceuticals and clinicals rebuild. All three: dedicated focus, independent growth, own capital allocation, insulation from each other's risk, and focused investors unlocking value.
rationale.gaps: Why the KHL amalgamation leg was dropped (post deliberations only), scheme costs, standalone overheads, and the Bhartia/Barwale leadership split are never explained; no valuation or adviser basis.

judge.reason: Segregation of distinct business verticals with separate risks, rewards and investors; consolidation of Power Evacuation Business into IRSL to unlock value and lend enhanced focus; establishing IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, creating two listed entities
judge.insiders: Inox Wind Limited, promoter and holding company, directly holds 51.13% of Inox Green; IRSL shares issued pro-rata to the same shareholders. Director/KMP stakes tiny (Bindu Saxena 12,640 shares). No separate incentive scheme stated.
judge.hidden_value: Removing ~Rs 1,000 crore gross block and Rs 50-55 crore annual depreciation leaves Inox Green a pure-play O&M business with ~50% EBITDA margins, tax shield and FY27 EBITDA guidance above Rs 600 crore; IRSL holds the capital-heavy, leveraged evacuation assets, losses and a Rs 96.8 crore tax demand
judge.selling_pressure_why: Only 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 held - small odd-lot stakes; 4,89,82,030 shares spread to O&M holders; different industry (EPC/power evacuation), loss-making, heavily indebted

Aug 24, 2026: after allotment of 4,89,82,030 shares, 'IRSL is taking necessary steps for crediting the aforesaid equity shares to the respective demat accounts... and for obtaining the listing and trading approvals for the said equity shares from the Stock Exchanges.' No completed listing date stated through the latest filing (Oct 7, 2026).

rationale.rationale: The separation is the demerger of Inox Green Energy Services Ltd's (IGESL) power evacuation / substation and common-infrastructure business into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, formerly Resco Global Wind Services), leaving IGESL a pure-play renewable O&M company and consolidating all evacuation/EPC infrastructure in IRSL, which gets automatically listed. Management's core explanation is historical and structural: when IGESL was spun out of Inox Wind, the EPC business was slump-sold to Resco, but the already-commissioned substations and transmission lines could not be moved because, as Devansh Jain said in Aug 2024, shifting them 'would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business'; so IGESL's balance sheet stayed 'unnecessarily inflated' with assets on which it is 'actually the trustee', while all new substations were being built in Resco anyway ('no future CapEx under Inox Green at all', Feb 2024). The financial fix they repeatedly quantified: a gross block of ~INR 1,000 crore (net block ~INR 750 crore, Aug 2024) leaves IGESL, annual depreciation of ~INR 50-55 crore (~INR 13-17 crore a quarter) is eliminated, PBT rises by that amount, and only ~INR 3-5 crore a quarter (~INR 10 crore a year, Feb 2026) of revenue goes out with virtually no cost and no interest moving — Akhil Jindal put the benefit at '~INR 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis' (Nov 2024), turning reported PAT of ~INR 6 crore into ~INR 18-20 crore. They stressed the evacuation assets are not needed for O&M ('not required for O&M services per se... that is required for further providing a turnkey solution'), so IGESL becomes a zero-capex, asset-light annuity business where EBITDA equals PBT and cash PAT, helped by a ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax-loss shield that stays at company level, with 'significant improvement in ROE and ROCE' (Jun 2026). The Scheme's own rationale adds that risks, rewards, financial profile, competition and opportunities are 'separate and distinct' for O&M versus power evacuation, that the evacuation business 'is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders', that consolidating it into IRSL (which already does the same business) unlocks value and lends enhanced focus, and that the result is two listed entities each free to pursue its own strategy. On the IRSL side, management argued the infrastructure is itself a high-value platform — INR 175 crore raised at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation (Sep 2025), ~10 GW of 'plug and play' evacuation infra made more valuable by the CERC hybridisation amendment — and that listing it 'will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green' (Nov 2025). The push came from the promoters/board (valuers appointed Aug-Nov 2024, scheme approved 13 Nov 2024) with investors on calls repeatedly asking about rationalising subsidiaries and value unlocking; Akhil Jindal framed the purpose as giving shareholders optionality — 'a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business' — and shareholders, warrant holders, secured and unsecured creditors all approved it before NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned it.
rationale.evolution: On the Feb 2024 call the idea did not exist yet; management only explained that all future common-infra capex would sit in Resco, not Inox Green, while legacy depreciation ran on. By the Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 (Oct 25, 2024) calls the board had appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate demerging the power evacuation business, pitched as a 'cleaner and asset-light balance sheet' worth ~INR 12 crore a quarter to the bottom line, and the board approved the Scheme on 13 Nov 2024; in Feb 2025 (Jan 31, 2025) Akhil Jindal said exchange approvals were due in February and NCLT would take 6-9 months, with IGESL holders getting ~20% of the renamed Inox Renewable Solutions. By Sep 2025 (Sep 1, 2025) stock-exchange no-objections were in and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad (approval expected in 2-3 quarters), IRSL had raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the CERC hybridisation ruling made its infra far more valuable; Nov 2025 (Nov 14, 2025) reported shareholder and creditor approval, and Feb 2026 (Feb 13, 2026) said hearings were in final stages with listing 2-3 months out. NCLT sanctioned the scheme on 13 Mar 2026, it became effective 4 May 2026, and on the Jun 2026 (May 29, 2026) call management confirmed approval and booked the benefits as done — INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore depreciation gone, ROE/ROCE improved — while refusing to give IRSL's standalone top line or EBITDA until listing; the record date was 1 Aug 2026 and 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares were allotted on 24 Aug 2026.

points.point: Pre-demerger baseline: management explained IGESL carries legacy substation gross block (4 GW capacity, 3 GW commissioned) with ~INR 13 crore quarterly depreciation, while all future common-infrastructure capex is being incurred in Resco Global, a 100% subsidiary of Inox Wind.
points.quote: So, no future CapEx under Inox Green at all. So, whatever is the depreciation which is being incurred on a quarterly basis will continue until and unless our net block gets consumed.

points.point: Board appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate the demerger; Mathusudhana framed it as producing a cleaner, asset-light balance sheet whose main benefit is eliminating depreciation.
points.quote: The proposed demerger will significantly add value through depreciation elimination.

points.point: Devansh Jain gave the historical reason the assets were stranded in IGESL: at the time of the EPC slump sale to Resco, only uncommissioned assets moved, and commissioned substations could not be shifted without re-opening contracts with over 200 customers.
points.quote: We could not shunt it out from this balance sheet into Resco because that would have entailed taking approval from over 200 customers and then arm twisting us in terms of renegotiating contracts and screwing the entire O&M business.

points.point: He added that IGESL's balance sheet was inflated by assets it merely holds as trustee (net block ~INR 750 crore), and that the remaining business is a zero-capex annuity with no land bank or future evacuation capex.
points.quote: Inox Green's balance sheet is unnecessarily inflated thanks to these historical substations which are lying on its balance sheet of which we are actually the trustee.

points.point: Akhil Jindal quantified the P&L effect for Pritesh Chheda: the whole depreciation goes, only INR 3-4 crore of quarterly revenue leaves, and IGESL shareholders receive Resco shares in lieu, with valuation yet to be fixed.
points.quote: Excluding the substation business, the revenue would be down by around Rs. 3 crores or Rs. 4 crores on a quarterly basis, and the whole depreciation will go away. So, broadly that will add around Rs. 12-odd crore in the bottom line on a quarterly basis.

points.point: Mathusudhana answered Bhavik Shah's objection that the transferred assets would come back as opex: the evacuation and common infrastructure is not needed to run O&M at all, it belongs to the EPC/turnkey business, so margins are unaffected.
points.quote: So as far as the power evacuation and the common infrastructure, we have developed is not required for O&M services per se. That is required for further providing a turnkey solution to the customers.

points.point: Jindal described the post-demerger entity as an asset-light balance sheet with no depreciation, so EBITDA is the benchmark for PAT; the ~INR 700 crore accumulated tax losses stay with IGESL because they sit at company, not asset, level.
points.quote: So when you're looking into the next year's balance sheet of Inox Green, it would be an asset-light balance sheet. And it would also have no depreciation charges as a continued item. What it means is that our profitability will be far more stronger.

points.point: Asked by Hansal Thakkar whether the subsidiaries would be rationalised into IWL shareholders' hands, Jindal said the whole intent of separating the businesses was shareholder optionality, and that no further corporate action is needed.
points.quote: And I think from a shareholder's perspective, a shareholder has got now a choice to hold any part of the business. He can hold the O&M business, he can hold the infrastructure business, he can hold the entire value chain together under Inox Wind.

points.point: Mathusudhana restated the balance-sheet numbers (INR 1,000 crore gross block off, INR 50-55 crore annual depreciation eliminated, PBT up by that amount, ROE/ROCE up), with exchange no-objections received and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad.
points.quote: Once the scheme is approved by the NCLT, the gross block of around INR1,000 crore will be off our balance sheet and subsequently the depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores annually will be eliminated, thereby increasing the PBT by that amount.

points.point: Sanjeev Agarwal gave the value case for the receiving entity: IRSL had just raised INR 175 crore at a ~INR 7,400 crore valuation, and the new CERC hybridisation rules multiply the value of its site infrastructure (Devansh: ~10 GW of plug-and-play infra).
points.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

points.point: With shareholder and creditor approval obtained, Devansh Jain framed the separation as a value-unlocking event for both the parent and IGESL, with IRSL listing as Inox Wind's EPC arm.
points.quote: I believe that the de-merger and subsequent listing of Inox Renewable Solutions will unlock substantial value for both Inox Wind and Inox Green.

points.point: Answering Prit Nagersheth on how much revenue comes off, management sized the revenue leakage at only ~INR 10 crore against ~INR 50 crore of depreciation removed, i.e. no material impact on the INR 600 crore FY27 EBITDA math.
points.quote: So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet. And around INR 50 odd crores of depreciation will go out from the balance sheet.

points.point: Mathusudhana confirmed NCLT Ahmedabad approval and booked the benefits as realised: INR 1,000 crore gross block and INR 50-55 crore annual depreciation eliminated, profitability and returns up; Devansh said remaining steps were administrative, 1-2 months.
points.quote: It has also led to significant improvement in ROE and ROCE of Inox Green.

points.point: Management declined to disclose IRSL's top line or EBITDA profile until the demerger dates are announced, and tied the post-demerger IGESL story to ~INR 600 crore FY27 EBITDA converting almost fully to cash with no depreciation, no finance cost and a INR 700 crore tax shield.
points.quote: We cannot say at this point in time. I think once that demerged, we'll elucidate more plans. At this point in time, it's part and parcel of Inox Wind.

points.point: The Scheme's stated rationale is segregation of two verticals whose risk-reward and financial profiles differ, consolidation of the evacuation business into IRSL which already runs it, and establishing IGESL as a pure-play O&M player, producing two listed entities.
points.quote: Further, the Power Evacuation Business is capable of attracting different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders.

points.point: Consideration to IGESL shareholders was fixed by registered valuer Finvox Analytics (fairness opinion from Marwadi Chandarana) at 122 IRSL shares per 1,000 IGESL shares; appointed date 1 Oct 2024, NCLT sanction 13 Mar 2026, effective 4 May 2026, record date 1 Aug 2026, 4,89,82,030 IRSL shares allotted 24 Aug 2026.

rationale.rationale: These texts announce no separation: the only board-approved reorganisation is the opposite — a consolidation. On 29 September 2026 the boards of JSW Cement Limited (JCL) and its 66.23%-owned listed subsidiary Shiva Cement Limited (SCL) approved a Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-232 read with Sections 52 and 66, amalgamating SCL into JCL with appointed date 1 April 2026, no cash consideration, and a swap of 5 JCL shares of ₹10 for every 41 SCL shares of ₹2 (JCL's own SCL equity cancelled; the ₹100 crore of 1% OCCRPS it holds also cancelled). The problems management says it solves are: dependence on third-party clinker — SCL's 1.32 mtpa Sundargarh (Odisha) clinker plant becomes backward integration, 'avoiding third-party purchases and associated mark-ups'; split funding — a single entity can raise funds on 'more favorable terms' and inter-company guarantees disappear; two listed entities' duplicated administration, record-keeping, consolidation effort and legal/regulatory compliance; a broken balance sheet at SCL (FY26 turnover ₹435.17 crore, net worth negative ₹30.08 crore versus JCL's ₹5,995.28 crore and ₹7,029.47 crore), whose ₹133.92 crore accumulated losses are written off against its securities premium, while JCL's amalgamation adjustment deficit is set against its own premium account (left at ₹4,335.67 crore) — described as 'right sizing' the financial statements; and SCL's illiquid minority float, whose 33.50% public holders move into a larger, institutionally-held stock. Structurally it is tiny and non-dilutive: shares rise from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537, promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%, public from 27.03% to 27.67%. No investor, lender or JV partner is said to have asked for the Shiva merger; valuation was by PwC Business Consulting and BDO Valuation, with fairness opinions from SBI Capital Markets (JCL) and DAM Capital (SCL), JM Financial as exclusive financial advisor and Price Waterhouse & Co as tax adviser; closing is guided at 12-14 months subject to stock exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai and Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation. The genuine separations in these texts are different and smaller: the ₹191.63 crore cash sale of Algebra Endeavour / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd (a Gujarat power plant) to Nuvoco Vistas (SPA 17 November 2025), and JCL selling up to ₹123 crore of JSW One Platforms shares as Promoter Selling Shareholder in that company's IPO (board 13 August 2026, alongside JSW Steel's up to ₹811 crore).
rationale.evolution: The Shiva amalgamation never appears in any of the four earnings calls supplied — the consolidation theme surfaces only around the UAE clinker JV: on the 3 September 2025 Q1 FY26 call Kamlesh Bagmar (Lotus Asset Managers) argued holding Fujairah clinker through a JV 'don't make much sense for the shareholders', and CFO Narinder Singh replied the financial investors would exit over time and it would become a full subsidiary; on the 21 May 2026 Q4 FY26 call Raghav Maheshwari (Equirus) asked directly about merging the JV and was told 'not as of now', maybe in 2-3 years once the financial investor is given an exit, while the new 1.65 MTPA Fujairah grinding unit was instead placed in a wholly owned subsidiary at USD 39 million. The 13 February 2026 investor presentation disclosed the only completed carve-out — the Nuvoco SPA for Vadraj Energy Gujarat at ₹191.63 crore — and footnoted Shiva's 1.0 MTPA Sambalpur grinding unit built under a commercial arrangement with Bhushan Power and Steel. The Shiva merger then arrives fully formed in the 29 September 2026 board outcome and press release, and is restated as a 'Key Business Update' in the 27 October 2026 Q2 FY27 press release; the November 2025 call transcript is unreadable, so any discussion there cannot be checked.

points.point: The transaction is an amalgamation of the listed 66.23%-owned subsidiary Shiva Cement into JSW Cement, appointed date 1 April 2026, explicitly to create one unified platform rather than to separate anything.
points.quote: Creating a consolidated cement platform supports Transferee Company's strategy, enabling category leadership, increased competitiveness, enhanced market share and efficient resource utilization.

points.point: Core industrial logic is backward integration: Shiva's 1.32 mtpa clinker plant at Sundargarh, Odisha stops being a third-party-style supply and becomes internal, cutting external procurement and mark-ups.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will result in backward integration of clinker manufacturing with the Transferee Company's cement manufacturing business.

points.point: Financial rationale is single-entity borrowing capacity and the removal of inter-company guarantees between parent and subsidiary.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will lead to greater ability of the consolidated entity to access and raise funds within a single entity on more favorable terms, leading to elimination of inter company guarantees and facilitate more efficient funding arrangements.

points.point: Running two listed companies is called out as duplicated cost and compliance — two sets of records, two consolidations, two regulatory burdens.
points.quote: The proposed amalgamation will result in a simplification of the existing corporate structure and eliminate administrative functions and duplications, reducing regulatory and legal compliances of two listed entities, eliminating multiple record keeping and reducing time and efforts for consolidation of financials at the group level,  consequently reducing the administrative costs of maintaining separate companies, while reducing the multiple legal and regulatory compliances.

points.point: Shiva is financially impaired: paid-up equity ₹159.00 crore, FY26 turnover ₹435.17 crore and net worth negative ₹30.08 crore at 31 March 2026, against JSW Cement standalone turnover ₹5,995.28 crore and net worth ₹7,029.47 crore; ₹133.92 crore of accumulated losses are extinguished against its securities premium.
points.quote: With effect from the Appointed Date, and upon coming into effect of the Scheme, the debit balance of Retained Earnings and SPA in the books of Transferor Company is likely to be  INR (133.92) crore and Nil respectively.

points.point: The parent's amalgamation deficit is absorbed into its own securities premium, which is left at ₹4,335.67 crore — the 'right sizing' of both balance sheets.
points.quote: With effect from the Appointed Date, and upon coming into effect of the Scheme, the balance of Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit Account is likely to be Nil. The balance of SPA in books of Transferee Company is likely to be INR 4,335.67 crore.

points.point: Shiva's 33.50% public float is given liquidity: 5 JSW Cement shares of ₹10 per 41 Shiva shares of ₹2, lifting JSW Cement's count from 1,36,33,64,936 to 1,37,55,13,537 and promoters from 72.02% to 71.39%.
points.quote: The public shareholders of the Transferor Company would become shareholders in the Transferee Company, which has a higher traded equity share base, greater market liquidity, and a diversified institutional investor base, thereby providing shareholders with enhanced liquidity, broader market participation, and improved opportunities for value realization.

points.point: CEO Nilesh Narwekar framed it as integration and simplification, with completion guided at 12-14 months subject to exchanges, SEBI, NCLT Mumbai and Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation.
points.quote: The proposed merger is a strategic step towards creating a more integrated and efficient business.

points.point: The only consolidation pressure voiced by investors concerned the UAE clinker JV, not Shiva — Kamlesh Bagmar of Lotus Asset Managers argued holding Fujairah through a JV was poor for shareholders; the CFO said the financial investors would exit and it would become a full subsidiary, timeline undecided.
points.quote: So lastly, like, doesn't it make a bigger sense to have, like, say, clinker capacity of Fuj airah under our own hold entirely?

points.point: Asked again about folding the Fujairah JV in, management deferred it to 2-3 years because a financial investor must first be given an exit — while the new 1.65 MTPA UAE grinding unit was put in a wholly owned subsidiary (USD 39 million) that consolidates into the parent, with the JV selling clinker to it at arm's length.
points.quote: Not as of now. Probably going forward in next 2 -3 years, we will have a look because there is a financial investor sitting there, we'll have to provide exit to him.

points.point: The actual disposal in the period was non-core: Algebra Endeavour / Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd, owning a Gujarat power plant, sold to Nuvoco Vistas for cash; the November 2025 filing confirms the division contributed nothing to turnover, income or net worth.
points.quote: Entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with Nuvoco Vistas Corp. Ltd. for the transfer of Vadraj Energy Gujarat Ltd. (owning a power plant in Gujarat), for a consideration of Rs. 191.63 crore

points.point: Because Shiva is a subsidiary, the deal is a related-party transaction under LODR; arm's length rests on independent registered valuers (PwC Business Consulting, BDO Valuation) and a category 1 merchant banker fairness opinion, with no cash moving.
points.quote: Additionally, the consideration to be discharged for the Scheme of amalgamation is determined by independent registered valuers on which a fairness opinion has been issued by an independent category 1 merchant banker, the transaction therefore is at arm's length.

rationale.what_management_expects: For JSW Cement: in-house clinker (1.32 mtpa) replacing third-party purchases and mark-ups, lower costs, single-entity funding on better terms, no inter-company guarantees, simpler compliance, category leadership and market share; securities premium of ₹4,335.67 crore absorbs the amalgamation deficit. For Shiva holders: shares in a larger, more liquid, institutionally-held entity; ₹133.92 crore of losses written off.

rationale.rationale: Management is demerging the Sugar Business of Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd. (PAIL) into Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL), a wholly owned subsidiary, so that PAIL becomes a pure-play premium alco-bev company; CFO Natwar Aggarwal framed it on the April 29, 2026 call as "we want to be a global alco-bev company and in that pursuit we want to focus on our core brand portfolio," with the scheme Board-approved April 28, 2026, filed with SEBI, KPMG as adviser, and completion envisaged in FY27. The stated intent is to pool human and capital resources behind the Alco-Bev portfolio (Indri single malt, Camikara rum, Cashmir vodka, Whistler blended whisky) and to list sugar — described as a "traditional heritage business" — as a separate entity rather than sell it. The economics behind it are visible in the numbers management cited: Alco-Bev revenue grew 42% to INR 908 crore (from INR 639 crore) with 31.5% EBITDA margins and 45–50% IMFL margins, while sugar was only INR 233.05 crore of turnover (20.53% of the listed entity) and dragged Q4 standalone EBITDA margin down ~300 bps as sugar's quarterly EBITDA margin collapsed from 11% to 2%; the segment tables show the sugar segment result at a loss of INR 904.62 lakh in FY26 versus a loss of INR 327.13 lakh in FY25, with sugar segment assets of INR 10,553.97 lakh against segment liabilities of INR 22,166.79 lakh. Management also repeatedly blamed sugar seasonality for making quarter-to-quarter margins hard to read. The scheme's own rationale (Annexure B) lists focused attention for each core business and the ability to attract required investment, greater business focus and enhanced shareholder value, more efficient use of financial resources, managerial talent, technical skills and marketing resources, value unlock "through price-discovery of the individual entities," the "right operating architecture" with sharper individual strategies and "clear capital allocation," and separately listed companies attracting a specific set of investors with financial flexibility and "stronger capital market outcomes." Mechanically it is a mirror listing: no cash consideration, 1 PFEL share of INR 10 for every 9 PAIL shares (ratio fixed on sugar's turnover and assets), PFEL's pre-scheme capital cancelled, no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern, producing "two listed companies with proportionate shareholding." No investor, lender or business partner is identified anywhere as having demanded the separation — it is presented as a management/Board decision, recommended by the Audit Committee and Independent Directors, alongside the unrelated FY27 agenda of INR 250–300 crore incremental Indri revenue, INR 300–400 crore from the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh plant, 60–70% growth and brand-side inorganic options.
rationale.evolution: Only one earnings call falls in the window, the FY26 call of April 29, 2026, and the demerger appears there already as a done decision rather than an idea being floated — announced in the CFO's opening remarks the day after the April 28, 2026 Board meeting approved the scheme and filed it with the exchanges/SEBI, with KPMG as partner and FY27 as the completion target. It resurfaced later in the same call only when Himanshu Shah of Dolat Capital pressed on intent (sell or separately list), drawing the explicit answer that sugar would be listed separately, not sold. The filings then track execution rather than rationale: the April 28, 2026 Regulation 30 outcome with the full Annexure B rationale, share entitlement ratio and sugar turnover of INR 233.05 crore (20.53%), the April 28, 2026 press release restating the pure-play framing, and the August 17, 2026 intimation of BSE/NSE no-adverse-observation letters dated August 14, 2026 (SEBI comments dated August 13, 2026) clearing the way for the NCLT petition. Earlier filings in the window (November–December 2025) concern only CCD and warrant conversions and never mention a separation.

rationale.rationale: Thomas Cook (India) Ltd (TCIL) is carving out its Resorts and Resort Management business — the six resorts it owns/operates directly under the Nature Trails brand, which it had itself absorbed from Nature Trails Resorts Pvt Ltd by slump sale for Rs 522.5 mn (appointed date 1 March 2025) — and demerging it into its wholly owned subsidiary Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd (SHRL), which will then be separately listed on BSE and NSE. Management's stated logic is twofold: operationally, the resorts "would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry" (SHRL ran 75+ resorts/3,700+ rooms at scheme date, 78 resorts/~3,800 rooms across 65 destinations by FY26-end, FY26 revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA INR 1,701 mn at 31%, PBT INR 1,142 mn at 21%, 25 straight profitable quarters, debt-free with ~INR 3,400 mn cash); and financially, the split is meant to "unlock value" and "attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment," leaving TCIL to "concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business." The demerged undertaking is tiny in revenue terms — INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, ~0.4% of TCIL standalone turnover — so the driver is structural, not scale: SHRL's board says it "has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry," with two listed entities each pursuing "growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics." Bolted onto the same composite scheme are three capital-structure fixes aimed squarely at EPS and optics: consolidating four Re 1 shares into one Rs 4 share (47,69,50,562 shares becoming 11,92,37,641) to "better reflect the true market value" and "convey stronger financial stability and valuation metrics"; absorbing three dormant subsidiaries — TC Visa Services (India), Jardin Travel Solutions and Borderless Travel Services — that are "incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs"; and cutting face value from Rs 4 to Rs 3 with no payout to "right size the balance sheet and capital structure." Consideration is 81 SHRL shares of Rs 10 for every 100 TCIL shares of Re 1, with no cash; TCIL keeps its existing SHRL shares (~7%), promoters end at 65.55% of SHRL and public at 32.30%. The initiative came from the Board on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and an Independent Directors Committee — no lender, partner or named investor demand is disclosed anywhere in the calls or filings, though analysts had repeatedly pressed management on deployment of the ~INR 780-800 crore net cash pile and on Sterling's EBIT failing to scale with its room additions.
rationale.evolution: Across the May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 calls there is no hint of a separation: the only structural move discussed is the opposite direction — the March 2025 slump sale pulling Nature Trails' three Mumbai-area resorts (80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crores revenue) into TCIL — while analysts push on cash use and on why Sterling's EBIT stayed flat at ~INR 129 crores despite adding 1,200-1,300 rooms, and on 6 February 2026 Mahesh Iyer still says "there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition." The Board then granted in-principle approval on 20 March 2026 and the full composite scheme (demerger, 4:1 consolidation, merger of three dormant subsidiaries, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 capital reduction) was announced that day. It was discussed on an earnings call for the first time on 13 May 2026, where Iyer framed it as a "strategic divestment"/value unlock, Vikram Lalvani confirmed "the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated," and Debasis Nandy reaffirmed the original 12-15 month timeline with completion expected by Q1 FY28. Execution then tracked that guidance without the plan itself changing: BSE no-adverse-observation on 31 August 2026, NSE no-objection on 1 September 2026, SHRL's registered office shifted from Tamil Nadu to Maharashtra effective 13 July 2026, and an NCLT Mumbai procedural order dated 4 November 2026 admitting the application and directing TCIL shareholder and unsecured-creditor meetings.

points.point: First earnings-call disclosure of the March 2026 board approval, framed as a strategic divestment of the resort business into Sterling that unlocks shareholder value.
points.quote: Before we move on to the segmental analysis, I will discuss the strategic divestment announcement that was made in March 2026, where the Board has granted in-principle approval for the demerger of our resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts.

points.point: Iyer's stated benefit for the remaining TCIL: a cleaner capital structure and resources concentrated on Travel and Financial Services (forex, corporate travel, MICE, DMS).
points.quote: For Thomas Cook (India) Limited, this restructuring allows us to streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business.

points.point: The face-value consolidation plus absorption of the three dormant subsidiaries is pitched explicitly as an EPS and corporate-structure simplification measure.
points.quote: The consolidation of our face value per share, along with the merger of the three dormant subsidiaries, further simplifies our corporate structure and improves our Earnings Per Share, directly benefiting our shareholders.

points.point: Lalvani places the demerger alongside Sterling's own next phase — brand re-architecture and expansion to 95 resorts/4,500 rooms in 2027 — as process already under way.
points.quote: In parallel, as you are aware, the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated.

points.point: Nandy gave the only timeline guidance: 12-15 months from board approval, NSE/BSE applications filed and queries being answered, completion expected Q1 FY28.
points.quote: So when we took the Board approval for this particular demerger project, we said that it will take us 12 to 15 months.

points.point: Sterling's readiness argument on the call: FY26 as an inflection year with revenue INR 5,487 mn, EBITDA 31%, PBT margin 21%, 25 consecutive profitable quarters and a debt-free balance sheet with ~INR 3,400 mn cash.
points.quote: FY '25-'26 marks a defining year for Sterling, a decisive inflection point where scale, profitability and balance sheet strength have expanded simultaneously, not sequentially.

points.point: Core operating rationale: the resorts belong with Sterling because Sterling has the hospitality operating expertise, catering to a different demographic with more curated experiences (adventure holidays, educational trips, corporate getaways).
points.quote: TCIL and SHRL's Management believes that the Resort Business of TCIL would reap more benefit from being owned and operated by SHRL in light of their vast expertise in the hospitality industry.

points.point: Sterling is presented as having outgrown subsidiary status and ready for its own listed existence in a fast-growing sector — the justification for subsequently listing SHRL on BSE and NSE.
points.quote: Further, SHRL's Management is of the view that SHRL has matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast-growing hospitality industry.

points.point: The value-unlock case is explicitly about attracting different investor bases to travel/financial services versus leisure hospitality, with each entity pursuing sector-specific growth strategies with agility.
points.quote: Unlock value for the shareholders of TCIL by demerging the Resorts and Resort Management business into SHRL and to attract differentiated investor cohorts for each business segment

points.point: Segregating verticals is expected to improve operating efficiency and profitability at both entities because each faces different industry dynamics.
points.quote: In this manner, the two listed entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability.

points.point: Scale of what is actually moving: the demerged undertaking's turnover was only INR 70 crores for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of TCIL's standalone turnover — six Nature Trails resorts.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.

points.point: Consideration is all-paper at 81:100, no cash; TCIL retains its existing SHRL stake, leaving promoters at 65.55% (including 7% held by TCIL) and public at 32.30% of SHRL.
points.quote: for every 100 (One Hundred only) equity shares of Thomas Cook (India) Limited of face value of INR 1/- each credited as fully paid up, the issue and allotment by Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of 81 (Eighty One only) equity shares of Sterling Holiday Resorts Limited of face value of INR 10/-each credited as fully paid up ("Share Entitlement Ratio").

points.point: Three dormant shells (TC Visa Services, Jardin Travel Solutions, Borderless Travel Services — FY25 turnover Rs 1.2 cr, nil and nil) are folded into TCIL purely to cut compliance and overhead and free management attention.
points.quote: TCVSL, JTSL and BTSL are dormant and non-operative companies, incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs.

points.point: The Rs 4-to-Rs 3 face-value reduction involves no payout to shareholders and no change in share count; it is a balance-sheet right-sizing aimed at EPS, and is stated not to prejudice creditors.
points.quote: The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed reduction of share capital is required to right size the balance sheet and capital structure of TCIL such that TCIL has a more efficient capital structure and the shareholders also benefit in terms of improved earnings per share.

points.point: The 4-into-1 share consolidation is justified on ratio optics — making reported per-share metrics reflect intrinsic value and signal financial stability.
points.quote: The Management of TCIL believes that the proposed consolidation of the face value of its equity shares will result in a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios.

points.point: Six weeks before the announcement, management told investors asking about the ~INR 1,000 crore gross cash pile that no cash-return or acquisition discussions were live — no separation was signalled on this call.
points.quote: But currently, there are no conversations around either any kind of disbursement of cash to shareholders or for that matter, any acquisition.

points.point: The opposite-direction precursor: in March 2025 TCIL bought the Nature Trails resorts business into itself by slump sale (three resorts near Mumbai, 80-90 rooms, INR 10-15 crores revenue) — the very undertaking now being demerged out to Sterling.
points.quote: We completed this, the slump sale in March. Now this actually includes 3 resorts close to Bombay.

points.point: Analyst pressure on Sterling's standalone performance versus listed hospitality peers, which Lalvani answered by citing the completed transformation from vacation-ownership to a hospitality model.
points.quote: But if you see, if you see the revenue, we are quite underperforming the industry.

points.point: Standing investor concern the separation does not address: Sterling's EBIT stayed around INR 129 crores for two years despite roughly 1,200-1,300 extra rooms, attributed to membership-revenue sunset, resort ramp-up lags and ROU depreciation.
points.quote: But our EBIT continues to actually be steady in terms of INR 129 crores over the last 2 years, in fact, a decline from FY '24.

rationale.what_management_expects: TCIL: streamlined capital structure, resources focused on travel and financial services, improved EPS from the 4:1 consolidation, Rs 4-to-Rs 3 reduction and dormant-subsidiary merger, lower admin cost. SHRL: separate listing on BSE/NSE, own growth path in fast-growing hospitality, hospitality-expert ownership of the resorts. Both: differentiated investor cohorts, sector-aligned strategies, improved operational efficiency and profitability.
rationale.gaps: No valuation methodology or derivation of the 81:100 ratio, no quantified value unlock or SHRL financials post-demerger, no accounting treatment of the capital reduction, no shareholder-vote or listing-date specifics.

rationale.rationale: HEGAM's separation is the "Composite Scheme of Arrangement" among HEG Advanced Materials Limited (formerly HEG Limited, the Demerged Company), HEG Limited (formerly HEG Graphite Limited, the Resulting Company) and Bhilwara Energy Limited (the Transferor Company): the legacy Graphite Undertaking — the graphite electrodes business, plus the overseas investment and the assets and liabilities of the TAWA power plant — was demerged into the Resulting Company on a going-concern basis with mirror shares issued to HEGAM shareholders, while Bhilwara Energy Limited was simultaneously amalgamated into HEGAM. As the filings present it, the purpose is to put the mature, cyclical electrodes business (FY26 revenue ₹2,568.50 crore, H1 FY27 ₹1,207.36 crore and PAT ₹192.33 crore, carrying ₹4,419.21 crore of segment assets and ₹1,245.85 crore of liabilities) in one listed vehicle, and leave HEGAM as a "technology-led, globally competitive advanced materials platform" spanning anode materials (TACC), graphene (HEG Graphene Materials), battery energy storage (Replus Engitech, 74% held) and green power. The amalgamation of Bhilwara Energy brings 278 MW of debt-free hydro (86 MW MPCL + 192 MW AD Hydro) plus 14 MW of wind into HEGAM, which the CFO says "provides a sound financial foundation for the Group" with "stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore" annually — i.e. the hydro cash flow and the ₹1,322.84 crore cash pile now sit against the heavy new-materials capex rather than against electrodes. The problem it solves is capital allocation and identity: HEGAM's board on 3 November 2026 approved a revised Phase-1 anode cost of ~₹2,350 crore (20,000 MT, COD June 2027, 61% built), a ₹1,606 crore Phase-2 to 44,000 MT by March 2029, a ₹475 crore crucible plant for "backward integration" and cost optimisation, and a ₹500 crore 500 MTPA graphene plant — none of which belong on an electrode balance sheet. The company also altered its main object clause to insert "Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and other allied material" (CIN changed from L23109MP1972PLC008290 to L35100MP1972PLC008290) and implemented an ESOP of up to 98,93,970 options, so each entity can be objected, incentivised and financed on its own. Leadership was split along the same line: Ravi Jhunjhunwala moved to Chairman, MD & CEO of the demerged HEG Limited (graphite), while Riju Jhunjhunwala leads HEGAM and has now taken the chair of MPCL and AD Hydro. A lender appears in the record on the power side: CYHPL bought Statkraft's 49% of MPCL on 17 November 2025 and intends to merge MPCL and ADHPL into itself "for consolidating the hydro power asstes of the group in the CYHPL in line with undertaking given by CYHPL to ICICI Bank."
rationale.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts were supplied, so the sequence can only be traced through filings: by 19 January 2026 the Scheme was already public enough to warrant an investor "Webinar on Update on Composite Scheme of Arrangement," and the 49% MPCL buy-out from Statkraft (SPA 9 September 2025, closed 17 November 2025) had pre-positioned the hydro assets. Shareholders approved it at the NCLT-convened meeting on 5 May 2026 with requisite majority; the NCLT Indore Bench sanctioned it on 13 August 2026; the board fixed 1 September 2026 as Effective Date (Appointed Date backdated to 1 April 2024) and allotted the new shares on 7 September 2026, lifting paid-up capital from ₹38.60 crore to ₹65.96 crore. Only after effectiveness did the plan visibly widen from "separate graphite" to "build out advanced materials": the 3 November 2026 board added Phase-2 anode (44,000 MT), crucibles, graphene, an ESOP and the new object clause, while on 29–30 October 2026 the object-clause CIN change was registered and HEGAM had to publish the unlisted Resulting Company's results on its behalf pending listing.

rationale.rationale: The separation at issue is the demerger of Lloyds Enterprises Limited's (LEL) Real Estate Business Undertaking into a new, separately listed vehicle, Lloyds Realty Limited (LRL), carried out inside a Composite Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230–232 read with Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013 that the Board approved on 22 December 2025; the same scheme first merges Lloyds Realty Developers Limited (LRDL, Transferor 1) and Indrajit Properties Private Limited (IPPL, Transferor 2) into LEL, so that all realty assets sit in one place before being carved out into LRL. The only rationale management itself states is in the Chairman's speech at the 40th AGM (9 July 2026): the merger-and-demerger scheme means 'our real estate business will be listed, unlocking its true potential and delivering greater value to shareholders', set against a realty platform spread across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Panvel, Khopoli, Dadar and Thane with 'nearly 14 million square feet of upcoming projects under development' — i.e. a capital-hungry pipeline that needs its own currency and price discovery. For the parallel group merger the Chairman gives the generic benefits: 'enhance operational efficiencies, optimize resource utilization, strengthen the overall business structure, and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders'. The filings show why real estate sat awkwardly inside LEL: for 9M FY26 the Real Estate segment did only ₹53.30 crore of revenue and ₹0.88 crore of segment result (down from ₹11.26 crore) on ₹993.09 crore of segment assets and ₹553.40 crore of segment liabilities, while Steel (₹492.80 crore revenue, ₹255.60 crore result) and Engineering (₹795.75 crore, ₹151.08 crore) carried the group, and subsidiary LRDL itself ran a ₹1.26 crore net loss; consolidated FY26 total income was ~₹2,200 crore against ~₹800 crore standalone, with LEL otherwise functioning as a holding/trading company (stakes of ~4.13% in Lloyds Metals and Energy, ~31% in Geomysore, and material subsidiary Lloyds Engineering Works with a group order book of ~₹8,000 crore and 44% PBT growth). No investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for the separation; the only parties on record demanding anything are the regulators — SEBI, NSE and BSE required LEL to disclose to shareholders the 'Need for the merger/demerger, rationale of the scheme and swap ratio', synergies, minority impact and a cost-benefit analysis, plus lender NOCs and 'Conditions imposed by lenders, if any'. The same unlock-by-listing logic recurs twice more in the group: LEWL's absorption of Lloyds Infra, Metalfab and Techno Industries to end 'silos' and create a ₹6,150 crore-order-book design-to-execution entity, and the SISCOL acquisition (88.12% for ~₹1,073.40 crore), where a DRHP within 30 months is meant to 'facilitate independent price discovery', market visibility and access to capital.
rationale.evolution: No earnings-call transcripts are on file, so the idea is traceable only through filings. It surfaces fully formed on 22 December 2025, when the Board approved the Composite Scheme (LRDL + IPPL into LEL, real-estate undertaking out into LRL) and filed it with BSE and NSE the same day; a week later (29 December 2025) the group announced the separate LEWL merger of LICL, Metalfab and Techno Industries, and the 9 February 2026 results notes restated the Scheme verbatim alongside a ₹500 crore NCD approval, the ₹361 crore Tata Capital/Bajaj Finance/Jio Credit borrowings and the block-deal sale of LEWL shares to Thriveni Earthmovers. On 15–16 May 2026 LEL received NSE's 'No objection' and BSE's 'no adverse observations' (with LRL's listing left to exchange discretion, an Information Memorandum, frozen shares and a 60-day post-NCLT listing timetable), followed on 18–19 May 2026 by exchange NOCs and CCI clearance for the LEWL merger; by the 9 July 2026 AGM the Chairman described the scheme as approved, an NCLT application filed, and the realty business as one that 'will be listed'.

rationale.rationale: This is not a sale but a three-way split by demerger: a Scheme of Arrangement approved by MSL's board (first on 22 May 2026, then re-approved 7 October 2026 with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026) carves two 'Demerged Undertakings' out of Maharashtra Seamless into two wholly owned subsidiaries that will themselves be listed on BSE and NSE. Demerged Undertaking 1 — the Mangaon, Maharashtra seamless pipe plant (125,000 MTPA) plus the 10 MW captive solar plant at Beed — goes to MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL); Demerged Undertaking 2 — the Narketpally, Telangana seamless mill (200,000 MTPA), the Khetusar (20 MW) and Pokhran (5 MW) solar plants in Rajasthan, and the rig Jindal Explorer — goes to United Seamless Limited (USL), i.e. the asset base MSL bought out of IBC as United Seamless Tubulaar for INR477 crores plus INR73 crores of reactivation capex. On FY2025-26 operational turnover the split is Undertaking 1 INR793 crores (16.98%), Undertaking 2 INR693 crores (14.84%) and the residual company (Nagothane pipes, ERW, treasury) INR3,185 crores (68.18%) of INR4,671 crores. The board's stated reasons are that the undertakings have 'distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration' — specifically three different mill technologies, CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon and FQM at Telangana, each needing its own modernization and technical expertise — so each should run as a focused, independently reported vertical. It also says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have 'different capital intensity and funding requirements', so splitting them allows better assessment of capital needs and more flexibility for expansion; the renewable plants are attached to the mills they can power; and the rig business, long described on calls as outside the core, is segregated because it has 'distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business'. No cash changes hands: shareholders get 1 share of INR5 in each resulting company for every 5 MSL shares, producing the same proportionate holding (promoter ~70.30%, public ~29.70%, 2,67,99,850 shares in each), which the filing calls 'value neutral'; creditor liabilities are neither reduced nor extinguished and travel with each undertaking. Notably, the nine earnings calls supplied — including Feb 2026, three months before the first board approval — contain no mention of a demerger at all; the only antecedents are repeated investor pressure to exit the rig and one shareholder's demand to split the company, and management's standing answer that it would continue 'in the steel pipe segment only' and that exit was 'for the Board to decide'.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced only as a rig exit: on the Feb 2024 call (30 Jan 2024) Chairman D.P. Jindal said of staying in rigs 'we have to take the appropriate decision at the right time', and on the Nov 2024 call (29 Oct 2024) an investor asked directly about demerging or selling the rig, to which management said it was something 'we want to do, but it is subject to Board approval'. Pressure widened over the next year: on the Feb 2025 call (28 Jan 2025) management personally agreed the rig-to-Jindal-Drilling structure 'doesn't look in line' with its governance clean-up, on the Jun 2025 call (27 May 2025) it confirmed 'there was a view of getting out of the rig business' with no board update, and on the Aug 2025 call (31 July 2025) a shareholder explicitly asked management to 'divide the company in two parts' — a holding company and a seamless company — and got only 'I don't have anything to add'. By the Nov 2025 call (5 Nov 2025) there was still 'no update on the proposal', and the Feb 2026 call (29 Jan 2026) discussed only cash conservation, treasury and a hunt for distressed acquisitions. The actual plan then appeared without any call commentary: board approval 22 May 2026, a 15 June 2026 notice that the Scheme was 'under further review', and a revised, re-approved Scheme on 7 October 2026 that widened it from a rig/holding split into a full three-way break-up of the three mills by technology, with 'related assets and liabilities' tightened to 'specified assets and liabilities' and 'mirror shareholding' restated as 'same proportionate shareholding'.

points.point: Two undertakings are carved out into two wholly owned subsidiaries, MSL Seamless Tubes Limited and United Seamless Limited, both to be listed, with an Appointed Date of 1 October 2026; the Mangaon 125,000 MTPA mill and the 10 MW Beed captive solar plant form Undertaking 1.

points.point: Undertaking 2 bundles the Telangana (Narketpally) 200,000 MTPA mill with the Rajasthan solar plants and the rig Jindal Explorer into United Seamless Limited — effectively re-separating the ex-United Seamless Tubulaar asset base and the rig in one entity.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 2: Seamless pipe manufacturing facility of the Demerged Company located at Narketpally, Telangana (200,000 MTPA), solar power plants at Khetusar (20 MW) & Pokhran (5MW) in Rajasthan, rig Jindal Explorer along with the specified assets and liabilities of Demerged Undertaking 2.

points.point: The headline justification is that one company holds businesses with nothing in common operationally — different geographies, products, technologies, customers and logistics — so each should be managed separately.
points.quote: The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.

points.point: The most concrete operating reason given is that the three mills run on three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management and modernization programme — which maps exactly onto the three-way split.
points.quote: The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.

points.point: Capital allocation is cited: pipes, drilling and renewables have different capital intensity, so separation is meant to let each assess and fund its own needs — relevant given the stalled INR852 crore capex plan and the INR350 crore Nagothane hot-mill upgrade never started.
points.quote: Efficient Capital Allocation: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.

points.point: The rig is singled out for segregation on the grounds that it is commercially unlike pipe manufacturing — the same objection investors had raised on calls for two years.
points.quote: Focused Development of Rig Operations: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.

points.point: The renewable plants are deliberately attached to the mills they sit beside rather than kept central, framed as energy-management efficiency and sustainability support for each business.
points.quote: The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.

points.point: Separate financial and operational reporting per entity is itself presented as a benefit — transparency and performance evaluation — which speaks to the calls where management refused to give product-wise or mill-wise margins.
points.quote: Improved Transparency and Value Creation: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.

points.point: No cash is paid; shareholders receive 1 INR5 share in each resulting company per 5 MSL shares, giving identical proportionate ownership (promoter 70.3008%, public 29.6992%, 2,67,99,850 shares each) and, the board says, value neutrality.
points.quote: The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.

points.point: Lenders are explicitly left untouched: no arrangement or compromise with creditors, liabilities travelling with each undertaking — i.e. the split is not presented as lender-driven or a debt restructuring.
points.quote: The liabilities towards the creditors of the Demerged Company and/or the Resulting Companies under the Scheme are neither being reduced nor being extinguished and the liabilities pertaining to the respective undertakings shall be assumed and discharged by the respective Resulting Companies in the ordinary course of business.

points.point: The plan was not stable: approved 22 May 2026, pulled back for review on 15 June 2026, and re-approved only on 7 October 2026 with tightened wording ('specified' rather than 'related' assets, 'same proportionate' rather than 'mirror' shareholding) and slightly revised indicative share counts (promoter 70.2784% to 70.3008%).

points.point: Six months before board approval, an analyst asked specifically about getting the Jindal Explorer rig off the books and was told there was no update, with the rig about to start a new ONGC contract.

points.point: On the last call before the first board approval, management described the future as cash conservation and opportunistic distressed acquisitions, with no mention of any restructuring, while defending the INR3,500 crore treasury against shareholders noting ~50% of market cap was cash.

points.point: The same call set out the economics of the Telangana asset that now forms United Seamless Limited: INR477 crores purchase plus INR73 crores reactivation, INR100-200 crores of EBITDA a year, and ~INR375 crores of tax saved from USTPL's INR1,500 crore-plus accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation.

No margin, cost, ROCE or valuation figures were given.
