listing.text: PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, LISTED — Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited trades since 2025-06-02 (NSE equity list); the parent keeps 44%

rationale.rationale: Across these texts Aegis is not demerging a division to its own shareholders — one filing states plainly "Yes, transaction is outside the Scheme of Arrangement" — it is carving its port terminalling business out of Aegis Logistics Ltd (ALL) into the Royal Vopak joint venture Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd (AVTL), IPO-ing it, and then migrating terminal assets into AVTL and its subsidiaries by slump sale; ALL retains Mumbai Liquid, Mumbai LPG, LPG/ammonia Distribution, Infrastructure Development (EPC), Sourcing and treasury. Management's stated reason is capital: the group is funding roughly USD 1.2 billion of gross capex (about INR 10,000 crores) by FY27 and a USD 5 billion pipeline to 2030 (including a non-binding INR 20,000 crore Vadhavan MoU, INR 1,675 crores at JNPA/J2, INR 525 crores per ammonia terminal), and Murad Moledina said the AVTL IPO's "primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy" — GATI being Gateway Access to India. The dilution problem is answered two ways: in Nov 2024 he argued equity infused into the JV "will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies," so rising minority interest is offset by interest savings; post-listing he called it EPS accretive because reinvested proceeds more than compensate for profit shared with minorities. The split is engineered so cash returns to the parent: ALL (or a 100% subsidiary) builds the assets and bills AVTL at arm's length with a ~20–25% margin — 30% on signing the framework agreement (INR 500 crores of the INR 1,675 crore J2 project) and 70% on completion — so "we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash," eliminated on consolidation but real at the standalone level, while ALL also keeps 44.71% of AVTL and management control, so AVTL is still consolidated line by line. Partner structure, not lender pressure, shapes it: Vopak dilutes equally alongside ALL; SEBI rules legally oblige a Phase-II equity infusion within three years; Itochu has taken 10% of Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Ltd with intent to reach 25%; L&T (Kandla green ammonia) and Hindustan Zinc (15-year ammonia take-or-pay) sit on the project side. Consolidation of stragglers followed — Haldia's Hindustan Aegis LPG (25,000 MT, HPCL contract to 2038) moved 75% into AVTL, with 51% sold by Aegis Gas for INR 701.6 crores, and the Pipavav ammonia terminal transferred to ATPL for INR 525 crores — and performance has been strong throughout: FY26 revenue INR 8,333 crores (+23%), normalised EBITDA INR 1,599 crores (+36%), PAT INR 1,107 crores (+41%), EPS 25.59, cash and investments ~INR 5,939 crores versus INR 150 crores in FY22, consolidated debt-to-equity 0.04 and no net debt.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced only as press speculation: on the Aug 2024 call (Jul 31, 2024) Murad Moledina refused to engage on an AVTL fundraise news item — "nothing finalized as of now" — and Anil Sarin used that call to lobby against it on behalf of minority holders, asking that capital instead be raised in the Holdco; the Nov 2024 call (Nov 19, 2024) opened by disclosing the DRHP had been filed the previous day, with Moledina declining detail ("We are not at liberty to talk as of now") beyond saying proceeds would repay debt and that dilution would be shared equally by both partners and done in two phases. By the Aug 2025 call (Aug 8, 2025) AVTL was listed (June 2025, INR 2,800 crores raised, ALL at 44.71%) and the rationale was given formally — debt reduction, GATI, EPS accretion, Phase-II infusion legally due within three years — plus the first slump sales (Sea Lord's Mangalore terminal, business transfer agreements of Jun 19, 2025) and the rule that "most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak." Thereafter it became mechanical: Nov 2025 (Nov 7) and the Oct 28–29, 2025 filings moved Hindustan Aegis LPG and Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) into AVTL (INR 701.6 crores for 51%; ALL retaining 34% indirectly, offset by ~INR 700 crores cash), Feb 2026 (Jan 30, 2026) defined the parent's remaining six businesses, the Mar 26 / Aug 24, 2026 filings assigned and executed the INR 525 crore ammonia BTA to ATPL, and the Jun 2026 call (Jun 9, 2026) plus the Sep 28, 2026 board approval of INR 6,000 crores of borrowing limits and INR 6,000 crores of fundraising confirmed the steady state: ALL builds and funds, AVTL owns.

points.point: Investor Anil Sarin explicitly lobbied against separately listing AVTL, saying minority holders would be confused about which entity to own and that capital should instead be raised in the listed Holdco; management called the discussion premature.
points.quote: it would be so much better if you retain that in the consolidated hold and raise money in the Holdco.

points.point: Asked directly about press reports of an AVTL IPO, the CFO would not confirm it, framing it only as one of several ways to fund the capex programme.
points.quote: As far as the second news item is concerned, I can tell you, we always explore many possibilities of funding our capex program and nothing finalized as of now.

points.point: On the day after the DRHP was filed, the CFO gave the core defence of the structure: equity raised in the subsidiary repays infrastructure debt, so interest savings offset the increase in minority interest and the holdco is left unaffected.
points.quote: We have already said earlier that the equity infusion into the JV will be value accrued into the holdco because we are eliminating interest cost which is a very high cost for infrastructure companies.

points.point: The Chairman stated the stated use of IPO proceeds — debt reduction plus general corporate purposes — while an investor asked whether the listed parent would simply become a holdco since the bulk of the business was moving into the JV.
points.quote: The capital raise in AVTL will help the company reduce a certain portion of the outstanding debt and also some portion helped fund other general corporate purposes.

points.point: Post-listing (AVTL listed June 2025, ALL holding 44.71% with management control, so still consolidated line by line), the CFO gave the formal rationale and said reinvested proceeds would more than compensate for profit now shared with minorities.
points.quote: The primary objective was to reduce debt and strengthen the balance sheet enabling us to seize future growth opportunities and continue our GATI strategy.

points.point: The Chairman tied the separation to a regulatory obligation: a second equity infusion into AVTL is mandated within three years under SEBI rules, which he said largely funds the USD 1.2 billion-to-USD 5 billion capex plan at 0.6x gearing capped at 3.5x EBITDA.
points.quote: With the recently concluded Phase-I equity infusion by way of the IPO and as you know we are legally obliged to have a Phase-II equity infusion within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations, the Capex therefore will be largely funded.

points.point: The allocation rule between parent and AVTL was stated: standard port terminals go into AVTL under the GATI strategy, while other assets (e.g. the INR 250 crore Mumbai liquid expansion) stay in the parent, decided case by case on where value is maximised and whether partners are involved.
points.quote: But yes, most of the standard port terminals will be housed under the strategy GATI in Aegis Vopak, for sure.

points.point: Explaining the Haldia/Hindustan Aegis consolidation into AVTL, the CFO quantified the trade: holding drops from 51% to an indirect 34%, but roughly INR 700 crores of cash more than offsets the 17 points, and it lifts the subsidiary's EPS.
points.quote: The 17% that drops is compensated by the surplus INR 700 crores, whatever is going to come in our hands.

points.point: The cash mechanics of the two-entity structure were spelled out for a shareholder worried that the USD 5 billion capex benefits only AVTL: the parent builds at ~25% margin, is reimbursed in full plus margin, and also earns via its AVTL stake.
points.quote: So, for AVTL, if we develop, then obviously, AVTL pays for the entire amount, including our margin. So, we recover back whatever we have spent and the margin remains in cash.

points.point: Asked what is left in Aegis Logistics outside AVTL, the CFO enumerated the retained perimeter — and added that ammonia distribution is being added to it alongside LPG.
points.quote: So we have Mumbai Liquid. We have Mumbai LPG. We have Distribution. We have Infrastructure Development. We have Sourcing and we have treasury.

points.point: The steady-state operating model was confirmed: capex is incurred and the asset built at Aegis Logistics standalone (or a 100% subsidiary), billed as EPC, then transferred to Aegis Vopak, with consolidation capitalised at ALL's billed cost.
points.quote: So, we will be doing capex at the Aegis level, the Aegis Logistics. And then after creating the asset, will we then transfer it to Aegis Vopak, am I right?

points.point: The Aug 24, 2026 Business Transfer Agreement transferred the 36,000 MT Pipavav ammonia terminal to Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited by slump sale for INR 525 crores, and states the transaction sits outside any Scheme of Arrangement and is a related-party transaction at arm's length.
points.quote: The Transfer of storage terminal for Ammonia to ATPL will consolidate the terminalling services under the Group, enabling operational synergy.

points.point: The Oct 29, 2025 board approval priced the Haldia step: 6,21,146 shares (51%) of Hindustan Aegis LPG sold by wholly-owned Aegis Gas (LPG) Pvt Ltd to AVTL, an entity contributing 2.49% of turnover and 10.07% of net worth in FY25.
points.quote: The consideration to be received by AGPL against the sale of 6,21,146 Equity shares held by AGPL in HALPG from AVTL is  INR.7,01,60,71,920/-

points.point: A year after the AVTL IPO the parent itself moved to raise capital: the Sep 28, 2026 board approved raising borrowing limits to INR 6,000 crores and a fundraise of up to INR 6,000 crores via equity, FCCB/ADR/GDR, debentures or QIP, subject to shareholder special resolution.
points.quote: raising of funds for an amount aggregating up to Rs. 6,000 Crores, for cash, in one or more tranches

rationale.what_management_expects: AVTL: debt repaid, balance sheet strengthened, ~25% EBITDA on matured assets, terminals consolidated for operational synergy, partner capital from Vopak and Itochu. Aegis Logistics: upfront 20–25% EPC margin returned in cash, 44.71% of AVTL plus management control and line-by-line consolidation, high-return distribution/sourcing/treasury retained, EPS accretion, 0.6x gearing, and funding for USD 5 billion of capex to 2030.
rationale.gaps: No stated valuation of retained versus transferred businesses, no answer to the which-entity-to-own dilution objection, no Phase-II infusion size, terms or timing, no lender rationale.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is GAIL's own directly-authorised city gas distribution (CGD) retail business — the six geographical areas Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum (Jamshedpur), Cuttack and Khordha (Bhubaneswar) — which the Board resolved to hive down into its 100% subsidiary GAIL Gas Limited as a slump sale on a going-concern basis, effective 01.01.2027, with the subsidiary then to be listed via IPO diluting up to 25% of GAIL's equity. Management's stated reason was structural, not financial distress: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta said it was 'in order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach' — i.e. GAIL group CGD was split across GAIL's own balance sheet (six GAs, 0.36–0.55 MMSCMD, 195→215 CNG stations and 3.53→4.64 lakh DPNG connections over FY25–Q3FY26, volumes up ~25% in FY25 but 'currently in their early stages of development'), GAIL Gas (16 GAs plus 9 JVs, 7.0→7.8 MMSCMD, 12.46 lakh DPNG connections, 674 CNG stations, FY25 turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore up 42%, PAT Rs 451 crore up 40%) and 72 group GAs in all. A pipeline-and-marketing parent was also an awkward owner of a retail business: management said 'we are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies', and segment reporting of the CGD/marketing split was itself confusing analysts (the Rs 400 crore standalone-to-consolidated regrouping queried in Jul 2025). The upside case cited was CGD demand: a PNGRB projection of consumption rising '2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY 24' (~15% CAGR), PNGRB capping CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion lowering CGD input costs. For the IPO, the argument was scale and timing — 'GAIL Gas is one of the biggest company in the country in terms of city gas distribution... now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas' — with a consultant already selected and a roughly one-year timeline. The impetus came largely from sell-side investors (Citi's Saurabh Handa on restructuring CGD investments in Nov 2024; Alliance Services' Balaji Das on the IPO consultant in Oct 2025); the only external consent management named was CCEA, 'since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA' — no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. Running in the opposite direction, GAIL simultaneously pulled Konkan LNG Limited in: it bought out MSEB Holding's 7,40,55,220 shares via a NCLT-approved capital reduction (paid 06.07.2026, GAIL to 100%) and then merged KLL (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into GAIL to 'create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure'.
rationale.evolution: The idea first surfaced only as an unprompted analyst question on the Nov 06, 2024 Q2 FY25 call, where R.K. Jain said no call had been taken on restructuring GAIL Gas — 'this is in our mind, but nothing concrete' — while adding that GAIL was 'looking for listing one or two JVs'; the Jan 30, 2025 call did not touch it. It became concrete at the May 14, 2025 annual analyst meet, where the CMD disclosed the Board's recommendation (passed 13.05.2025) to transfer the six GAs to GAIL Gas for a 'single entity... retail focused business approach', subject to CCEA. On Oct 31, 2025 the second leg appeared: GAIL confirmed it had started the GAIL Gas listing process, had selected a consultant, and expected 'a one year time line or so'; the Feb 02, 2026 Q3 FY26 call was silent on both. The filings then executed it: 31.07.2026 KLL merger into GAIL, and 30.10.2026 Board approval of the six-GA slump sale effective 01.01.2027 plus in-principle approval of a GAIL Gas IPO diluting up to 25%.

points.point: Citi's Saurabh Handa raised the split of CGD investments between GAIL standalone and GAIL Gas and asked whether GAIL would restructure them — the first time the idea appears in the record.
points.quote: On your City Gas investments, whether they are at the standalone entity or in GAIL Gas? Is there any thought process to look at restructuring these streamline these investments?

points.point: Director (Finance) R.K. Jain confirmed restructuring was under internal consideration but that no decision existed, while separately flagging that GAIL was working on listing one or two JVs with an update promised in Q3.
points.quote: As a company about GAIL Gas has not yet taken any call for restructuring of GAIL Gas. This is in our mind, but nothing concrete I can share with you right now.

points.point: Alongside CGD restructuring, Jain said listing of group entities was already in progress and at 'a good stage', promising an update in Q3 FY25.
points.quote: So also, we are looking for listing one or two JVs, which we are in the process and once we move forward and we take a call, we'll come back to you, but that we are certainly working and we are in a good stage.

points.point: CMD Sandeep Kumar Gupta disclosed the Board's 13.05.2025 recommendation to transfer GAIL's six directly-held CGD geographical areas to wholly-owned GAIL Gas Limited — the core rationale being one single, synergistic, retail-focused CGD entity.
points.quote: In order to have a single entity for development of GAIL's CGD business and for bringing business synergy, efficiency and retail focused business approach, the Board has recommended to transfer six geographical areas of GAIL to its wholly owned subsidiary, GAIL Gas Limited.

points.point: The only approval condition management named was CCEA, because the six GAs (Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack) had been awarded to GAIL by CCEA rather than won by GAIL Gas.
points.quote: This is subject to approval of CCEA since these six GAs were authorized to GAIL by CCEA.

points.point: The six GAs were described as early-stage but fast-growing (volumes up ~25% in FY25, then ~0.4–0.45 MMSCMD) and under continuous cost review — the sub-scale retail assets being pushed into the dedicated CGD vehicle.
points.quote: In the Financial Year 24-25, these six GAs have shown impressive growth with volumes increasing by approximately 25%. We are constantly reviewing these CGDs to optimize costs and enhance efficiencies.

points.point: The growth case for a standalone CGD entity rested on PNGRB's demand projection, supplemented by PNGRB's proposal to cap CNG/domestic-PNG tariffs at Zone 1 and expected GST inclusion to cut CGD input costs.
points.quote: the CGD sector is anticipated to be the key driver of growth, with consumption expected to increase 2.5 times to 3.5 times by 2030 and 6 times to 7 times by 2040 from the baseline of approximately 37 MMSCMD in FY '24

points.point: GAIL Gas's own FY25 numbers framed the receiving entity as a scaled, improving business: turnover Rs 12,231 crore, PBT Rs 615 crore (+42%), PAT Rs 451 crore (+40%), 16 GAs owned plus 9 JVs.
points.quote: During the current financial year, that is FY '25, GAIL Gas Limited's turnover stood at Rs. 12,231 crores as against Rs. 10,944 crores in FY '24. PBT increased by 42% and stood at Rs. 615 crores as against Rs. 434 crores in FY '24.

points.point: On the other entity later consolidated in, management said Konkan LNG (Dabhol) would swing to profit once the all-weather breakwater let it run 34–36 cargoes versus 21, worth roughly Rs 300 crore.
points.quote: So this year certainly we were not in positive because of the breakwater issue. But going forward, we will have positive bottom line from KLL.

points.point: An investor (Balaji Das) pressed on the GAIL Gas IPO and the consultant being hired for listing analysis, confirming the second leg of the plan was investor-driven.
points.quote: And the second question is on, we had like on the listing of the GAIL Gas IPO actually. So, any further progress on consultant and when are the future plans actually for GAIL Gas actually, because we heard that we are hiring consultants for analysis of listing.

points.point: Jain confirmed the listing process had begun — consultant selected, order imminent — and justified it on GAIL Gas's scale: 7.72 MMSCMD of volume and more GAs than any peer, with Bangalore alone at 1 MMSCMD.
points.quote: And we in GAIL believe that now is high time that we started the process of listing GAIL Gas, in that regard we have already started the process of hiring of consultant.

points.point: He put a roughly one-year timeline on the listing, contingent on the consultant's study — the only timing guidance given on the IPO.
points.quote: So, we are on a path to study about listing of GAIL Gas and after conclusion of that study, certainly that study is very important for us, we expect a one year time line or so should be good enough.

points.point: The last call in the record discussed the six GAs and GAIL Gas purely operationally (0.55 MMSCMD, 215 CNG stations, 4.64 lakh DPNG; GAIL Gas 7.8 MMSCMD, PBT Rs 143 crore) with no mention of the transfer or the IPO.
points.quote: GAIL has direct authorization of 6 GAs and has an infrastructure of 215 CNG stations and 4.64 lakh DPNG connections.

(wholly owned Subsidiary of GAIL) through slump sale by Execution of Business Transfer Agreement on going concern basis, with effective date of transfer as 01.01.2027.

points.quote: accorded in-principle approval for Listing of shares of GAIL Gas Limited, (a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL) (GGL) on the Indian stock exchanges through Initial Public Offering (IPO) route by diluting GAIL's equity in GGL upto 25%.

points.point: Filing 31.07.2026: in the opposite direction, GAIL approved absorbing wholly-owned Konkan LNG (FY26 turnover Rs 741 crore, versus GAIL's Rs 1,41,483 crore) into itself under Section 233, with KLL's shares cancelled and no change in GAIL's shareholding.
points.quote: To create a larger and stronger vertically integrated entity, simplify and rationalize group structure which will enhance operational efficiencies.

points.point: Filing 10.07.2026: the KLL merger was preceded by an NCLT-approved capital reduction (order 03.06.2026) buying out partner MSEB Holding, taking GAIL from 50% to 100% of Konkan LNG before the absorption.
points.quote: an aggregate of 14,81,10,440 equity shares of ₹10 each, including 7,40,55,220 equity shares held by GAIL and 7,40,55,220 equity shares held by MSEB in KLL stand cancelled and extinguished i.e. MSEB holding in KLL reduced to Nil and GAIL shareholding increased to 100% of the equity share capital of KLL.

listing.text: PARTIAL SPIN-OFF, IPO DRHP FILED — Indian Gas Exchange Limited; At the IEX Analyst Meet held July 24, 2026 the CFO said "the good part is that they filed the DRHP in this month and hopefully (would be) getting listed soon";

rationale.rationale: The separation here is not a demerger of IEX's own operations but the carve-out of its gas arm, Indian Gas Exchange (IGX), via an offer-for-sale IPO, driven purely by PNGRB's exchange ownership rules, which cap any single shareholder at 25% and any trading member at 5%. IEX held 47.3%-47.5% of IGX and had to cut that to 25% within five years; that five-year window expired in December 2025, so IEX took a one-year extension from PNGRB, now running to 31 December 2026. Management said the original slippage was commercial, not strategic: 'there were huge challenges in the gas market and gas exchange' and the 'business ramp-up has not happened at the rate at which we were expecting it' (Nov 2025). With IGX now scaled - FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28% YoY, over 40% CAGR), PAT Rs 41.9-42 crore (+35%), roughly 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of the spot market, 23 delivery points versus 4 in FY22 and 10 contract types versus 6 - IEX chose the IPO over other divestment options and formally asked IGX to proceed. The DRHP was filed on 14 July 2026 with SEBI and BSE as a pure offer for sale of up to 16,710,000 shares by IEX, i.e. the 22.3% it must shed; no fresh issue, proceeds or valuation was discussed. The same ownership-cap logic makes IEX house each new commodity in its own company: Indian Coal Exchange Ltd was incorporated in June 2026 with board approval, a mineral exchange company is planned, and its shareholding rules are 'similar to what has been notified for the power exchange and the gas exchange.' The only parties asking for the separation were regulators (PNGRB; the Ministry of Coal rules for the coal exchange) - not investors, lenders or partners; investors asked only about timing and for a proportionate reservation in the IGX IPO, which Goel refused because it is 'an independent IPO'. Separately, management rejected the analyst suggestion that the exchange's clearing and settlement function must be hived into its own entity, saying the PSS Act requires registration, not separation, with no financial impact.
rationale.evolution: The idea surfaced on the Nov 2025 call (31 Oct 2025), where Goel disclosed the 25% PNGRB deadline of December 2025, blamed the slow gas-market ramp-up for the delay, said the regulator had assured an extension (IEX asked for eighteen months), and that IEX was 'considering different options for divestment'. By the Feb 2026 call (30 Jan 2026) the option had narrowed to an IPO: IEX had asked IGX to proceed, targeting completion within the year subject to SEBI clearance. On the Apr 2026 call (24 Apr 2026) the extension was confirmed to 31 December 2026 and the process was 'progressing well'. The DRHP followed on 14 July 2026, and at the Jul 2026 analyst meet (24 Jul 2026) Goel sized it as a 22.3% sell-down while also disclosing that Indian Coal Exchange Ltd had been incorporated in June 2026 as a separate company.

points.point: First disclosure of the mandated sell-down: IEX's 47.5% stake in IGX must fall to 25% by December 2025 under PNGRB regulations, with an extension requested (one and a half years asked) and the regulator supportive.
points.quote: As per the PNGRB regulations, we have to bring down the equity to 25% by December 2025.

points.point: Reason the deadline could not be met on the original schedule was weak gas-exchange ramp-up, and the route was still undecided at this point.
points.quote: So we have applied to PNGRB and the regulator was quite supportive, and they have assured that they will give time extension. And we are also working out option s, we are considering different options for divestment and complying with the regulatory provisions.

points.point: Goel attributed the shortfall explicitly to gas market conditions rather than any strategic choice.
points.quote: because in the past, there were huge challenges in the gas market and gas exchange. The business ramp -up has not happened at the rate at which we were expecting it.

points.point: The divestment route is fixed as an IPO; IEX directs its associate to execute it, with timing dependent on SEBI clearances.
points.quote: As far as IPO is concerned, basically, as per the regulations, our holding in the gas exchange is 47.5% and w e have to bring it out to 25% as per regulations. So , we have requested IGX to proceed with the IPO for this.

points.point: The PNGRB extension is confirmed as running to end-December 2026, setting the hard deadline for the sell-down.
points.quote: PNGRB has given us time up to 31st of December 2026.

points.point: Process underway but CMD gave no detail on status, pricing or structure.
points.quote: I think IGX IPO process is we have initiated the process.

points.point: The filing confirms the structure: a pure offer for sale by IEX of up to 16,710,000 IGX shares, no fresh issue, filed with SEBI and BSE on 14 July 2026.
points.quote: The Offer comprise s of an offer for  sale of up to 16,710,000 equity shares by IEX, and remains  subject to receipt of applicable approvals, market conditions, and other relevant considerations .

points.point: Goel quantifies the stake being sold - 22.3% of IGX, taking IEX from 47.3% to the 25% regulatory ceiling - and ties it directly to the expired five-year PNGRB window.
points.quote: As you may be aware that we have already filed a DRHP (Draft Red Herring Prospectus) for IPO of IGX as we today hold 47.3% in IGX.

points.point: The compliance driver and the one-year extension are restated as the sole rationale for the share sale.
points.quote: In fact, this 5 -year period was over in the month of December 2025. So , we took an extension of one year from the PNGRB. And therefore, to sell this 22.3% equity, we have offered that in the IPO.

points.point: An investor (Paresh Sanghani) asked for a proportionate reservation of IGX shares for IEX shareholders; Goel refused, treating IGX as a standalone issuer, and offered a buyback instead.
points.quote: The IGX IPO is an independent IPO, but buyback , yes definitely , we will consider it in future because now SEBI also has revised its rules for doing the buyback through the market .

points.point: IGX's scale-up is presented as what makes the listing viable: 76.8 million MMBtu at over 40% CAGR and Rs 42 crore profit, within consolidated FY26 PAT of Rs 493 crore (IEX standalone Rs 474 crore).
points.quote: it was a very new concept when it was started in 2019 and it reached with CAGR growth of over 40% a volume of 76.8 million MM Btu and reported profit of 42 crores .

points.point: The same separate-entity logic is applied to new commodities: a dedicated coal exchange company was incorporated with board approval in June 2026, with a mineral exchange company to follow.
points.quote: And we with the approval of the (IEX) B oard have al ready incorporated Indian Coal Exchange Ltd – a separate company for this purpose .

points.point: Why each exchange must be a separate company with diluted ownership: identical shareholding caps apply across power, gas and coal exchanges.
points.quote: Nobody can hold more than 25 percent, and no trading member can hold more than 5% .

points.point: Management explicitly rejected a second possible separation - hiving off clearing and settlement into its own entity - saying the PSS Act demands registration, not a separate company, with no financial impact.
points.quote: There is no question of any separation because this narrative is coming where SEBI requires the separation of the clearing and settlement function for the stock exchanges .

rationale.what_management_expects: Compliance first: IEX falls to 25% of IGX, keeping an associate stake in a business they expect to grow volumes 25-30% annually as gas prices fall; IGX gets its own listing and price. Each new commodity (coal, minerals) sits in its own company under the same 25%/5% ownership caps. No margin, capital or valuation benefit for IEX was claimed.
rationale.gaps: No price band, valuation, IGX stake-sale proceeds or gain, no post-IPO accounting/control impact, no use of cash, and no plan if the 31 December 2026 deadline is missed.

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is NLC India Ltd's renewable energy (solar/wind) portfolio, carved out of the lignite-mining and thermal-power parent into NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary. The filings state the reason explicitly as policy-driven monetisation, not a strategic idea originated by management: the 31.10.2025 intimation says the hive-off of 7 RE assets totalling 1,430 MW is 'under Asset Monetization Plan approved by the Ministry of Coal, Administrative Ministry', and the Q2 FY27 accounts repeat that it is 'In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal'. Scale cited: the 7 assets earned Rs 701.61 crore of revenue in FY25 (4.59% of consolidated revenue of Rs 15,282.96 crore) but carried net worth of Rs 3,869.26 crore (20.67% of owners' equity of Rs 18,722.97 crore) — i.e. a capital-heavy, low-revenue block being moved off the parent's balance sheet at book value, with consideration by equity shares/acknowledgement of debt, and Government of India approval already received. Execution was phased: Phase I (1,430 MW) transferred w.e.f. 01.01.2026; a second addendum dated 03.09.2026 added 708.96 MW (including a 4 MW green hydrogen project, assets at various stages of construction/operation) for Rs 853.97 crore, contributing only Rs 41.16 crore of FY26 revenue (0.24%) and Rs 925.08 crore of net worth (4.30%). The separate vehicle is visibly being used to raise third-party capital and partners that the parent could not house: a maiden green loan with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation of JPY 15.464 billion (USD 100 million) under the ECB framework 'to fund renewable energy projects through its subsidiary NIRL', a PTC India JV for 2,000 MW, an OREDA MoU/JV, a DIPAM-approved JV with MAHAPREIT, an SJVNL 200 MW wind PPA and an NCRTC LoA for 110 MW captive solar — now sitting as step-down subsidiaries NARL, NRRL, NNRL, NORL and NPRL. The end state is a listing: the Board gave in-principle approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026 and on 04.11.2026 approved an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each held by NLCIL in NIRL as part of NIRL's proposed IPO, after NLCIL injected a further Rs 2,000 crore of equity on 12.10.2026 taking its NIRL investment to Rs 5,119.75 crore.
rationale.evolution: The seven earnings calls tagged Feb 2024, Aug 2024, Nov 2024, Feb 2025, May 2025, Aug 2025 and Feb 2026 (held 10.02.2026) contain no extractable transcript text — six are scanned images and the Feb 2026 item is only the covering letter — so the idea cannot be traced call by call from these documents. From the filings the sequence is: in-principle approval for the Business Transfer Agreement to hive off the RE assets on 07.08.2025 (referenced in the 31.10.2025 intimation), BTA signed 31.10.2025 for 7 assets/1,430 MW under the Ministry of Coal's Asset Monetization Plan, transfer effected 01.01.2026, in-principle Board approval for listing NIRL on 12.01.2026, an addendum on 03.09.2026 adding 708.96 MW plus a 4 MW green hydrogen project, and OFS/IPO approval on 04.11.2026. The plan therefore widened from a one-off intra-group asset transfer at book value into a phased carve-out plus an IPO of the subsidiary, with the scope growing to include under-construction and green-hydrogen assets and five new partner-funded step-down subsidiaries.

points.point: The separation is a Ministry of Coal-mandated monetisation: 7 renewable assets of 1,430 MW hived off from NLCIL to wholly owned subsidiary NIRL under the approved Asset Monetization Plan, with Government of India approval already obtained.
points.quote: we write to inform that the Company has entered into a Business Transfer Agreement with NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company on 31st October, 2025, for proposed Hived off of the 7 Renewable Energy Assets with total Capacity of 1,430 MW from the Company to its Wholly Owned Subsidiary, NIRL, under Asset Monetization Plan approved by the Ministry of Coal, Administrative Ministry.

points.point: The disclosed economics show a capital-heavy, low-revenue block: 4.59% of consolidated revenue but 20.67% of owners' equity, transferred at book value with consideration in shares or acknowledgement of debt.

points.point: Q2 FY27 accounts restate the driver as the National Monetization Pipeline and set out the two-phase mechanics, Phase II being 708.96 MW for Rs 853.97 crore under a second addendum.
points.quote: In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) with NLC India Renewables Limited on 31st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy assets.

points.point: The end-point is an IPO of NIRL with NLCIL selling down: OFS of up to 10 crore shares approved on 04.11.2026, following in-principle listing approval on 12.01.2026.

points.point: Lenders and partners are transacting with the subsidiary, not the parent: a maiden offshore green loan of JPY 15.464 billion (USD 100 million) from SMBC under the ECB framework is explicitly routed through NIRL.
points.quote: Signed its maiden Green Loan agreement with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) under the ECB framework , amounting to JPY 15.464 billion (USO 100 million), to fund renewable energy projects through its subsidiary NIRL.

points.point: NIRL has become the JV platform for state and PSU partners (PTC India 2,000 MW, OREDA, MAHAPREIT with DIPAM approval, SJVNL 200 MW wind PPA, NCRTC 110 MW captive solar), now held as step-down subsidiaries.
points.quote: NIRL signed a JV agreement with PTC India Ltd, for development of 2000 MW of green energy capacity and formation of JV company is in progress.

points.point: The parent is funding the vehicle ahead of the IPO, taking its NIRL equity to Rs 5,119.75 crore, while renewables segment assets roughly doubled to Rs 10,881.76 crore from Rs 5,470.15 crore a year earlier.
points.quote: The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 2,000 crore on 12th October 2026.

points.point: The structure deliberately avoids a merger/demerger scheme: it is a related-party slump sale at book value between holding company and wholly owned subsidiary, so Regulation 37A does not apply.
points.quote: No amalgamation/ merger is envisaged. Hence compliance w.r.t. Regulation 37A of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, is not applicable as the transaction is being entered between the Company and its Wholly Owned Subsidiary i.e. NIRL.

rationale.what_management_expects: Not stated in words. The documents imply only: a dedicated, separately capitalised renewables vehicle (NIRL equity Rs 5,119.75 crore) able to raise third-party green debt (SMBC USD 100 million ECB) and partner equity via JVs with PTC, OREDA, MAHAPREIT, SJVNL and NCRTC, monetising assets per the Ministry of Coal plan and realising value through an NIRL IPO/OFS, leaving NLCIL focused on mining and thermal.
rationale.gaps: No call transcripts were extractable, so no management commentary, margin, valuation, capital-allocation or focus rationale; IPO size, pricing, timing, use of proceeds and residual NLCIL stake are unstated.

segments.measure_notes: Revenue = 'External Sales' for the Power - Renewable segment (consolidated Ind AS 108 segment note); the segment has no inter-segment sales, so External Sales = Total Revenue. Operating_profit = 'Segment Result', defined in the quarterly statement as Profit(+)/Loss(-) before tax and interest from each segment (i.e. segment EBIT before finance cost, other income and unallocable corporate expenses) — it is NOT EBITDA and NOT PBT. The 'Operating Profit' line in the segment note (FY2026 ₹3,747.90 cr; FY2025 ₹3,732.56 cr) is group-level after other income and unallocable expenses, not segment-level. No segment-level PAT is disclosed.

judge.what_is_spun: STL's Global Services Business (system integration / services arm), demerged out of Sterlite Technologies into a separate company
judge.reason: Not stated in the scheme filing; on the Jul 2026 call management said it had "consciously chosen to exit, sell off or shut down many businesses" and demerged system integration to be "very, very focused on the optical fibre cable connectivity side"
judge.insiders: Not stated for STL Networks. In the parent, promoter Twin Star Overseas Limited held 42.90%, rising to 47.75% fully diluted on exercise of 4,53,00,000 warrants at Rs.110; ultimate beneficial owner Mr. Anil Agarwal
judge.hidden_value: Leaves a pure-play optical parent: Q2 FY27 record revenue INR 2,529 Cr, EBITDA INR 846 Cr, PAT INR 517 Cr, order book INR 35,274 Cr, net debt-free, CRISIL AA/Stable. Any Kakinada writ contingent gain now belongs to STL Networks, not STL
judge.selling_pressure_why: Documents give no size, shareholding, index or float details for STL Networks Limited
judge.listing_timeline: No listing date stated; the August 21, 2026 filing says the demerger was "effective from the close of business hours on March 31, 2025" under the NCLT Mumbai order dated February 14, 2025, and that STL Networks Limited "has filed a requisite disclosure ... on BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited on August 20, 2026"

rationale.rationale: The business being separated is STL's Global Services (system integration / network-deployment) business, demerged out of Sterlite Technologies Limited (STLTECH) into a separate listed entity, STL Networks Limited, rebranded 'Invenia', leaving STL as a pure optical business (optical fibre, fibre cable, specialty cable, optical connectivity) plus the small STL Digital IT-services arm. Management's stated reason was portfolio simplification and focus: Ankit Agarwal said on the May 2025 call that the demerger 'aligns with our goal of portfolio simplification and sets the stage for focused growth in each of the businesses,' and in Jul 2026 placed it in a multi-year clean-up in which STL exited, sold or shut down wireless solutions, OSS/BSS, active components and other businesses to be 'very, very focused on the optical fiber cable connectivity side.' The second reason was capital and working-capital drag: the services business was a project business with large net fund involvement, and on the Jan 2025 call management's stated priority for it was 'select projects intake to improve the profitability and optimize the net fund involvement,' with Tushar Shroff conceding receivables and contract assets in state-government projects like T-Fiber and MahaNet were liquidating slower than planned because they depended on state budgetary allocation. The scale difference management cited: Global Services did INR 289 crores of revenue in Q3 FY25 at only INR 20 crores EBITDA (6.8% margin), versus the optical business at INR 924 crores and INR 119 crores (12.9%); consolidated net debt was INR 2,195 crores at Q3 FY25 and the retained (post-demerger) business reported net debt of about INR 1,350 crores at Q4 FY25, with a stated target of taking net debt/EBITDA from ~3x to 2x. Structurally, management wanted a clean break rather than a carve-out on paper: in Nov 2025 Ajay Jhanjhari said 'the entire thought process of doing demerger is that there should not be any intercompany guarantees because that is a separate company,' and 'No relationship between STL and STL networks from that perspective.' The INR 2,600 crore BharatNet Phase III Jammu & Kashmir package (3-year build plus 10-year maintenance) went with the demerged entity, and STL now supplies cable to it on an arm's-length basis — in Jan 2026 described as 'our group company, Invenia has secured Jammu Kashmir package, where we will be supplying the cable on arm's length basis.' Each entity also got its own leadership and identity: Pankaj Malik as CEO of STL Networks under the Invenia brand, with shareholders receiving a 1:1 share entitlement on holdings as of April 24, 2025. Across the calls, no investor, lender or partner is named as having demanded the separation; the only shareholder pressure visible is generic complaints about poor equity returns and past cash burn (Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 calls), which management answered by pointing to the business exits, the ~INR 1,000 crore QIP of April 2024, and the demerger as portfolio simplification.
rationale.evolution: The idea is already in execution by the Jan 23, 2025 call, where it appears as a standing FY26 priority ('work towards completing the demerger of the services business') with the NCLT timeline laid out — scheme approved by shareholders and creditors July 10, 2024, petition admitted October 2024, final hearing January 30, 2025, listing targeted by Q1 FY26. On the May 16, 2025 call Ankit Agarwal declared it done, effective March 31, 2025, named the new entity STL Networks, the new brand Invenia, Pankaj Malik as CEO and the 1:1 share entitlement, and reported the retained business separately at INR 1,350 crores net debt. By Jul 25, 2025 the plan had slipped only on listing (NCLT approval received Feb 2025, shares expected to list 'by the end of August'), and by Nov 6, 2025 the emphasis shifted to completing the operational separation — no intercompany guarantees, a roughly year-long transition to transfer everything. Thereafter it is treated as finished history: Jan 23, 2026 references Invenia only as a BharatNet customer served at arm's length, and Jul 24, 2026 cites 'we've also demerged our system integration business into a separate entity' purely as evidence of focus.

rationale.rationale: On the documentary record available, Edelweiss is not executing a demerger scheme but a sequence of subsidiary-level separations that convert a holding-company conglomerate into separately capitalised, separately owned businesses — described in its own press release as "seven independent and well-governed businesses" each with "dedicated management teams and strong boards." The clearest stated reason is the Alternative Asset Management arm, EAAA India Alternatives: management said the IPO was "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform," i.e. separating the fastest-growing, fee-income business (FPAUM INR 41,920 Cr, +33% YoY; nine-month fund raise INR 7,576 Cr, +67% YoY; total income Rs 963.76 Cr in FY26 versus Rs 584.25 Cr in FY24; net worth Rs 1,075.54 Cr) from the credit-heavy parent so it can be valued and institutionalised on its own. Critically, the EAAA listing was a pure offer for sale by holdco subsidiary ESIPL (originally up to Rs 15,000 mn, cut to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP, finally Rs 1,200 Cr gross / Rs 1,120.63 Cr net at Rs 1,665 per share) — no primary money went to EAAA, so the cash accrues to the Edelweiss holding structure, which fits the stated priority of "focused reduction in corporate net debt" (down 15% to INR 6,520 Cr over two years, with consolidated net debt INR 11,390 Cr and a 3.46x debt-equity ratio). The second separation is Housing Finance: Nido Home Finance was handed to a strategic majority investor, CA Sardo Investments (The Carlyle Group) with Salisbury Investments (Aditya Puri's family vehicle), investing ~INR 2,100 Cr — Rs 580.68 Cr of secondary for 45% plus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of primary equity and warrants at INR 193 — taking them to 58.26% immediately and 72.70% fully diluted within 18 months, so Nido "ceased to be a subsidiary" and Edelweiss fell to 38.91% (25.46% diluted). Here the separation solves a growth-capital problem Edelweiss itself was not funding: a business contributing only 5.47% of consolidated income (Rs 520.63 Cr) but consuming 13.99% of net worth (Rs 828.2 Cr) was recapitalised with third-party primary money, with Edelweiss retaining upside via a minority stake and "an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments." The same template was applied to the Mutual Fund arm, where a 15% sale of Edelweiss Asset Management and Edelweiss Trusteeship to WestBridge moved both into joint control, crystallising a Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised and Rs 281 Cr realised gain (and a Rs 389 Cr deferred tax charge) — evidence that the separations are also being used to mark up carrying value and lift reported net worth/PAT (nine-month PAT Rs 549 Cr, +45% YoY). Taken together, the stated logic is: each business reaches scale, then gets its own owner, its own capital and its own valuation, while the parent de-levers.
rationale.evolution: This cannot be traced call by call: all ten earnings-call transcripts supplied (Nov 2023, May/Aug/Oct/Nov 2024, May/Aug/Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026) contained no extractable text, so no dated management commentary is available. From the filings, the sequence is: EAAA's DRHP filed 19–20 January 2026 (OFS up to Rs 15,000 mn by ESIPL); on 10 February 2026 the Q3FY26 release framed it as "the first step towards building EAAA as a standalone institutionalized platform" and the same day the Carlyle/Salisbury definitive agreements for a majority of Nido were announced, with WestBridge's Mutual Fund investment consummated in that quarter; SEBI observations came 23 April 2026, the Nido transaction closed 25 September 2026 (versus a 31 July 2026 expectation), and the EAAA IPO was repriced down to Rs 12,000 mn in the RHP of 19 October 2026 before listing on 2 November 2026 at Rs 1,665. So the plan visibly scaled down in size (Rs 1,500 Cr to Rs 1,200 Cr) and slipped in timing, while widening from one business to three.

points.point: Nido was absorbing far more of the group's capital than it contributed in income — 13.99% of net worth for 5.47% of income — which the recapitalisation by third parties addresses.
Most of the Carlyle money is primary capital into Nido's balance sheet rather than cash out to Edelweiss: Rs 580.68 Cr secondary versus Rs 1,446.14 Cr of fresh equity and warrants.
points.quote: Further, in accordance with the Agreements, Nido has also issued 2,59,06,736 equity shares and 5,18,13,472 warrants, to the Buyers, for an aggregate amount of INR 14,46,13,99,102.56.

points.point: Edelweiss retains economic upside in the separated housing business through a retained minority stake and a contingent payment linked to Carlyle's realised returns.
points.quote: Pursuant to the Agreements and subject to applicable laws, the Sellers (Edelweiss) may also receive an additional payment based upon returns realized by CA Sardo Investments from its investment in Nido.

points.point: Control of Nido passes progressively to the buyers — 58.26% on closing rising to 72.70% fully diluted — while Edelweiss falls to 25.46%.
points.quote: the Buyers now hold 58.26% shareholding of Nido which would be increased to 72.70% within 18 months, on a fully diluted basis post conversion of the warrants.

points.point: The Mutual Fund business was separated on the same template, with a 15% strategic sale converting EAML and ETCL into jointly controlled entities.
points.quote: Additionally, the WestBridge investment in Mutual Fund received its final approval from the regulators, and the deal has been consummated this quarter.

points.point: That Mutual Fund separation crystallised very large accounting gains — Rs 2,440 Cr unrealised plus Rs 281 Cr realised — showing the separations also re-rate carrying values inside the consolidated accounts.
points.quote: Pursuant to the terms of the SHA, the Group now has joint control for both of these Entities with the new investor, and consequently, in accordance with Ind AS 110 and Ind AS 28, these entities are now classified as jointly controlled entities under Ind AS accounting principles.

points.point: The EAAA listing raised no primary capital for EAAA itself; proceeds went to the holding-company subsidiary ESIPL, consistent with using separation to fund parent de-leveraging.
points.quote: The IPO comprises an offer for sale (“OFS”) for an amount not exceeding Rs. 12,000 million, which is proposed to be undertaken by Edelweiss Securities & Investments Private Limited (“ESIPL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: The alternatives business being separated had tripled income over three years, supporting the argument that it deserves its own valuation.
points.quote: FY 2025-26: Rs 963.76 crores FY 2024-25: Rs 786.54 crores. FY 2023-24: Rs 584.25 crores.

points.point: On completion Edelweiss kept overwhelming ownership of EAAA — 83.88% across subsidiaries — so this is a listing and institutionalisation step, not an exit.
points.quote: Consequently, the Company, through all its subsidiaries, hold 54,233,039 equity shares of EAAA representing 83.88% of the total paid-up equity share capital of EAAA.

points.point: The separations are set against an insurance drag and a credit book being wound down, including a Rs 920 Cr discretionary overlay on discontinued security receipts and a 34% YoY cut in the wholesale book.
points.quote: the Group has recognised a discretionary management overlay provision of 920 crores on its discontinued Security Receipts (Purchased or Originated Credit-Impaired (POCI) loans) in the consolidated financial results as at 31 December 2025.

rationale.what_management_expects: EAAA becomes a listed, "standalone institutionalized platform" with its own valuation; Nido gets Carlyle/Puri growth capital and majority ownership while Edelweiss keeps 25–39% plus a returns-linked earn-out; Mutual Fund gains a strategic partner and a Rs 2,440 Cr value mark; the parent frees capital (Rs 1,120.63 Cr net OFS proceeds) to push corporate net debt below INR 6,520 Cr.
rationale.gaps: All ten earnings-call transcripts were unextractable, so management's spoken rationale, investor/lender demands, use of proceeds, valuation targets, and any formal demerger scheme are absent.

judge.selling_pressure_why: ACC holders receive shares of larger, same-industry listed Ambuja; no new or unrelated entity is created; documents state no index impact
judge.listing_timeline: No new listing; ACC is dissolved without winding up. On 27 October 2026: "Subject to regulatory, statutory and NCLT approvals, completion is expected during FY'27."

judge.reason: Acquisition of SteriScience's Poland fill-finish and Baroda carbapenem facilities into OneSource, raising FY28 revenue outlook to $500m+; the separate Singapore amalgamation was to simplify corporate hierarchy, enhance operational efficiency and eliminate redundant administrative, compliance and legal costs.
judge.insiders: Steriscience is a related party "which the family owns along with TPG"; Steriscience owns 51% of listed Brooks. Arun Kumar is Founder/Non-Executive Chairperson; swap would add ~2.5 crore shares, raising promoter shareholding.
judge.hidden_value: Incoming Poland and Brooks assets delivered H1FY26 combined revenue $29m and EBITDA $11m (38% margin), targeting $40m EBITDA; transferors carry accumulated losses to be set off against OneSource's securities premium. Listed Brooks' price fell below the ~INR2,200/share intended valuation.
judge.selling_pressure_why: No new entity is listed or distributed; the scheme issues shares to promoters, and the Board dropped it on May 13, 2026.
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — no demerged entity lists. judge.what_is_spun: Nothing separated; three wholly owned subsidiaries amalgamate into Piramal Finance Limited (transferee), not a demerger
demerged_business_names: Piramal Corporate Tower Private Limited (Transferor Company-1)
Piramal Agastya Offices Private Limited (formerly PRL Agastya Private Limited) (Transferor Company-2)
Piramal Finance Limited (formerly Piramal Capital & Housing Finance Limited) (Transferee Company)
judge.reason: Consolidate subsidiaries' operations for operating synergies, cost rationalization by eliminating redundancies, streamlined group structure with fewer legal entities, lower compliance and regulatory costs, long-term stakeholder value
judge.insiders: Promoters held 46.16% (10,46,35,805 shares) pre-issue; promoter group Nithyam Realty (Anand Piramal 99.9% owner, director) took 82,94,000 warrants at Rs.2,110, 3.53% post-issue
judge.hidden_value: Transferors have negative pre-merger net worth already in consolidated accounts: transferee net worth Rs.23,710.54 crore pre-merger vs Rs.23,449.63 crore post; no shares issued, capital structure unchanged; total assets Rs.1,09,542.43 crore, FY26 PAT Rs.1,540.02 crore
judge.selling_pressure_why: No new shares issued, no dilution, no change in capital structure or shareholding pattern; nothing new gets listed
judge.option_pricing_date: 20th August 2026 (relevant date for warrant pricing under Regulation 161); ESOP option pricing date not stated
judge.listing_timeline: not stated (no demerged entity; only equity shares allotted on exercise of warrants 'shall be listed on the Stock Exchanges', per 24th August 2026 board disclosure)
judge.read_next: NCLT Mumbai sanction order on Company Petition C.A. (CAA)/84/MB/2026 filed 4 July 2026; outcome not in these filings
judge.quote: The Scheme does not affect the rights and interests of the shareholders of the Transferee Company.

judge.listing_timeline: No separate listing; per the Scheme the New Equity Shares "shall be listed on all the Stock Exchanges on which the Equity Shares of the Transferee Company are listed as on the Effective Date" and "will remain frozen in the depositories system till listing/trading permission is given by the Designated Stock Exchange" (BSE as Designated Stock Exchange). Scheme effective November 03, 2026; 44,02,000 equity shares allotted November 04, 2026. No date given for trading approval.
judge.read_next: Listing/trading permission filing for the 44,02,000 new shares; then Ace Alpha valuation report and 863:1,000 exchange ratio

judge.selling_pressure_why: Sapphire promoters, including SFML's ~18.5%+ stake, move to public category in DIL; SFML and Arctic may still pursue a secondary sale.

judge.what_is_spun: No business is spun off; aluminium products business consolidated into one wholly owned subsidiary via internal amalgamation
demerged_business_names: Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Limited (formerly Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Private Limited) (Amalgamated Company)
DR Axion India Limited (formerly DR Axion India Private Limited) (Amalgamating Company 3)
judge.reason: Aluminium business and expansion land are fragmented across entities; consolidation under a single focused operating entity gives a stronger balance sheet, unified asset ownership, simplified structure, better managerial focus and efficiency
judge.insiders: Promoter/CMD Srinivasan Ravi sold 5,25,000 shares (2.01%) on 23 June 2026, holding falling 40.15% to 38.14%; no promoter shares issued in the merged subsidiary
judge.hidden_value: Aluminium is now the largest segment (H1 FY27 revenue Rs 3,29,879 lakhs) but lowest-margin; DR Axion turnover Rs 1,298.52 cr on net worth Rs 511.34 cr versus Sunbeam Rs 1,237.46 cr on Rs 107.43 cr; consolidated borrowings Rs 3,61,860 lakhs
judge.selling_pressure_why: No shares distributed to listed shareholders; Company not a party and its shareholding pattern is unaffected
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — on 11 March 2026 the Company said "Not applicable. The Company is not a party to the proposed Scheme, and the shareholding pattern of the Company will not be affected by the proposed Scheme."
judge.read_next: Draft Composite Scheme filed with NCLT, plus Aluminium Products segment EBIT margin in the next quarterly results
judge.quote: This opportunity can be better capitalized by consolidating the Aluminium business under a single focused operating entity having a stronger balance sheet, a broader product and manufacturing base, unified asset ownership, and a streamlined organizational structure.

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing spun off: all of REC Limited, a power-sector infrastructure finance NBFC, absorbed into PFC
judge.reason: Budget-announced restructuring to achieve scale and efficiency in public sector NBFCs: merged entity becomes Government's principal power-sector institution, with improved balance sheet strength, stronger capital base, higher operational efficiencies and greater credit flow
judge.insiders: PFC holds 52.63% of REC's share capital; Government of India to continue retaining majority voting rights and control; merged entity must remain a 'Government Company'; Presidential approval conveyed June 10, 2026
judge.hidden_value: Ratio of 88 PFC shares per 100 REC shares against REC FY2025-26 standalone net worth Rs 84,290 crore and turnover Rs 59,140 crore versus PFC's Rs 1,02,532 crore and Rs 58,504 crore; combined loan book over Rs 11 lakh crore
judge.selling_pressure_why: Same sector, same promoter; REC holders receive PFC shares 88:100; no unrelated-industry or index-exclusion facts stated
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — REC is to be dissolved without being wound up and its equity shares cancelled, with PFC shares issued to REC shareholders as on a record date 'to be determined by the Boards of PFC and REC... at a future date' (press release June 28, 2026); NSE/BSE No Objection Letters received October 19, 2026, scheme still subject to RBI conditions, NCLT, shareholder and creditor approvals
judge.read_next: The Scheme at recindia.com/scheme-of-merger — Para 25(1) pre-conditions and the June 28, 2026 joint valuation report behind the 88:100 ratio
judge.quote: The merger of REC into PFC shall create a financing entity with an aggregate loan book of over INR 11 lakh crore.

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing separated; four wholly-owned subsidiaries merged by absorption into Fortis Hospitals Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary
judge.reason: "Rationalisation of operational efficiencies and reduction of administrative and managerial overhead, which will help in achieving rationalization of cost by simplification of management structure and financial reporting."
judge.insiders: No new entity or shares; FHsL's shareholding in each transferor is cancelled. Promoter Northern TK Venture (IHH) holds 31.17% of Fortis; plans stake to 51%.

judge.hidden_value: Reveals the subsidiaries are near-dormant: Punjabexpo net worth Rs 771.77 lacs on Rs 241.53 lacs income, Vahni negative Rs (168.63) lacs, versus TIL net worth Rs 3,00,174.04 lacs and income Rs 5,27,259.58 lacs; TIL carries Rs 1,911 crore net debt

judge.listing_timeline: not stated

judge.what_is_spun: Nothing is spun off; Cigniti Technologies Limited is amalgamated into Coforge Limited and dissolved without winding up
demerged_business_names: digital assurance and engineering (software testing) services
judge.reason: "Coforge acquired Cigniti to gain access to its tenured relationships, expand its Healthcare business, and grow its presence in the Midwest and Western regions of the US."
judge.insiders: Not stated for promoters; Coforge already held 54% of Cigniti pre-scheme; Encora sellers Advent/Warburg rolled into ~20.85% all-stock, Advent's Shweta Jalan and Atin Jain joined board
judge.hidden_value: Acquired business's EBITDA margin expanded from ~11% to ~19% in six quarters; top two acquired clients went from $25mn to $75mn per annum; minority interest in Cigniti now eliminated, lifting consolidated PAT and EPS
judge.selling_pressure_why: Documents say new shares stay frozen until exchanges grant listing/trading permission; locked-in shares remain locked; no index or flowback commentary
judge.listing_timeline: On June 4, 2026: "The Company is in the process of completing other formalities with respect to the issue and listing of the said shares and will file the necessary documents with the stock exchanges for seeking listing and trading approvals"; NCLT order of April 29, 2026 directs allotment within 30 days of the Effective Date, with shares frozen until listing and trading permission; for the separate Encora preferential issue, in-principle listing approval was received May 22, 2026 (intimated May 23, 2026)
judge.read_next: Scheme of Amalgamation at Annexure P-1 and First Motion Order dated 17 October 2025, which set out the Scheme's rationale
judge.quote: Accordingly, the Scheme has become effective and consequently, the Transferor Company stands amalgamated with the Company and is dissolved without being wound up.

judge.hidden_value: Reverse: Nerofix had negative networth at 31 March 2025 per ROC report. Restatement adds revenue (FY26 ₹7,739cr to ₹7,887cr) but cuts PBT (₹838cr to ₹831cr) and equity (₹6,696cr to ₹6,634cr). Management calls Nerofix high double-digit growth
judge.selling_pressure_why: No new entity, no shares issued; Nerofix's entire paid-up capital cancelled; listed parent unchanged, so no index or distribution-driven selling
judge.listing_timeline: not stated — no entity lists; "the Scheme will be effective upon filing the certified copy of the Order with the Registrar of Companies, Mumbai" (25 September 2026); NCLT order delivered 24 September 2026, rectified 14 October 2026, certified copies "yet to be received" (4 November 2026)
judge.read_next: Note 4 restatement table in Q2 FY27 results, and the ROC observation that Nerofix had negative networth at 31 March 2025
judge.quote: Since, the Scheme provides for merger of a wholly owned subsidiary with its holding company, and no shares of the Transferee Company will be issued on the Amalgamation, the requirement of obtaining the No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Stock Exchanges is not applicable.
